## Environment

- llama.cpp @ `07822bdd` (the DSpark branch from PR #27383, with the runtime-wiring port of that commit; locally also carries the two small port-fix commits for conv-state slot write / layer-input wiring)
- Build: Vulkan, AMD gfx1151 (NUC), `llama-server`
- Target model: Qwen3.8-27B (UD-Q4_K_XL GGUF, has MTP layers — `--spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-mod` works on it)
- Draft model: Qwen3.6-27B-DFlash (Q5_K_M GGUF, no MTP layers)

## Repro

```
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  -md Qwen3.6-27B-DFlash-Q5_K_M.gguf \
  --spec-type draft-dflash,draft-mtp,ngram-mod \
  -ngl 99 -c 262144 --flash-attn on --cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0 \
  --spec-draft-type-k q4_0 --spec-draft-type-v q4_0 --adaptive-target 0.6
```

Server exits during model load.

## Log

```
I common_speculative_init_result: loading draft model '.../Qwen3.6-27B-DFlash-Q5_K_M.gguf'
W llama_init_from_model: context type MTP requested but model doesn't contain MTP layers
E common_speculative_init_result: failed to create MTP context
E srv    load_model: failed to create MTP context
E srv  llama_server: exiting due to model loading error
```

## Site

`tools/server/server-context.cpp:1136` — `ctx_dft == nullptr` → `SRV_ERR("failed to create MTP context")`. `ctx_dft` comes from `common_speculative_init_from_params(params_dft, model_tgt, ctx_tgt)`.

## Analysis

With a mixed spec-type list, the speculative init appears to request an MTP-type context when loading the `-md` draft model; the DFlash draft GGUF contains no MTP layers, so `ctx_dft` comes back null and the server dies at init. Two readings:

1. If `draft-mtp` combined with an external `-md` draft is an **unsupported combination**, it should be rejected at config parse time with a clear error (today the failure is a runtime null-ctx with a message that doesn't name the real cause — the draft model lacking MTP layers).
2. If the combination is **meant to work** (MTP from the target's own layers + DFlash/ngram from the external draft), the MTP context should be created against the target model, not the draft.

Happy to test a patch branch — the repro box is set up.
items.title: Combined --spec-type draft-dflash,draft-mtp,ngram-mod with -md draft fails at init: MTP context requested from non-MTP draft model

items.body:
**Repro** (Strix Halo / gfx1151 iGPU, ROCm, llama.cpp with `--spec-type draft-dflash,draft-mtp,ngram-mod` + `-md <draft.gguf>`):

Server dies at model load:
```
common_speculative_init_result: failed to create MTP context
llama_server: exiting due to model loading error
```

**Root cause**: in `tools/server/server-context.cpp` (spec-init path around line 1136), when the spec-type list mixes `draft-mtp` with an external draft-model type and `-md` is given, a single shared `cparams` carries `ctx_type = LLAMA_CONTEXT_TYPE_MTP` into the *external draft model's* `llama_init_from_model` call. MTP layers only exist in the target model, so that call returns nullptr and the (misleading) "failed to create MTP context" error fires — the draft model never loaded at all.

**Fix** (validated: with the patch the combined init proceeds past draft load — see memory note below): separate the cparams so the MTP context type is only applied to a context created against the *target* model, and route `ctx_dft`/`ctx_mtp` distinctly for combined spec-types. Patch attached (against the dflash-capable line; applies to the spec-init block).

**Additional datum** — memory feasibility: even with the init fixed, combined MTP + external-draft at a 262k-token production config did not fit a 64GB GTT budget alongside other residents (core-dump under pressure; the MTP context + draft context + KV coexist). Smaller contexts work. Worth documenting the added memory cost of combined spec-types in the docs.

Happy to send this as a proper PR if the maintainers prefer.

items.body:
When ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft splits allocation on buft max_size, a view-only tail at the end of the context could skip the final alloc_tensor_range. Persistent views (e.g. KV k_stream / v_stream) were then left without ggml_backend_view_init.
Allocate only parent tensors in alloc_tensor_range and initialize all views in a final pass over the context after all splits complete.
## Overview
`ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft` can split a context across multiple buffers when a tensor would exceed the backend buffer-type `max_size` (for example Vulkan's default 1 GiB). If the remaining tail of the context contains only views, the final `alloc_tensor_range` may be skipped, so those views never get `ggml_backend_view_init`.
Persistent KV stream views (`layer.k_stream` / `v_stream`) then keep `tensor->data == NULL` while `view_src` is allocated. Host state save/restore later calls `ggml_backend_tensor_get` / `set` on those views and hits:
`GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated")`
This change:
- allocates only parent tensors inside each split range
- initializes all uninitialized views in one final pass over the context
Also adds `test_view_init_after_max_size_split` in `tests/test-alloc.cpp`
to cover the oversized-parent + view-only-tail case.
## Additional information
Fixes #19839
Fixes #23737
Fixes #21762

Related:
- #21576 (state-IO `!tensor->data` guards; complementary discussion)
I reproduced the assert with Qwen3.6-27B (MTP) when a parent KV tensor exceeded buft `max_size` and the context ended with a view-only tail.
Note on #21576: skipping tensors with `!tensor->data` avoids the assert, but can omit real KV still reachable via `view_src` and misalign the serialized state. This PR fixes the missing view init in the allocator instead.
Prior investigation commit (same patch on older master; kept for reference):
https://github.com/Yoshi4470/llama.cpp/commit/99655d5854e63e736a6a93280e01b7e785a59ba5
## Test plan
- [x] `test-alloc` (includes new `test_view_init_after_max_size_split`)
- [x] Vulkan A/B on the Qwen3.6-27B MTP speculative path (same command, 10 runs each):
  - before (`e3546c794`): 0/10 (assert every time)
  - after (this PR): 10/10 (no assert, completed normally)
- [x] Earlier `amdvlk64.dll` crash after the assert site was resolved by an AMD driver update; treated as separate from this allocator fix
- N/A: equivalent-size CPU repro (not practical on this machine)

### Command used for the A/B runs:
- Vulkan / AMDVLK, Windows, AMD Software 26.6.4
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)
```
llama-cli.exe -np 8 -c 2097152 --no-mmap -m models/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ctkd q4_0 -ctvd q4_0 \
--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 -p "Hello!"
```
## Requirements
- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - Cursor assisted with implementing the finalize-views pass and regression test after I identified the root cause in the alloc split path, and with local verification.

items.body:
Description

On an AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395, gfx1151 iGPU, 128 GB unified memory) running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF with a build containing PR #27742, decode throughput collapses as a function of context depth only, not during generation:

  • ~19–21 tok/s for short prompts (< ~512 tokens)
  • drops sharply once total context passes ~1K tokens
  • plateaus at ~5.5–6.1 tok/s from ~2K onward (down to ~4.6 tok/s at 45K) — a ~3.5–4x cliff

Output quality is unaffected (a 45K-token needle-in-haystack test returns the exact hidden value). Prefill is also degraded at depth (pp1 @ d4096 ≈ 9 t/s vs ≈ 20 t/s at d0), but the generation-rate collapse is the main problem.

This looks HIP-path specific: on CUDA devices with the same model/quant the long-context decay is mild (~18.5 → ~15.7 tok/s at 30K depth on DGX Spark / GB10; similar reports on dual-4090 setups at 80–250K context still showing ~21 tok/s decode). Suspect the QSA indexer / ggml_top_k / small per-token gather op chain falling back to an unoptimized or CPU-synced path on HIP once sparse attention kicks in beyond the indexer activation threshold.

Standard llama-bench reproduction (no server needed)

llama-bench supports --n-depth to pad the KV with N previous chat turns, so the decode-rate-vs-depth cliff reproduces with a single command:

Results (mean ± stddev, tg256 @ depth):

context depth | decode t/s -- | -- 0 | 18.33 ± 1.43 256 | 19.56 ± 0.07 512 | 19.57 ± 0.09 1024 | 6.10 ± 0.07 1536 | 6.02 ± 0.07 2048 | 5.93 ± 0.08 3072 | 5.80 ± 0.05 4096 | 5.75 ± 0.06 8192 | 5.49 ± 0.04

(pp1 @ same depths: 19.7 / 19.4 / 20.1 / 13.3 / 7.5 / 5.9 / 10.8 / 9.0 / 6.0 t/s — prefill degrades too.)

The same cliff was independently confirmed through llama-server (-np 1, single client, no concurrency — verified via f_sim_best = 1.000 slot logs and repeat runs): tiny prompt 51 tok → 20.0 tok/s decode; 1402 → 13.2; 2026 → 7.1; 5555 → 5.8; 45634 → 4.6.

Environment

  • Model: unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF UD-IQ4_XS (93.7 GB, 3 shards) — cliff also seen with other quants on this hardware is untested; Q4_K_XL can't fit this machine
  • llama.cpp source: tarball at commit ef687669 (PR #27742 head merged into master 2026-08-27); llama-server --version reports 0.3.0-dev (build 0, commit unknown) because of the tarball build
  • Build flags (HIP): -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGGML_HIP_NO_VMM=ON -DGGML_HIP_MMQ_MFMA=ON -DGGML_HIP_GRAPHS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=OFF (PIC=OFF required: ggml 0.22.0 PIE default conflicts with HIP 32-bit relocations on this toolchain)
  • Backend: ROCm 7.2.4, device detected as AMD Radeon Graphics, gfx1151 (0x1151), VMM: no
  • OS/kernel: Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 7.0.0-30-generic
  • Env: LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE=1 (required — QSA + q8_0 KV asserts at qwen4exp.cpp:544 otherwise), LLAMA_MMAP_RANDOM=1 (makes no difference to the cliff; both values tested)
  • Server flags when reproduced via llama-server: -ngl 99 -c 131072 -np 1 --jinja -fa on --reasoning off --reasoning-budget 0 -t 32 --threads-batch 32 -b 8192 -ub 2048 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --load-mode mmap
  • Memory during the cliff is healthy (used ≈ 73–81 GiB, available ≈ 35–44 GiB, PSI ~0) — not a swap/thrash artifact; this was separately confirmed on a machine where the model fits fully resident

Additional data point

  • -fa off A/B run: the cliff persists almost unchanged (tg256 = 17.13 @ d0 → 6.07 @ d1024 → 5.75 @ d2048 → 5.41 @ d4096). So it is not the HIP flash-attention kernels — it points at the QSA indexer / top-k / gather op chain that activates beyond ~1K context regardless of the attention implementation.

Questions for maintainers

  1. Is the QSA lightning indexer (ggml_top_k and the per-token score/gather op chain) fully implemented in the HIP backend, or does it fall back to CPU at decode time? (Skipping top-k on CUDA reportedly crashes — the HIP equivalent path is what I suspect here.)
  1. GGML_HIP_GRAPHS=OFF is required on gfx1151 in this build configuration — could the loss of graph capture specifically hurt the many-small-kernels QSA decode step?
  1. Any recommended way to profile this on HIP (rocprof with our permissions setup) to narrow down which op blows up at ~1K tokens?

Happy to run additional configurations (other quants, -d sweeps, op-level traces) — this machine is otherwise idle and the model stays loaded.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

// there is very little benefit to offloading the input layer, so always keep it on the CPU
pimpl->dev_input = { cpu_dev, &pimpl->cpu_buft_list };

This keeps tok_embd on CPU even with -ngl 99, which forces GET_ROWS(tok_embd, inp_tokens) onto the CPU backend at the start of every forward pass. On Stix Halo where CPU and GPU share same DDR5 it hurts a lot.

Possible fix is to mirror the output-layer policy for the input layer when full offload is requested.

41.33 t/s tg (30% CPU usage)

After full GPU offload: 
47.24 t/s tg (2% CPU usage)

> Repro report for **PR #27742** — the PR discussion is locked (`too heated`), so filing here instead. Everything below is tested against that PR's head (`6c5afc86`) and also the #27774 head (`abdc7a0`).

## Multi-segment prompt regression on Strix Halo (gfx1151) — deterministic repro + a GPU-state gotcha

First of all, thanks for this PR — single-turn usage already works great here (thinking mode included, after the chat-template workaround below).

### Environment

- Strix Halo laptop APU: Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 + Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`), ROCm 7.2, kernel 6.19.8
- Tested both #27774 head (`abdc7a0`) and #27742 head (`6c5afc86`)
- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` `UD-Q4_K_XL` (111.3 GB)
- `llama-server -ngl auto -c 8192 --parallel 1 --jinja` with `LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE=1` (required, otherwise output is broken as noted earlier in the thread)

### Bug: any prompt with ≥2 message segments degrades to `//////`

Single-segment prompts are **perfect** (long 900-token user turns, thinking mode, cache-hit reruns all fine). Add a second segment and the very first generated token is already `/`, then `/` forever. 100% deterministic, temperature-independent.

Minimal repro via `/completion` (temperature 0):

**CLEAN:**
```
<|im_start|>user
What is the capital of France?<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
```

**DEGEN — multi-turn:**
```
<|im_start|>user
My name is Bob.<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
Noted!<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>user
What is my name?<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
```

**DEGEN — plain text before the first `<|im_start|>` (so even "preamble + one segment" breaks):**
```
Previous conversation: user said hi, assistant replied hello.
<|im_start|>user
What is the capital of France?<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
```

Also degenerate: standalone `system` message + user; `user`+`user`+`user`.

So the boundary is purely **segment count ≥ 2 (or any tokens preceding the first segment)** — content and length are irrelevant. Since the first sampled token is already wrong, this looks like a prefill-path bug for multi-segment inputs (PLE n-gram history / indexer state across segment boundaries?).

On the chat endpoint this means any multi-message conversation degenerates, while single-turn works — which also explains why template variations (system blocks etc.) make it look random. Workaround we use: a custom chat template that folds system text + tools into the first user turn, keeping the prompt single-segment. Thinking mode then works fine for single-turn.

### Gotcha: OOM-killed server leaves the GPU in a bad state

After `llama-server` gets OOM-killed (or `pkill -9`), the GPU enters a state where **every** subsequent run — any binary, any prompt, including previously-clean single-segment repros — outputs only `/`. This silently poisons triage: results look non-deterministic when they aren't. A function-level reset restores it without rebooting:

```
echo 1 | sudo tee /sys/class/drm/card1/device/reset
```

(Context if it matters: this machine already runs `amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0` on the cmdline from an earlier ring-timeout issue.)

### Question

Is multi-segment prefill known / on the roadmap? Happy to test any patch — the repro above is fully deterministic on my end.

items.body:
### Problem

Dense-model prompt processing on the Vulkan backend is well below the integer-dot peak on gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S / Ryzen AI Max+ 395). Profiling Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q5_K_XL-v2 with `GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER=1` at `-ub 2048`: ~85% of prefill time is `MUL_MAT` via the integer-dot `mul_mmq.comp` path (K-quant × q8_1), sustaining roughly half of what the same shapes reach after a tile change (see below). Decode is not affected by this and is already in the expected range for the memory bandwidth.

The large int-mmq K-quant tile is 128x128 at 256 threads (`l_warptile_mmq_int_k`). At dense prefill shapes (N = 512..2048 per ubatch) this underfills the shader cores and re-reads the A (weight) tile once per 128-token slab of N.

### Proposal

On RDNA3 iGPUs only, double BN and the workgroup size: 128x256 at 512 threads. Per-thread register tiling (TM/TN/WMITER) is unchanged — only the tile geometry and warp count move, halving the A re-reads per token. `wg_denoms` kept in sync so dispatch and split-k see the real tile. No shader changes.

Same-binary stash A/B, Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q5_K_XL-v2, RADV, `-fa 1 -b/-ub 2048`, r=5:

| test | stock | 128x256@512 | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| pp512 | 294.5 ±6.4 | 517.0 ±3.4 | 1.76x |
| pp4096 | 249.6 ±0.2 | 436.7 ±0.8 | 1.75x |
| pp16384 | 216.1 ±0.4 | 333.2 ±1.7 | 1.54x |
| tg128 | 10.76 | 10.82 | unchanged |

Greedy outputs are byte-identical (temp 0, diffed). Decode and speculative-verify batches (n ≤ 64) select the small/medium tile and are structurally unaffected — verified with an MTP/DFlash2 spec-decode server config: 28.7 t/s average decode at 64% acceptance, no regression.

### Scope / relation to #21344

- Single gated tile change (RDNA3 + integrated GPU via `device->uma`), not a sweep; other vendors and dGPU behavior untouched.
- `mul_mat_id` (MoE) tile families untouched.
- Neutral probes on this hardware: BM=256, 1024 threads, TM/TN/WMITER reshapings, wave32 — the 128x256@512 geometry is the whole effect.
- The coopmat dequant family (iq4_xs path) measurably dislikes the doubled tile and stays stock.

I have the patch on a branch; happy to open the PR if there's interest, and can run additional quant/model combos on request (Q4_K_XL and Q6_K_XL pp4096 numbers already collected).

items.body:
## Summary

Enables the existing `GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB` code paths on HIP via **hipCUB** (rocPRIM), which provides CUB-compatible APIs (`DeviceRadixSort`, `DeviceSegmentedRadixSort`, `DeviceScan`, `BlockScan/Load/Store`).

This fixes a severe decode cliff and a hard abort on ROCm for `qwen4exp` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next):

- **#27856** — decode collapses 19.6 → ~6 t/s once `n_kv` crosses ~1024 tokens on HIP (Strix Halo)
- **#27865** — over RPC, the worker aborts with `TOP_K failed: invalid configuration argument` once `n_kv` crosses 2048 columns

## Mechanism

Without `GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB`, the HIP backend reports `TOP_K`/`ARGSORT` as unsupported beyond **1024 columns** (`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu`, `supports_op`: `return op->src[0]->ne[0] <= 1024;`), because the no-CUB fallback (`argsort_f32_i32_cuda_bitonic`) exceeds launch limits past that (threads = `ncols_pad/2` > 1024, shared memory `ncols_pad * sizeof(int)` > 64 KiB smpb).

For `qwen4exp`, the QSA lightning indexer runs `ggml_top_k()` over a `[n_kv, n_tps]` tensor (`ne[0] == n_kv`) in **all 12 QSA layers on every decode token**. Past the 1024-column threshold the op moves to CPU — with a device→host copy of the scores, a CPU top-k, a host→device copy of the indices and a sync **per layer per token** → the observed 3–4× decode cliff. Over RPC the crash occurs because `ggml_backend_rpc_device_supports_op()` currently reports unconditional support, so the op is dispatched to a worker whose real backend cannot launch it.

With the CUB paths enabled, `top_k`/`argsort` use `DeviceRadixSort`/`DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` on the GPU for arbitrary column counts, and `supports_op` legitimately reports support.

## Changes

- `argsort.cu`, `top-k.cu`, `mean.cu`, `sum.cu`, `cumsum.cu`: include `<hipcub/hipcub.hpp>` instead of `<cub/cub.cuh>` under `GGML_USE_HIP` (using-declaration or `namespace cub = hipcub;` for the qualified usages in `cumsum.cu`)
- `argsort.cu`: skip the `DeviceSegmentedSort` capture-check on HIP and always use `DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` — rocPRIM has no `DeviceSegmentedSort`, and radix sort works both inside and outside stream capture
- `common.cuh`: alias the stream-capture-status API (`cudaStreamCaptureStatus`, `cudaStreamIsCapturing`, …) — the HIP runtime does not provide these aliases; guarded by `GGML_USE_HIP && GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB`
- `ggml-hip/CMakeLists.txt`: expose `GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB` as a CMake option (previously this define was not reachable from any build system on HIP)

**CUDA builds are unaffected:** every source change is guarded by `GGML_USE_HIP`; `ssm-scan.cu` already excludes itself on HIP and needs no change.

## Validation

2× AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151, ROCm 7.2.1, Thunderbolt RPC cluster), `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` UD-IQ4_XS (93.7 GB, 3 shards), 262144 ctx, `llama-server` + `ggml-rpc-server` (master):

- No TOP_K abort at large `n_kv` (previously a hard worker crash past 2048 columns, #27865)
- Decode: **20.2 t/s** at <1K context, **20.1 t/s** at 18K, 11.7 t/s at 52K — the 1K cliff from #27856 is gone; the remaining degradation is linear (~1 µs per KV token) and comes from the QSA attention being implemented as a mask over the full KV rather than gathering the top-k selection (separate, kernel-level optimization opportunity)
- Prefill: 282 t/s at 18K tokens (`-ub 512`)
- Output quality verified on long generations (800+ tokens, German and English)

Build: `cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGGML_CUDA_USE_CUB=ON …` with ROCm 7.2.1 (clang from ROCm, `CMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=<rocm>/bin/amdclang++`).

items.body:
ggml_cuda_op_top_k had a fast partial-top-k path only under CUB_TOP_K_AVAILABLE (NVIDIA CCCL >= 3.2 DeviceTopK). On ROCm/HIP that is never defined, so:
  - supports_op reported TOP_K unsupported for ne[0] > 1024, pushing it to the CPU backend (a per-token GPU<->CPU roundtrip + CPU sort), and
  - where it did run, it full-sorted every row. This collapses Qwen3-Next/qwen4exp QSA long-context decode on Strix Halo, while a same-bandwidth NVIDIA GB10 (DeviceTopK) stays flat.

- top-k.cu: add a HIP branch using rocPRIM partial_sort_copy on packed (score,index) keys (nth_element + sort of the first k). k == ncols falls back to bitonic (rocPRIM requires middle < size).
- ggml-cuda.cu: enable TOP_K in supports_op on HIP when k < ncols (or ncols <= 1024), and disable graph capture for graphs whose TOP_K uses the partial path (it syncs the stream), mirroring the MUL_MAT_ID guard.

Validation on gfx1151 / ROCm 7.2.1:
- test-backend-ops -o TOP_K: 517/517 OK (incl. ncols up to 16384).
- qwen4exp UD-IQ4_XS single-stream, graphs ON: S_TG at N_KV 640/2176/8320 = 21.5/20.7/19.3 t/s (was 21.5/8.8/8.1) -> long-context collapse eliminated.

## Overview This PR improves routed MoE prefill performance on RDNA3 by changing how llama.cpp chooses MMQ N-tile sizes. Instead of using the worst case expert width, it estimates the typical routed expert width and uses that when it is smaller than the RDNA3 maximum tile width. The launch grid still uses the original worst case width, so output coverage and correctness are preserved. The change is limited to host side tile selection in `mul_mat_q_case` and does not modify structs, call sites, launch parameters, or device kernels. Benchmarks on a Radeon Pro W7800/gfx1100 with ROCm 7.2.3 show large prefill gains in many routed MoE cases, while decode and non RDNA3 architectures are mostly unchanged. If maintainers or other contributors have access to NVIDIA, CDNA, RDNA2, or RDNA4 hardware, the natural follow up would be to test the same routed width picker under the corresponding MMQ/launch policy and enable it per architecture where it is beneficial. ## Benchmark Summary Hardware/software: - AMD Radeon Pro W7800, gfx1100 / RDNA3 - ROCm 7.2.3 - HIP backend, `-ngl 99` - `GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON` - `-fa 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv f16 -sm none -t 4 --poll 0 -r 5` The improvement depends on the physical ubatch/chunk width that reaches routed MoE MMQ, not total context length: ```text win when: ncols_typical < mmq_x_max crossover_ubatch: 128 * n_experts / n_expert_used ``` So long prompts can still benefit when they are processed in smaller ubatch chunks.

items.body:
## Environment

- llama.cpp: upstream master as of 2026-08-26 (build **b10643**), self-built Release / CUDA sm_86. The only local patches are unrelated GGML kernel optimizations; `common/chat.cpp` and the server chat pipeline are vanilla.
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M GGUF with embedded official jinja template (+mmproj)
- Server flags: `-c 120000 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 --split-mode layer -ts 1,1,1 --spec-type draft-mtp --tools all` (jinja default on)
- Client: OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, streaming, `tool_choice: auto`, ~33 tools (agentic CLI workload)

## Observed

Episodically (~2×/day under heavy agent use) a slot finishes a long generation normally and then the request dies:

```
I slot print_timing: id 3 | task 0 | eval time = 515042.58 ms / 11708 tokens
I slot print_timing: id 3 | task 0 | draft acceptance = 0.52296 (7151 accepted / 13674 generated)
I slot      release: id 3 | task 0 | stop processing: n_tokens = 37979, truncated = 0
W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <think>
W srv          stop: cancel task, id_task = 0
```

Note that `common_chat_peg_parse()` logs `effective_input.substr(result.end)` — i.e. **only the unconsumed tail**. In both captured occurrences that tail was literally `<think>\n` (8 bytes).

## Analysis

The model produced a fully valid turn — reasoning + content + one or more well-formed `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` blocks that match the per-request grammar — and then emitted a stray opening `<think>` immediately before stopping. Since the lazy grammar necessarily releases around/between tool calls, a few free tokens can land there; generation then stops (EOS / `n_predict`) leaving an unclosed tag behind.

The strict final parse (non-partial `common_chat_peg_parse()`) fails on that tail and throws:

```
The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format
```

…which makes the server cancel the task, so the client loses the entire already-generated response (~11.7k tokens here) purely because of 8 bytes of trailing garbage.

## Suggested remedies

Any of the following would remove the user-visible failure:

1. Make the autoparser's tool-call root tolerate trailing garbage after the last complete call (e.g. optional untagged `rest()` before end).
2. In `common_chat_peg_parse()` for non-partial input: before failing, retry the parse truncated right after the last complete `</tool_call>`; if it succeeds, return the structured message.
3. At minimum, don't throw on a *final* parse mismatch — degrade to raw-content passthrough instead of canceling the task.

We are running (2)+(3) locally with good results and would be happy to prepare a PR if this direction is acceptable.

## Related

- #27720 — gpt-oss malformed Harmony channel header fails the final PEG parse and errors the turn
- #27279 — peg-native + `response_format.json_schema`: parse throws → 500
- #27025 — same error string, Muse Glimmer tool calls

items.body:
When ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft splits allocation on buft max_size, a view-only tail at the end of the context could skip the final alloc_tensor_range. Persistent views (e.g. KV k_stream / v_stream) were then left without ggml_backend_view_init.
Allocate only parent tensors in alloc_tensor_range and initialize all views in a final pass over the context after all splits complete.
## Overview
`ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft` can split a context across multiple buffers when a tensor would exceed the backend buffer-type `max_size` (for example Vulkan's default 1 GiB). If the remaining tail of the context contains only views, the final `alloc_tensor_range` may be skipped, so those views never get `ggml_backend_view_init`.
Persistent KV stream views (`layer.k_stream` / `v_stream`) then keep `tensor->data == NULL` while `view_src` is allocated. Host state save/restore later calls `ggml_backend_tensor_get` / `set` on those views and hits:
`GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated")`
This change:
- allocates only parent tensors inside each split range
- initializes all uninitialized views in one final pass over the context
Also adds `test_view_init_after_max_size_split` in `tests/test-alloc.cpp`
to cover the oversized-parent + view-only-tail case.
## Additional information
Fixes #19839
Fixes #23737
Fixes #21762

Related:
- #21576 (state-IO `!tensor->data` guards; complementary discussion)
I reproduced the assert with Qwen3.6-27B (MTP) when a parent KV tensor exceeded buft `max_size` and the context ended with a view-only tail.
Note on #21576: skipping tensors with `!tensor->data` avoids the assert, but can omit real KV still reachable via `view_src` and misalign the serialized state. This PR fixes the missing view init in the allocator instead.
Prior investigation commit (same patch on older master; kept for reference):
https://github.com/Yoshi4470/llama.cpp/commit/99655d5854e63e736a6a93280e01b7e785a59ba5
## Test plan
- [x] `test-alloc` (includes new `test_view_init_after_max_size_split`)
- [x] Vulkan A/B on the Qwen3.6-27B MTP speculative path (same command, 10 runs each):
  - before (`e3546c794`): 0/10 (assert every time)
  - after (this PR): 10/10 (no assert, completed normally)
- [x] Earlier `amdvlk64.dll` crash after the assert site was resolved by an AMD driver update; treated as separate from this allocator fix
- N/A: equivalent-size CPU repro (not practical on this machine)

### Command used for the A/B runs:
- Vulkan / AMDVLK, Windows, AMD Software 26.6.4
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)
```
llama-cli.exe -np 8 -c 2097152 --no-mmap -m models/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ctkd q4_0 -ctvd q4_0 \
--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 -p "Hello!"
```
## Requirements
- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - Cursor assisted with implementing the finalize-views pass and regression test after I identified the root cause in the alloc split path, and with local verification.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Summary 
On hybrid SSM/attention MoE models (general.architecture=qwen35moe, carrying ssm.* keys and
full_attention_interval), llama-server grows RSS by a fixed ~126 MiB on every request and never
releases it. Growth is perfectly linear and does not decelerate — 40 consecutive requests took RSS from 1340
MiB to 6379 MiB at exactly +126 MiB each. 
The allocation is anonymous (RssAnon grows; RssFile stays flat at 110 MiB) and is reclaimed only by
restarting the process. 
A non-SSM model on the identical build, GPU and driver does not leak at all (gpt-oss-20b mxfp4: +0 MiB
request over 12 requests), which is what points at the hybrid/recurrent path rather than at the server or the
backend generally.

Reproduction

What it is NOT — controlled matrix 
Every row is the same measurement protocol; only the named variable changed.variable value A value B leakllama.cpp build b9722 b10673 (~950 newer) 126.3 / 125.9MTP spec-decode on off 126.5 / 126.3context size 147456 32768 126.3 / 126.3context size 163840 (Ornith 1.0) — 126vision / mmproj on off 126.3 / 126.9max_tokens 220 / 90 40 126.5 / 126.3 / 126KV cache type q4_0 f16 126.3 / 127flash attention on off 126.3 / 127model file Ornith 1.5 Ornith 1.0 (different file) 126 / 126architecture qwen35moe (SSM) gpt-oss-20b (no SSM) 126 / 0 
So it is independent of build, MTP, context length, vision, generated tokens, KV quantization and flash attention
— and it tracks the architecture. 
Why we suspect the recurrent/SSM state path 
The leak is a fixed size per request, unaffected by context length or tokens generated. That matches an
allocation sized by the SSM state dimensions rather than by sequence length. The affected GGUFs carry: 
qwen35moe, ssm.conv_kernel, ssm.group_count,

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 0.1.0-dev (build 1, commit 4df29be)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Source at `4df29be4f4c3673f428170fda944a5b19f743bb8`, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`
(`CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE=-O3 -DNDEBUG`), g++ 14.2.0.

The `llama-server` that produced the coredump is a Vulkan build; the `llama-tokenize` used for every
threshold below is a HIP/ROCm build of the same commit with the same flags. The pre-tokenizer path is
CPU-only and identical in both, and both report the same version string.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core), llama-server, llama-tokenize

### Command line

```shell
llama-server \
  --model gpt-oss-120b-MXFP4.gguf \
  --n-gpu-layers 99 --ctx-size 131072 --parallel 2 --cont-batching \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 2048 --load-mode none \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8081 --metrics --no-ui --no-slots
```

None of these flags is load-bearing. The crash is in pre-tokenization, before anything
backend-, batch- or KV-related is reached, and `llama-tokenize` reproduces it with no GPU at all.

### Problem description

**A single POST to `/v1/chat/completions` whose prompt contains a long unbroken run of one character
class terminates the server process with SIGSEGV, during tokenization, before any inference
happens.** It takes ~26,000 characters at the default 8 MiB stack. There is no error, no 4xx and no
log line — the process is simply gone, taking every slot's KV cache and prompt cache with it.

It requires no `tools`, no grammar, no streaming and no concurrency.

**What matters is the longest unbroken run that one alternative of the pre-tokenizer expression can
consume, not the prompt length.** libstdc++'s executor recurses once per repetition, and *every*
quantified alternative in this expression is a driver — not only the letter ones. Measured against
the shipped `llama-tokenize` at an 8 MiB stack, exit 139 = SIGSEGV:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `'x' * 26,000` → ok · `'x' * 26,500` | **SIGSEGV** |
| `'X' * 26,000` → ok · `'X' * 26,250` | **SIGSEGV** |
| `'日' * 26,000` → ok · `'日' * 26,250` | **SIGSEGV** |
| `'.' * 26,000` → ok · `'.' * 27,000` | **SIGSEGV** |
| `' ' * 26,000` → ok · `' ' * 28,000` | **SIGSEGV** |
| `'_' * 36,000`, `'\n' * 36,000` | **SIGSEGV** |
| English letters, spaces removed — 35,000 | **SIGSEGV** |
| Japanese, punctuation removed — 30,000 | **SIGSEGV** |
| `'Xx' * 18,000` — 36,000 alternating-case letters | ok |
| `'1234567890' * 6,600` — 66,000 digits | ok |
| English prose *with* spaces — 66,000 | ok |
| Japanese *with* ordinary `。` and `、` — 51,000 | ok |

Reading the alternation, three kinds of run recurse:

- **letters of a single case** — `((?=[\p{L}])([^A-Z]))+` drives lowercase runs and
  `((?=[\p{L}])([^a-z]))+` drives uppercase runs. A case change breaks both, which is why
  `'Xx' * 18,000` survives while `'x' * 26,500` and `'X' * 26,250` each die. Non-ASCII letters sit in
  **both** classes.
- **non-letter, non-digit, non-space characters** — ` ?[^\s\p{L}\p{N}]+[\r\n/]*`, so a long run of a
  single punctuation or symbol character is its own driver.
- **whitespace** — `\s*[\r\n]+`, `\s+(?!\S)`, `\s+`.

**Digits are the exception**: `\p{N}{1,3}` is bounded, so 66,000 digits tokenize fine.

So a space or a full stop ends a *letter* run but opens a run of its own. What keeps ordinary text
safe is that it alternates *short* runs of different classes — prose interleaves letter runs of a
dozen characters with one-character space runs, and neither approaches the threshold. Measured:
66,000 characters of English prose and 51,000 codepoints of Japanese with `。` and `、` both
tokenize normally.

**Non-ASCII does not lower the codepoint threshold.** `unicode_regex_split` collapses each non-ASCII
codepoint to a single category byte, so one CJK codepoint costs the same stack as one ASCII letter —
`'日'` brackets at 26,000 / 26,250, identical to `'X'`. What differs for scripts without inter-word
spaces is that long unbroken letter runs arise there naturally, where in English they have to be
constructed.

**It is reachable by an untrusted caller without anything exotic**: a ~26 KB body of one repeated
character — a letter, a space, a full stop — kills the process, repeatedly. `set_payload_max_length`
is never called anywhere in the tree outside its own definition in the vendored cpp-httplib, so
there is no size cap in front of it, and tokenization happens *before* the context-length check
(`tokenize_input_prompts` at `tools/server/server-context.cpp:4198`, inside
`handle_completions_impl`; the "exceeds the available context size" check is at `:3115`, after the
task is queued), so `--ctx-size` does not bound it either.

We have not surveyed which real-world content reaches ~26,000 characters of one class. The cases we
can name are programmatically whitespace-stripped text, a pathologically long single-case identifier
or concatenated token stream, and long runs of padding, separator or indentation characters.

### Root cause

`gpt-oss` resolves to `LLAMA_VOCAB_PRE_TYPE_GPT4O` (o200k_harmony, `case` label at
`src/llama-vocab.cpp:428`). Its pre-tokenizer expression is `src/llama-vocab.cpp:433`:

```
[^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?((?=[\p{L}])([^a-z]))*((?=[\p{L}])([^A-Z]))+(?:'[sS]|'[tT]|…)?|
[^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?((?=[\p{L}])([^a-z]))+((?=[\p{L}])([^A-Z]))*(?:'[sS]|'[tT]|…)?|
\p{N}{1,3}| ?[^\s\p{L}\p{N}]+[\r\n/]*|\s*[\r\n]+|\s+(?!\S)|\s+
```

That string is **not** in `unicode_regex_split_custom()`'s list of hand-written fast paths
(`src/unicode.cpp:1050`), so every tokenize call for this vocab falls through to
`unicode_regex_split_stl()` (`src/unicode.cpp:739`, reached from `:1367`) and therefore to
libstdc++'s `std::regex`, whose executor is a **recursive** backtracking DFS.

The worst driver is:

```
((?=[\p{L}])([^A-Z]))+
```

a lookahead **inside** a greedy repetition. libstdc++ recurses once per repe
items.title: server / tokenizer: SIGSEGV (stack overflow) in `unicode_regex_split_stl` — the o200k / GPT4O pre-tokenizer regex recurses once per character, so a ~26,000-character unbroken run of one character class kills the process

### Name and Version

`llama-server --version` → `version: 0.1.2-dev (build 10488, commit 9d77fa172)`, built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64 (the official `llama-b10488-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64.zip`). I checked `common/chat.cpp` history through b10622: no gpt-oss/Harmony parser changes since b10488, so I believe this still reproduces on master.

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, driver 591.86, i7-13700K.

### Models

`ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF` → `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4.gguf` (sha256 `27cd6c432c7672cb812a92f611cf3ba7bbc35928262bb1e1253ff4ee6ae35901`, verified against HF LFS).

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

gpt-oss-20b at the OpenAI-recommended sampling (`--temp 1.0 --top-p 1.0`; server-default top_k 40 / min_p 0.05) occasionally emits a **malformed Harmony channel header** at the start of a turn: after `<|channel|>` it produces free text, `??`, `commentary 2?`, `commentary?commentary?`, or a doubled `<|channel|>commentary to=assistant<|channel|>commentary?...` — and only then (sometimes) the well-formed `<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>...`.

`common_chat_params_init_gpt_oss` tolerates exactly one variant of this — the `stray_commentary` arm from #21286 (`<|channel|>commentary` + optional ` to=assistant`, followed immediately by a well-formed channel). Everything else fails the final PEG parse, `common_chat_peg_parse` logs `unparsed peg-native output`, and the server returns an error mid-stream: **"The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format"**. The rest of the turn — usually a perfectly good `analysis` block and a valid tool call — is discarded.

Observed rate on a production Home Assistant voice assistant (tool-calling, ~13k-token prompt, `--jinja`, reasoning_effort medium via `LLAMA_ARG_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS={"reasoning_effort":"medium"}`): **3 of 72 turns** over ~48 h, 6 more in the two days before — 9 distinct garblings, listed in full below. Every one is a hard failure to the client even though the model's actual content after the bad header is intact.

Launch flags:
```
llama-server.exe --model gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4.gguf --alias qwen3.5-9b --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 -ngl 99 -c 24576 --jinja --parallel 1 -fa on --cache-reuse 256 -ub 2048 -b 2048 --metrics --no-webui --temp 1.0 --top-p 1.0
```

Steps to reproduce: run a long tool-calling conversation at temp 1.0 with the stock gpt-oss chat template and a tools array (ours is ~24 function tools); roughly 1 turn in 25 trips it. I can't force it deterministically — it is a sampling event — but the raw outputs below are exactly what the parser received.

Suggested handling (either would fix every case below): treat any `<|channel|>` prefix that is not a recognised channel name as stray text and resume at the next `<|start|>assistant<|channel|>` / `<|channel|>analysis|final|commentary<|message|>`; or, when the final parse fails but a lenient re-parse succeeds, return the lenient result instead of erroring (the lenient path already exists for `is_partial=true`). Happy to test a branch — this rig produces a hit within an hour or two of normal use.

### First Bad Commit

Unknown — the stray-header tolerance in #21286 (Apr 2026) covers one shape; these are the others. Present at b10488; no relevant parser commits since.

### Relevant log output

Nine distinct `unparsed peg-native output` lines (truncated to the header + first sentence; the trailing content in each was a normal analysis block and, where applicable, a valid `to=functions.*` tool call). Timestamps are seconds since server start.

```
10.01 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary to=assistant<|channel|>commentary?commentary=short?comment?…???<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We need to answer: "What causes the porch light to come on at night?" ...
346.05 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>We need to answer: Is the sump pump something I should worry about tonight? We must consider safety. ...
2750.27 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary to=assistant ...commentary?<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>The user: "ask the expert whether we should replace the roof this fall or wait until spring." ...
177.21 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary... The user asks: did the Cubs win yesterday? The sports scores result includes many games ...
177.38 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary 2? The request "turn on the light" ambiguous. We have to ask clarifying question ...
179.42 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary?commentary?We need temperature difference. Also need outside temperature. Get outdoor temperature.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>Need GetLiveContext for Outdoor Temperature.<|end|
182.48 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>commentary says tool returned, so now respond.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>User asked: "is there a tornado risk tonight"
185.23 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>...?We need answer. The user: "did the Cubs win yesterday". It's 2026-08-21? Actually current date is 2026-08-22. ...
1.06 W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <|channel|>??<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We must comply with the gating rules. Input: "should I seal the driveway this weekend" ...
```

Client-side symptom (Home Assistant `llama_cpp` integration via the `openai` Python client): `openai.APIError: The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format`, raised from the SSE stream.

### Operating systems

### Command line

Two Apple M4 machines, 16 GB unified memory each, connected by a Thunderbolt bridge.

# machine A (main node) -- FAILS
llama-bench -m Qwen_Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-IQ3_XXS.gguf \
  --rpc 192.168.2.1:50052 -ts 0.50/0.50 -fa on -b 1024 -ub 512 -p 512 -n 128

# machine A -- IDENTICAL except for -mmp 0 -- WORKS
llama-bench -m Qwen_Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-IQ3_XXS.gguf \
  --rpc 192.168.2.1:50052 -ts 0.50/0.50 -fa on -b 1024 -ub 512 -p 512 -n 128 -mmp 0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When a model is sharded across an RPC device, the main node appears to retain the entire
model in memory rather than only its own share. The effective size limit for a distributed
model therefore stays roughly equal to what a **single** node can hold, which defeats the
purpose of splitting it.

Disabling mmap (`-mmp 0`, or `--load-mode none` on `llama-server`) fixes it completely, with
no other change.

Model used: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-IQ3_XXS`, 15,761,446,528 bytes (14.68 GiB).
Metal `recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize` is 13,958.64 MB on the main node and 12,713.12 MB on
the worker, so 14.68 GiB fits on neither alone but fits easily across both.

**A/B, one variable:**

| flags | result |
| --- | --- |
| default load mode | fails, `llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3` |
| `-mmp 1` (explicit) | fails, same error |
| `-mmp 0` | works: 322.75 t/s prompt, 26.12 t/s decode |

**Measured during a failing run**, sampling resident memory on both machines at the same
moment:

- main node `llama-bench` RSS: **12.15 GiB**
- RPC worker `ggml-rpc-server` RSS: **7.57 GiB**
- total resident across both: **19.7 GiB, for a 14.68 GiB model**

The worker really does receive its shard, and the main node keeps a full copy anyway.

The OOM is on the main node's local Metal device (`MTL0`), and compute buffers are far too
small to explain it:

```
sched_reserve: RPC0[192.168.2.1:50052] compute buffer size =    70.02 MiB
sched_reserve:       MTL0 compute buffer size =   493.52 MiB
sched_reserve:        CPU compute buffer size =     8.52 MiB
```

**Threshold behaviour**, all with the same two machines and default load mode:

| model | size | result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 | 11.28 GiB | works, splits correctly (5.68 GiB on the worker) |
| GLM-4.7-Flash IQ4_XS | 15.13 GiB | fails |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B IQ3_XXS | 14.68 GiB | fails |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M | 20.76 GiB | fails |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B Q3_K_S | 20.11 GiB | fails |

Everything at or below about 12 GiB works. Everything above fails. That threshold matches
the main node's own Metal working set, not the combined capacity of the two machines. With
`-mmp 0` every one of the failing models above loads and runs correctly across the split.

**Hypothesis, offered tentatively.** Metal on this build reports `use residency sets = true`
at init. If the mmapped model pages are placed in a residency set on the main node, the OS
cannot evict them, so sharding weights to the RPC device never releases the main node's
mapping. I have not read the allocator closely enough to confirm this, and the mechanism may
be different. The observation and the `-mmp 0` workaround are what I am confident about.

**Why this is easy to miss.** The failure does not look like an out of memory error from the
client side. `llama-bench` reports `failed to decode prompt batch, res = -3` and
`llama-server` reports a generic decode failure, so it reads as a model or architecture
problem rather than a memory one. I spent several hours attributing it to specific model
architectures (and wrongly concluded that three separate models were unsupported) before
finding that one flag fixed all of them.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected. Observed on b10470 (`34af94c`). I do not know whether earlier versions behave
differently, and I have not tested current master.

### Relevant log output

```
ggml_metal_synchronize: error: command buffer 0 failed with status 5
error: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
graph_compute: ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async failed with error -1
process_ubatch: failed to compute graph, compute status: -1
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
test_prompt: failed to decode prompt batch, res = -3
llama_bench: error: failed to run prompt
```

## Overview

This adds an optional CUTLASS path for block-scaled dense GEMMs on SM120 and SM121.

NVFP4 and MXFP4 weights are repacked when loaded. Prefill uses the CUTLASS W4A4 kernel, while M=1 NVFP4 decode uses MMVQ with the repacked layout. Unsupported cases keep using the existing CUDA path.

### CUTLASS weight repacking



Existing GGUF files are loaded unchanged. When a supported dense MXFP4/NVFP4 tensor is uploaded, its FP4 values are packed row by row with K padding. The scales are stored in two layouts: a 128-row tiled layout for the SM120 CUTLASS kernel and a row-major layout for small-batch decode. Prefill and decode share the FP4 values, so only the scales are duplicated. Unsupported tensors remain in the normal CUDA buffer.


## Results

### Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4

Tested on one Pro 6000 using Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4. 

| Test | Native | Repacked | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| pp512 | 4,677.41 tok/s | 5,275.83 tok/s | +12.79% |
| pp2048 | 4,731.96 tok/s | 5,298.54 tok/s | +11.97% |
| pp8192 | 4,549.87 tok/s | 5,067.73 tok/s | +11.38% |
| tg128 | 51.7937 tok/s | 52.2284 tok/s | +0.84% |

All 10 repacked backend test cases passed.

### Qwen3.6-27B MXFP4

Tested on an Pro 6000 with the same binary.

#### Prefill

| Test | Native | CUTLASS | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| pp512 | 5,269.90 tok/s | 5,717.95 tok/s | +8.50% |
| pp2048 | 5,520.01 tok/s | 6,251.92 tok/s | +13.26% |
| pp8192 | 4,975.71 tok/s | 5,431.93 tok/s | +9.17% |

#### Decode

| Test | Native | Repacked | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| tg128 | 80.956 tok/s | 81.884 tok/s | +1.15% |

Prefill uses the cutlass path, while m=1 decode uses the repacked reader. all 12 mxfp4/nvfp4 backend correctness tests passed.

## Build

The path is disabled by default and requires CUDA 12.9 or newer.

```bash
cmake -B build \
    -DGGML_CUDA=ON \
    -DGGML_CUDA_CUTLASS=ON

cmake --build build --config Release -j
```

CUTLASS is fetched automatically by CMake at a pinned revision. An existing checkout can be used with `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_CUTLASS`.


## Requirements

-  I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
-  AI usage disclosure: Yes, paired with Codex

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

This PR has comprehensive decode-side optimizations on K-quant dense models for Adreno GPUs, including optimization for skinny GEMM that are essential for speculative decoding and MTP (multi-token prediction):
- A tiled lm_head/embed GEMV layout.
- A cooperative-K medium-batch q4_K/q6_K GEMM to lower register pressure
- A multi-row f16 decode GEMV (attention projections + lm_head) 
- A q4_K MUL_MAT+GLU decode fusion. 
- Every default is gated on measured, per-device data, and each piece has an env override.

Fleet defaults vs upstream, Adreno 840 (A8X), Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M:

| | delta | pairs | order bias |
|---|---|---|---|
| **tg128** | **+16.99%** (16.91 vs 14.45 t/s) | 4/4 | +0.03% |
| pp512 | −0.00% (neutral) | 3/4 | +0.01% |

Per switch, against the route each replaces:

| switch | A8X (840) | X2E (X2-90) |
|---|---|---|
| tiled lm_head/embed GEMV | **+11.9%** tg128 (6/6 pairs) | **+6.9%** tg128 (4/4 pairs) |
| cooperative-K medium-batch GEMM | — | **+85.8 / +84.4 / +83.6%** at pp2 / pp4 / pp8 (12/12) |

Note the wins live in the decode GEMV and the medium-batch GEMM, not long prefill. 
- This is a **K-quant dense-decode** win
- MXFP4/MoE models and Q8_0 builds are structurally untouched.

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

## Additional information
 
<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

**Gating:**

- The tiled defaults are on for X2E and A8X specifically; 
- The A7X regresses on the tiled layout and is excluded. Env forces either way.
- The q4_K split-K GEMV is X2E-only: 
  - ungated it measured 840 −1.3% / 850 −20.0%. 
  - With the gate,  both parts keep their existing path.
- The flat-GEMV large-m escape stays opt-in
  - it is slower than the multi-quad route that now covers the same long-vocab shapes (A8X -10.3%, X2E -3.7%).
  - This supersedes the routing added in #26427 rather than disabling it. 
  - With the escape off, a vocab-scale K-quant lm_head is not sent back to the old `gemv_noshuffle` path: it lands on the multi-quad GEMV, which is default-on with no device gate (`ne01 % 4 == 0`, `ne01 >= 32768`).
  - The `ne01 % 128` correctness escape is independent of the opt-in and still fires first.

**Correctness ordering.** 
- The `ne01 % 128` escape guards a layout bug, not a performance choice:
   - the noshuffle layout packs two rows per 32-bit texel and the GEMV reads it with a `ne01/2` texel stride under an exact-cover dispatch with no store guard, so `ne01 % 128 != 0` misaligns every odd column and writes past the end of `dst`. 
   - It now precedes the opt-in gate, so it stays reachable in the default configuration. 
   - Order is: tiled deferral, correctness escape, opt-in, size heuristics.

**Which models see the gain.** 

Gated on a q4_K/q6_K lm_head/embed (tiled additionally needs vocab ≥ 32768, ne00 ≥ 512, and for q6_K vocab % 128 == 0; the cooperative-K GEMM needs a q4_K GEMM at n_q ∈ [2..8]). 

Scanned over a 108-GGUF local model set: **65 eligible, 43 not.**
- *Benefits:* 
  - Q4_0/Q4_K_M quants of Qwen3 (1.7B/4B), Qwen3.5-4B (incl. MTP), 
  - gemma-4  (E2B/E4B/12b/26B-A4B), gemma-3n-E4B, 
  - Llama-3/3.2, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen — the mainstream dense-decode set.
- *Does not benefit:*
  - every `-Q8_0` build (24 — the lm_head stays Q8_0); 
  - F16/BF16/Q4_0/F32  lm_heads (7, including **both gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 builds — gpt-oss gets none of this**, it contains zero q4_K/q6_K tensors); 
  - q6_K vocab not a multiple of 128 (6, e.g. gemma-3-4b at  262208); 
  - vocab < 32768 (3); ne00 < 512 (2).  

**Intel NEO GPU** 
- The rms+rope fusion precondition also fixed a previously-undetected garbage path on Intel NEO: `RMS_NORM_MUL_ROPE` 8/72 → 72/72. 
- This is not an Adreno-only cleanup.

## Requirements

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

This PR widens kernel selection to the shapes that were falling through, speeds up the cluster
kernel, and moves gemma-4's DK=512 decode onto the GPU via FA on. Massive gains on TG are observed:
a number of models now run faster with FA on than off.

### Issues
The Adreno decode flash-attention path selected its multi-query (MQ) and cluster kernels for a narrow set of shapes; everything else fell back to the `q1`/`q1_split` kernels. Those fallbacks are bad in two specific ways:
- **Register pressure.** `flash_attn_f32_f16_q1_split` reports 1168 bytes of private memory per work item (the q8_0 twin 1664, the DV=512 `q1` 2048) against the ~512-byte budget where this compiler stops spilling; their workgroup cap drops to 192.
- **Redundant traffic.** They run one workgroup per *query* head, so every head in a GQA group re-reads the same K and V rows. The MQ kernels read each row once per KV head.

### Solutions
**Commit 1 - coverage and cluster performance.**
- Adds `MQ_GQA=2/3` programs at head_dim 128, an `MQ_GQA=8`/`FA_CL_C=16` cluster at head_dim 64 (the stock GQA=8 width fails the `DK_VEC % FA_CL_C` check there), and the same cluster for q8_0 KV, which previously had no MQ route at all. - Four performance changes follow:
  -  pooling the flash-decoding partials buffer (it was a `clCreateBuffer` per attention layer per token);
  -  folding the per-head cluster reductions into one halving butterfly (32 `sub_group_shuffle_xor` per KV row down to 15, bit-identical)
  - a head split that runs an `MQ_GQA = gqa/N` program on N workgroups per KV head.
  - a 64-thread workgroup for it.

**Commit 2 - gemma-4 DK=512 decode.**
- gemma-4 interleaves DK=256 sliding-window layers with DK=512 global ones. `supports_op` declined FLASH_ATTN_EXT for DK=512 at decode, so every global layer became a CPU island: 17 graph splits against 3, with that layer's K and V views (8.4 MB each at n_kv=4096) copied device-to-host every token.
- Declining was nevertheless the better trade, because the only DK=512 decode kernel was the 2 KB/work-item `q1` - forcing that back onto the GPU measures 27% *slower* than paying for the CPU islands.

The shared DK=512 program is built `-D FA_DECODE_MINIMAL` (dropping `q1_vec`) to stay under the shader compiler's host-memory ceiling, so that spilled fallback was all those layers had. Two new single-kernel programs fix that, the way `FA_PREFILL_ONLY` already isolates the BM tile:
- `FA_VEC_ONLY` builds `q1_vec` alone (2 KB -> 192 B per work item) and `FA_MQ_SPLIT_ONLY` builds`q1_vec_mq_split` alone. The same narrow build also serves DK=256 GQA=8, whose stock kernel requests a 192-thread workgroup that the X2-90 refuses per-kernel - it registered as compiled and then never dispatched.
- These shapes carry their own `n_kv` floor, since gemma-4's window caps n_kv at 1024/256, below the split-tuned `FD_MIN_N_KV`; the floor is scoped to shapes that have a narrow kernel, so no other model's decode routing changes.

### Results

tg32 at depth 4096 against the same tree with the new paths disabled, as base/patched/patched/base
sequences with a clock proxy sampled per arm.

| model | shape | X2-90 | X1-85 | Adreno 840 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 | dk 64, GQA 8 | +7.7% (+19.8% at d16384) | - | +8.3% |
| Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M | dk 128, GQA 4 | +4.8% (+5.9% at d16384) | +18.0% | +61% |
| Llama-3-8B Q4_0 | dk 128, GQA 4 | +3.2% | - | +42% |
| Mistral-7B v0.3 Q4_K_M | dk 128, GQA 4 | - | - | +33% |
| gemma-4 E4B Q4_0 | dk 512 + dk 256 | +44.5% (+59.6% at d8192) | +21…37% | +34…36% |
| gemma-4 E2B Q4_0 | dk 512 + dk 256 | +53.9% (+60.1% at d8192) | +17…45% | +96% |

Two notes:

- On the Adreno 840, GQA=4 at head_dim 128 previously ran *slower* with flash attention than
  without.
   - FA-on now beats FA-off by 9-13% on all three GQA=4 models there, so the "use `-fa 0` on  this device" workaround is no longer needed for that shape.
   - GQA=3 still trails FA-off by ~10% and is not addressed here.
- On gemma-4, `-fa auto` previously resolved to **disabled**, because the DK=512 decline fired at the `n_q == 1` probe shape. It now resolves to **enabled**. Users who never passed `-fa` will see this change.

## Additional shapes and kernel improvements

Four further gaps in the same routing table, added after the first review pass.

### Head size 128: the head split, and an `n_kv` floor of its own

**The head-split program was never built at head size 128.** It was fenced to head size 64, and the
narrow multi-query builder to head sizes 256 and 512, so a GQA-8 shape at 128 — Qwen3-30B-A3B's
decode shape — had no head-split form to route to and ran one work-group per KV head. Building it
there is worth, per-op on `test-backend-ops` at KV 4096 and 8192 with the split off then on:
+49.9% / +51.8% on an Adreno X2-90, +82.1% / +55.3% on an Adreno 840, and +112.4% / +119.3% on an
X1-85. Three generations, no inversion. End to end on Qwen3-30B-A3B that is +23.5% and +28.8% tg at
4096 and 8192 tokens of depth.

**The multi-query routes inherited the flash-decoding split's `n_kv` floor**, which answers a
different question — whether splitting the KV range across work-groups pays — and at 2048 it meant
the MQ routes did not engage at all below that length. Giving them their own floor at 32 gains, at
depth 0 and 1024: +12% / +63% on Qwen3-30B-A3B, +10% / +43% on Qwen3-4B, +1% / +8% on gpt-oss-20b,
and neutral on gemma-4-26B. Depth 4096 is flat everywhere, which is the control — above the old
floor the routing does not change, and it does not move.

`FLASH_ATTN_EXT` in `test-backend-ops`: 5117 and 2696 cases OK, 0 FAIL, unchanged from the
unpatched baseline build on the same device.

### GQA ratio 16

gemma-4-12B has 16 query heads over a single KV head on its 8 global-attention layers, i.e.
DK=DV=512 at GQA ratio 16. The narrow multi-query decode gate admits ratios 4, 8 and 2, so that
shape matched no arm and every one of

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
Issues: 
- The gpt-oss MoE FFN applies its three per-expert biases as three separate `ADD_ID` ops. 
- Each is an **in-place** read-modify-write of a `[n_ff, n_expert_used, n_tokens]` f32 tensor - 23.6 MB read and 23.6 MB written per layer to perform one add per element
- In every case the very next operation reads that same memory again.

This optimization folds them into the ops that already read the tensor:
- **gate and up biases** are folded into `swiglu_oai`, in a new kernel  `kernel_add_id_add_id_swiglu_oai`  `kernels/moe_add_id_glu.cl`). Six passes over the tensor become two reads and one write.
- **the down bias** is folded into the MoE combine, via a sibling kernel `kernel_moe_combine_bias_f32` so the existing unfused combine is left untouched.

Both matmuls keep their own dispatches. Only the epilogue collapses, so the change is independent of the expert weight type and does not touch the vendor GEMM.

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->
Adreno X2-90, `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4-q8attn.gguf`, `-fa 1 -ngl 99`, f16 KV, with Adreno binary (QPM) kernels, matched pairs with alternating lead:

| test | before | after | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| pp512 | 683.93 / 683.73 | 706.89 / 707.82 | **+3.36% / +3.52%** |
| pp2048 | 626.52 / 624.84 | 645.26 / 645.30 | **+2.99% / +3.27%** |
| tg32 | 37.69 / 37.64 | 37.91 / 37.71 | +0.58% / +0.19% |

Adreno 840, `gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4.gguf`: **+1.08%** (gate/up fold) and **+0.54%** (down fold), each the mean of 4 matched pairs with every pair agreeing in sign.

Per-fusion attribution, measured by toggling the opt-outs on one binary: gate/up fold **+2.25%**, down fold **+1.26%**. Control with both disabled returns to baseline at **-0.24%**.

Verified **not** to fire on gemma-4-26B-A4B, which has no per-expert biases and fuses gate and up into a single `ffn_gate_up_exps` tensor: measured +0.12% / +0.19%, i.e. noise. Models outside the pattern decline cleanly and are unaffected.

### Correctness

Output is byte-identical to the unfused path for each fusion independently.

### Name and Version

```
version: 1 (8086439)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Also verified present on current `master` (`a4107133a634`, 2026-07-04) — see "First Bad Commit / still-present" below.

### Operating systems

Linux (x86_64)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```
llama-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8091 \
  -m gpt-oss-120b-mxfp4-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -ub 512 -c 32768 --jinja -fa on
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

For `gpt-oss` (harmony format), a **non-streaming** chat completion whose final message contains bare content with **no channel markup** hard-throws HTTP 500 instead of returning the content.

**Root-cause chain (all still present on current master):**

1. `common_chat_params_init_gpt_oss()` in `common/chat.cpp` builds a PEG grammar whose top-level alternation (`final_msg | unsolicited`, or `tool_call | final_msg` with tools) requires `<|channel|>...<|message|>` markup on every branch. There is no content-only / bare-final fallback arm.
2. When the model emits a content-only final (which gpt-oss does intermittently — notably under a system prompt demanding "strict JSON only, no channels, no reasoning"), the final parse fails.
3. For the **non-streaming** path, `tools/server/server-task.h:388` calls `update_chat_msg(content, /*is_partial=*/false, ...)`.
4. The lenient partial-AST fallback in `common/chat.cpp` (`if (is_partial && result.end > 0) { ... return msg; }`) is therefore unreachable, and the mismatch throws `"The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format"`, surfaced to the client as a bare HTTP 500.

No CLI flag relaxes this for gpt-oss (`--jinja` cannot be dropped for this model). Streaming requests are unaffected because they exercise the `is_partial=true` path.

**Repro:** `POST 127.0.0.1:8091/v1/chat/completions`, model `gpt-oss-120b`, with a system prompt insisting the assistant reply with strict JSON and nothing else — no reasoning, no channel markup:

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-oss-120b",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a strict JSON API. Reply with a single JSON object and NOTHING else — no reasoning, no channel markup, no prose."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Return {\"ok\": true}"}
  ]
}
```

- Reproduces the 500 **5/5** with the strict-JSON system prompt above.
- A plain "reply with JSON" (no strict-no-channel instruction) returns 200.
- **Non-deterministic** on identical requests — hit rate ~23% across mixed structured/JSON traffic in production.

**First Bad Commit / still-present:** Not a regression — this is a design limitation of the harmony non-streaming path. Verified byte-identical on build `8086439` (2026-06-17) and current `master` `a4107133a634` (2026-07-04): the `common_chat_params_init_gpt_oss` grammar, the `is_partial`-gated fallback, and `server-task.h:388`'s hardcoded `is_partial=false` are unchanged across the ~190 commits between them.

**Suggested directions (non-prescriptive):**

- Allow a content-only final to parse leniently (treat unmarked trailing content as the `final` channel) rather than hard-throwing; **or**
- On the non-streaming final path, fall back to the lenient (`is_partial`-style) parse before throwing, so a well-formed-but-unmarked final degrades to plain content instead of a 500.

Related-but-distinct precedent: the Gemma-4 analog (#25072 / PR #25100, closed without merge) was ruled a template bug; this one is specifically the gpt-oss non-streaming final path.

### Relevant log output

```
srv  ... : ... "The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format"
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
```

## Title
Duplicate rule definitions in generated GBNF grammar with large `tools` list (harmony/gpt-oss) → "failed to parse grammar"

## Description

When sending a chat completion request with a large `tools` array (17 function definitions, none using `$ref`/`$defs`) to `llama-server` running `gpt-oss-120b` (harmony chat format, started with `--jinja`), the JSON-schema-to-grammar converter emits **the same GBNF rule name with an identical body twice**, and the server then fails with:

```
failed to parse grammar
Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar
```
returned as HTTP 400 to the client.

This is *not* the same as #21228 (MAX_REPETITION_THRESHOLD / `$ref` expansion) — there is no `$ref` or `$defs` anywhere in the schema, and the failure is a hard 400, not a silent fallback to unconstrained generation.

## Environment

- llama.cpp build: `b10069-178a6c449` (from `system_fingerprint` in a successful response on the same server)
- Model: `ggml-org/gpt-oss-120b-GGUF` (MXFP4 quant), harmony chat template
- Server started with `--jinja -ngl 999`
- Client: OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, `tools` array with 17 function definitions (a coding-agent tool list — file read/write/edit/grep/glob/bash/etc.)

## What I observed

Across repeated requests with the full 17-tool list, the generated grammar (visible via server stdout/stderr) contains duplicate `::=` definitions for the same rule name. The specific rule that duplicates **varies between requests** — observed twice, in two different tools:

Run 1 (duplicate in the `todowrite` tool's array-of-objects property):
```
tool-todowrite-schema-todos-item-content-kv ::= "\"content\"" space ":" space string
tool-todowrite-schema-todos-item-content-kv ::= "\"content\"" space ":" space string
```

Run 2 (duplicate in the `question` tool's array-of-objects property):
```
tool-question-schema-questions-item-options-kv ::= "\"options\"" space ":" space tool-question-schema-questions-item-options
tool-question-schema-questions-item-question-kv ::= "\"question\"" space ":" space string
tool-question-schema-questions-item-options-kv ::= "\"options\"" space ":" space tool-question-schema-questions-item-options
tool-question-schema-questions-item-question-kv ::= "\"question\"" space ":" space string
```

Both times the server then fails to parse its own generated grammar:
```
E failed to parse grammar
E srv    send_error: task id = 0, error: Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar
E srv  process_sing: failed to launch slot with task, id_task = 0
```

Both `todowrite` and `question` define an array property whose `items` schema is a plain object with 3+ required string-typed properties (`content`/`status`/`priority`, and `question`/`header`/`options` respectively) — no `$ref`, no shared/reused schema object, no anyOf/oneOf.

## What does NOT reproduce it

To isolate the trigger, I tried two smaller repros against the same running server/model:

1. A single synthetic tool with one array property whose `items` schema has 3 required string properties (structurally identical to the `todowrite`/`question` array-item shape) — **succeeded (200 OK)**, no duplication.
2. Just the `todowrite` + `question` tools together (2 of the 17) — **succeeded (200 OK)**, no duplication.

So the bug does not reproduce with 1 or 2 tools in isolation — it needs the full (or at least a much larger) combined tool list to trigger. This points at something scale-dependent in the rule-name cache/dedup logic (e.g. a hash collision, a vector reallocation, or an ordering bug that only surfaces once enough rules have been registered), rather than something wrong with any single tool's schema.

## Reproduction

Minimizing further wasn't successful (see above), so here is the full request that reliably reproduces it on our setup. Save as `repro.json` and:
```
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:PORT/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @repro.json
```

`repro.json`:
```json
{
  "model": "ggml-org/gpt-oss-120b-GGUF:gpt-oss-120b-MXFP4",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "call todowrite with one item, then call question with one question"
    }
  ],
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "agent_manager",
        "description": "Inspect and orchestrate Agent Manager sessions, or start new sessions, in the VS Code extension.\n\nUse `action: \"list\"` to inspect the compact Agent Manager overview and `action: \"prompt\"` to send one instruction to one existing managed session. List results include user-defined sections, ungrouped worktrees, and managed local sessions. Optional filters can narrow by section ID or by `idle`, `busy`, `retry`, `offline`, or `waiting` state. Prompting is targeted only: it does not broadcast, create a session, or wait for the target to finish.\n\nTo start sessions, keep using the existing `mode` and `tasks` input without an action. Use start mode when the user explicitly asks you to fan out work into Agent Manager, create Agent Manager worktrees, or start multiple Agent Manager sessions for independent tasks.\n\nModes:\n- `worktree`: creates a new Agent Manager git worktree for each task, like the New Worktree dialog.\n- `local`: creates Agent Manager sessions in the current workspace directory without git worktree isolation.\n\nEach task may provide a prompt, a short display name, a branch name, a `model`, and a model-specific reasoning `variant`. ## Overview
This PR is to fix a bug in MoE scatter. 

- MoE prompt processing on the OpenCL backend is not reproducible run-to-run: the same binary on the same prompt returns one of several outputs. 
- Measured on granite-3.0-3b-a800m-Q4_K_M (Adreno X2-90, greedy, llama-simple -n 64, 3 prompts × 5 runs each), every prompt produced 2–3 distinct outputs across 5 runs.

### Root cause
- `kernel_moe_scatter` assigns each token its slot within its expert via `atomic_inc(&slot_counter[expert])`, so the token→slot packing depends on which work-item wins the atomic and varies every run. 
- The ragged MoE prefill GEMM is sensitive to that packing order; the non-ragged path happens to be immune.

### Fix
- This PR replaces the atomic slot grab with a deterministic rank: a token's slot is its position in flat (token, k) order among the tokens routed to the same expert — a fixed function of the routing input. 
- One workgroup per expert walks the routing list in blocks of 64 with a workgroup scan and a running carry. 
- Default on; GGML_OPENCL_MOE_STABLE_SCATTER=0 restores the previous behavior.
- 2 files, backend-only (ggml-opencl.cpp + kernels/moe_sort_by_expert.cl).

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->
### Determinism verification
- With the fix: 5/5 identical runs on every prompt, and the output matches an O(N·topK) reference implementation exactly.
- Six MoE models on the X2-90, 3 runs each, all single-output and coherent: gpt-oss-20b-MXFP4, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Q4_K_M, Qwen3-unsloth-30B-A3B-Q4_0, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4_MOE, and granite-3.0-3b in Q4_K_M and MXFP4_MOE. 
- gpt-oss also 3/3 on the Adreno 840.

### Cost
Prefill only — the scatter runs on the GEMM path, decode never calls it: pp512 −0.63% on granite-3.0-3b (40 experts), −0.15% on Qwen3-30B-A3B (128 experts).
### Scope
- This fixes run-to-run reproducibility. 
- The ragged and non-ragged paths still produce different roundings of equal quality (MUL_MAT_ID max err 2.68e-05 vs 2.79e-05 against the CPU reference); 
- A host comment claiming the ragged path is byte-identical is corrected as part of this change. That difference is a rounding choice, not a wrong answer.
### Testing
test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT_ID: Adreno X2-90, 383 OK / 0 FAIL.
The Adreno 840 declines all MUL_MAT_ID cases at these shapes in test-backend-ops; its evidence is the real-model determinism runs above.

## Overview

This PR improves NVFP4 W4A4 activation quantization in both quality and performance

## Additional information

1. Quality was gained by adding per-channel-based amax scaling as an alternative path to honoring pre-calibrated scales. This was proposed here https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/22042#discussioncomment-16681029
2. Perf was realized by:
   * Adding a fused kernel that computes per-channel-based amax first
   * Reducing latency+ maximizing coalescing without templating by doing 256-bit (i.e. one thread = 1 sector) loads
   * Use nvfp4 intrinsics as they are fundamentally faster (they dispatch to dedicated instructions in the ISA that do HW-accelearted conversion)
   * Doing the scale in the MMQ epilogue before writing back to GMEM. The ternary operator reduced predicate efficacy on non-NVFP4 quants so I restricted this to NVFP4 only for now

Note: I did try to get rid of scale-search completely, but did not manage to be iso-quality. I traded 5% E2E performance by adding this back in as it increases quality arguably

items.body:
## Overview
**Why** Performance gain via fusion 

**What** 

This branch changes the implementation of

$$s_W \odot ({\hat{W}}X) \quad \text{and} \quad s_W \odot ({\hat{W}}X) + b$$

used repeatedly throughout model layers (for instance Qwen dense projections and MoE expert projections).

For a quantized weight matrix $\hat{W}$, input $X$, external weight scale $s_W$, and optional bias $b$, the master branch evaluates these as separate graph operations:

$$C = \hat{W}X$$
$$Y = s_W \odot C \quad (\text{+ optionally} ; b)$$

This means MMQ writes $C$ to global memory, then a separate elementwise kernel reads $C$, multiplies by $s_W$ (and optionally adds $b$), and writes $Y$.

The branch computes $Y$ directly in the MMQ writeback stage, removing one intermediate tensor write/read and one CUDA kernel launch per layer. On the compute graph level the branch detects and optimizes the MUL_MAT → MUL(scale) and MUL_MAT_ID → MUL(scale) → ADD_ID(bias) patterns.

It moves $s_W$ and $b$ from separate graph operations into the final MMQ writeback, with:

Scalar scale — single $s_W$ value applied uniformly across all output rows (dense projections, GGML_OP_MUL_MAT)
ID-indexed scale — per-expert $s_W[e]$ selected by token routing index (MoE expert projections, GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID)
ID-indexed bias — per-expert row $b[e, :]$ added after scale, also index-selected (MoE projections, GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID only)
The fused epilogue is supported for all quantized types handled by MMQ (Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0, MXFP4, NVFP4, and others). A compile-time mmq_epilogue_mode::none specialization is generated for the highest-volume type/size combinations to avoid any register pressure overhead in the common no-epilogue case.

It does not change attention, routing, SwiGLU, expert aggregation, shared-expert gating, or residual equations.

$ ./llama-server --version
ggml_cuda_init: GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ:    no
