## Overview

Make `test-save-load-state` run across **all supported architectures** in ctest, instead of only the single `llama` arch (the downloaded `tinyllamas/stories15M` model).

- Add a `--models DIR` mode to `test-save-load-state` that runs the full save/load suite (tests 1-5) over every `*.gguf` in a directory, reporting per-model PASS/FAIL and exiting non-zero if any model fails.
- Replace the old single-model ctest with one that runs over all architectures using the existing `generate-models` fixture (`test-llama-archs -o <dir>`), mirroring how `test-recurrent-state-rollback` is wired. The single-model `-m` mode is preserved (still used by `ci/run.sh`).
- Bump the dummy-model training context from 128 to 256 in `test-llama-archs` so the per-sequence context (padded up to a multiple of 256) no longer exceeds `n_ctx_train` and triggers the "possible training context overflow" warning.

Running the suite over all architectures surfaced a few real save/load bugs, all fixed here:

- `context`: the on-device state seq copy required the write-side and read-side chunking to match 1:1, which diverged for non-contiguous sources; copy the flat write-side data into the read-side targets with a byte cursor across both tensor lists so the chunking no longer needs to match (fixes `memory buffer mismatch` on the gemma2 / gpt-oss / lfm2 device seq copy).
- `tests`: the dsv4 KV cache keeps per-sequence streams even in unified mode, so the baseline state save and the seq-copy loads now agree on `n_seq_max` (fixes the deepseek4 host seq-copy `n_stream` mismatch).
- `model`: `llm_graph_input_la` (minimax-01) stored a reference to the `llm_graph_params` temporary in `llama_context::process_ubatch`, which dangled on graph reuse and read destroyed stack memory in the state-load decode path; store a copy like the other graph input classes (fixes the minimax-01 state-load crash).
- `tests`: dummy DSA indexer heads now match the fused Lightning Indexer kernel (fixed NH=64) so the op runs on-device instead of falling back to CPU.

The full suite currently passes for all 109 generated architectures.

## Additional information

- The `test-save-load-state` ctest is now labeled `main` (it uses the generated dummy models, no download needed) and requires the `generate-models` fixture.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 0.1.0-dev (build 1, commit 4df29be)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Source at `4df29be4f4c3673f428170fda944a5b19f743bb8`, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`
(`CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE=-O3 -DNDEBUG`), g++ 14.2.0.

The `llama-server` that produced the coredump is a Vulkan build; the `llama-tokenize` used for every
threshold below is a HIP/ROCm build of the same commit with the same flags. The pre-tokenizer path is
CPU-only and identical in both, and both report the same version string.

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core), llama-server, llama-tokenize

### Command line

```shell
llama-server \
  --model gpt-oss-120b-MXFP4.gguf \
  --n-gpu-layers 99 --ctx-size 131072 --parallel 2 --cont-batching \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --batch-size 2048 --ubatch-size 2048 --load-mode none \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8081 --metrics --no-ui --no-slots
```

None of these flags is load-bearing. The crash is in pre-tokenization, before anything
backend-, batch- or KV-related is reached, and `llama-tokenize` reproduces it with no GPU at all.

### Problem description

**A single POST to `/v1/chat/completions` whose prompt contains a long unbroken run of one character
class terminates the server process with SIGSEGV, during tokenization, before any inference
happens.** It takes ~26,000 characters at the default 8 MiB stack. There is no error, no 4xx and no
log line — the process is simply gone, taking every slot's KV cache and prompt cache with it.

It requires no `tools`, no grammar, no streaming and no concurrency.

**What matters is the longest unbroken run that one alternative of the pre-tokenizer expression can
consume, not the prompt length.** libstdc++'s executor recurses once per repetition, and *every*
quantified alternative in this expression is a driver — not only the letter ones. Measured against
the shipped `llama-tokenize` at an 8 MiB stack, exit 139 = SIGSEGV:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `'x' * 26,000` → ok · `'x' * 26,500` | **SIGSEGV** |
| `'X' * 26,000` → ok · `'X' * 26,250` | **SIGSEGV** |
| `'日' * 26,000` → ok · `'日' * 26,250` | **SIGSEGV** |
| `'.' * 26,000` → ok · `'.' * 27,000` | **SIGSEGV** |
| `' ' * 26,000` → ok · `' ' * 28,000` | **SIGSEGV** |
| `'_' * 36,000`, `'\n' * 36,000` | **SIGSEGV** |
| English letters, spaces removed — 35,000 | **SIGSEGV** |
| Japanese, punctuation removed — 30,000 | **SIGSEGV** |
| `'Xx' * 18,000` — 36,000 alternating-case letters | ok |
| `'1234567890' * 6,600` — 66,000 digits | ok |
| English prose *with* spaces — 66,000 | ok |
| Japanese *with* ordinary `。` and `、` — 51,000 | ok |

Reading the alternation, three kinds of run recurse:

- **letters of a single case** — `((?=[\p{L}])([^A-Z]))+` drives lowercase runs and
  `((?=[\p{L}])([^a-z]))+` drives uppercase runs. A case change breaks both, which is why
  `'Xx' * 18,000` survives while `'x' * 26,500` and `'X' * 26,250` each die. Non-ASCII letters sit in
  **both** classes.
- **non-letter, non-digit, non-space characters** — ` ?[^\s\p{L}\p{N}]+[\r\n/]*`, so a long run of a
  single punctuation or symbol character is its own driver.
- **whitespace** — `\s*[\r\n]+`, `\s+(?!\S)`, `\s+`.

**Digits are the exception**: `\p{N}{1,3}` is bounded, so 66,000 digits tokenize fine.

So a space or a full stop ends a *letter* run but opens a run of its own. What keeps ordinary text
safe is that it alternates *short* runs of different classes — prose interleaves letter runs of a
dozen characters with one-character space runs, and neither approaches the threshold. Measured:
66,000 characters of English prose and 51,000 codepoints of Japanese with `。` and `、` both
tokenize normally.

**Non-ASCII does not lower the codepoint threshold.** `unicode_regex_split` collapses each non-ASCII
codepoint to a single category byte, so one CJK codepoint costs the same stack as one ASCII letter —
`'日'` brackets at 26,000 / 26,250, identical to `'X'`. What differs for scripts without inter-word
spaces is that long unbroken letter runs arise there naturally, where in English they have to be
constructed.

**It is reachable by an untrusted caller without anything exotic**: a ~26 KB body of one repeated
character — a letter, a space, a full stop — kills the process, repeatedly. `set_payload_max_length`
is never called anywhere in the tree outside its own definition in the vendored cpp-httplib, so
there is no size cap in front of it, and tokenization happens *before* the context-length check
(`tokenize_input_prompts` at `tools/server/server-context.cpp:4198`, inside
`handle_completions_impl`; the "exceeds the available context size" check is at `:3115`, after the
task is queued), so `--ctx-size` does not bound it either.

We have not surveyed which real-world content reaches ~26,000 characters of one class. The cases we
can name are programmatically whitespace-stripped text, a pathologically long single-case identifier
or concatenated token stream, and long runs of padding, separator or indentation characters.

### Root cause

`gpt-oss` resolves to `LLAMA_VOCAB_PRE_TYPE_GPT4O` (o200k_harmony, `case` label at
`src/llama-vocab.cpp:428`). Its pre-tokenizer expression is `src/llama-vocab.cpp:433`:

```
[^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?((?=[\p{L}])([^a-z]))*((?=[\p{L}])([^A-Z]))+(?:'[sS]|'[tT]|…)?|
[^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?((?=[\p{L}])([^a-z]))+((?=[\p{L}])([^A-Z]))*(?:'[sS]|'[tT]|…)?|
\p{N}{1,3}| ?[^\s\p{L}\p{N}]+[\r\n/]*|\s*[\r\n]+|\s+(?!\S)|\s+
```

That string is **not** in `unicode_regex_split_custom()`'s list of hand-written fast paths
(`src/unicode.cpp:1050`), so every tokenize call for this vocab falls through to
`unicode_regex_split_stl()` (`src/unicode.cpp:739`, reached from `:1367`) and therefore to
libstdc++'s `std::regex`, whose executor is a **recursive** backtracking DFS.

The worst driver is:

```
((?=[\p{L}])([^A-Z]))+
```

a lookahead **inside** a greedy repetition. libstdc++ recurses once per repe

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
/usr/local/bin/llama-server --split-mode tensor --model /home/myuser/models/unsloth/qwen3.6/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q6_K_XL.gguf --alias Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q6_K_XL --temperature 1.0 --top-k 20 --top-p 0.95 --min-p 0.0 --presence-penalty 1.5 --ctx-size 122880 --n-gpu-layers all --device CUDA0,ROCm0 --tensor-split 1.2,1 --main-gpu 0 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q5_1 --spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-mod --device-draft CUDA0 --n-gpu-layers-draft all --spec-draft-n-max 3 --prio-draft 3 --no-mmproj-auto --no-mmproj-offload --mlock --no-mmap --prio 3 --cache-ram -1 --kv-unified --log-verbosity 4 --parallel 2
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

#### Hardware

- Intel i9-11900K
- NVIDIA RTX A4000
- AMD RX 6900XT

#### GGML Backends

- CUDA
- ROCm/HIP

#### Problem

`--split-mode tensor` doesn't work with my CUDA+ROCm mix (raises `GGML_ASSERT(meta_buf_ctx->bufs[i])`). Prior to [`b9890`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b9890), I used `-sm row` (#24216), which worked and, as expected, noticeably sped up pp/tg. Since the CUDA backend no longer supports `-sm row` (`b9890` and later), I am forced to revert back to the default `-sm layer` (which works but is slower). When using `-sm row`, I did encounter the occasional error (usually a buffer or KV cache issue) when tuning `tensor-split`, `main-gpu`, and MTP draft params, but it otherwise worked fine when properly tuned.

I have tested and `-sm tensor` and `-sm row` for the following models in `b9890` (logs for both are below), yielding identical `GGML_ASSERT(meta_buf_ctx->bufs[i])` failures across all `-sm tensor`, and identical `llama_model_load: error loading model: device CUDA0 does not support split buffers` failures across all `-sm row`:

- Qwen3.6 27B [Unsloth UD-Q5_K_XL, Unsloth UD-Q6_K_XL]
- Qwen3.6 35B-A3B [Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL]
- Gemma4 31B [Unsloth it QAT UD-Q4_K_XL] + MTP [Unsloth it Q4_0]
- MiniMax M2.7 [Unsloth UD-IQ4_XS]

I have also tested the following, yielding the same failures:

- `main-gpu 0` vs `main-gpu 1`
- various `tensor-split`
- various `cache-ram`
- various `ctx-size`
- various `ctk` and `ctv` (symmetric and asymmetric)
- no spec/draft, `spec-type draft-mtp`, `spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-mod`

I use the CUDA and ROCm backends. I previously used CUDA+Vulkan for either and/or both GPUs in earlier builds (~`b9770` and earlier), but I had similar/identical failures with `-sm tensor`, and `-sm row` was somewhat unpredictable (leading me to switch to CUDA+ROCm, which was more stable).

#### Reproduce

I used the above `llama-server` command line for Unsloth's Qwen3.6 27B UD-Q6_K_XL. I also substituted `--split-mode tensor` for `--split-mode row`, which predictably failed.

The only set environment variable is `LLAMA_API_KEY`. I don't set `GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1` as it markedly handicaps speed.

Here are my build commands:
```
cmake --fresh -B 'build' \
  -DLLAMA_OPENSSL=ON \
  -DGGML_BACKEND_DL=ON \
  -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF \
  -DGGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON \
  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON \
  -DGGML_BLAS=OFF \
  -DGGML_HIP=ON \
  -DGGML_CUDA=ON \
  -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES='86' \
  -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER='/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc' \
  -DGGML_CUDA_NCCL=OFF \
  -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON
cmake --build 'build' --config Release -j $(($(nproc)-1))
sudo cmake --install 'build'
```
Note: I use `-DGGML_CUDA_NCCL=OFF` as I believe NCCL is ineffective with a mixed setup. I also recall previously running into some issues when building with `-DGGML_CUDA_NCCL=ON` (~`b9770` and earlier).

### Command line

```shell

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Loading large models with the ROCm backend hangs on my device. It loads in to memory (I can see memory usage grow) but it slows down as more memory is allocated and eventually just hangs. Or maybe slows down to a point where progress is so glacial I cannot observe it in a reasonable time. This bug only seems to affect larger models.

#### The following models exhibit this behaviour:

- MiniMax M2.1 (mradermacher/MiniMax-M2.1-i1-GGUF:IQ3_XXS, ~82GB in weights)
- Step 3.5 flash (bartowski/stepfun-ai_Step-3.5-Flash-GGUF:Q3_K_S, ~80GB)
- PrimeIntellect INTELLECT-3 (bartowski/PrimeIntellect_INTELLECT-3-GGUF:Q5_K_S, ~71GB)
- Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct (Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q6_K, ~61GB)
- GLM-4.6V (unsloth/GLM-4.6V-GGUF:Q4_K_XL, ~61GB)

Loading does not finish and it seems to be using between 1.7-2.0 CPU cores once stuck.

#### The following models load and run correctly on ROCm:

- gpt-oss-120b (mradermacher/gpt-oss-120b-Derestricted-i1-GGUF, ~60GB - slows down a lot near the end)
- GLM 4.7 Flash (unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-GGUF:Q8_K_XL, ~33GB - loads quickly)

All of these models load and run correctly using the Vulkan backend.

#### Additional info

I also tried some models with the CUDA backend and ZLUDA, which exhibited the same behaviour - smaller models load correctly, but loading larger models slows down until it seems to hang entirely.

## Summary

Under parallel mixed load (`-np 4 --kv-unified`), `llama-server` on an **integrated HIP GPU** (Strix Halo / gfx1151, 128 GB UMA) returns **complete responses that verbatim belong to a different, earlier request**. A large-prompt request receives, as its entire response, the literal answer text of a short request from an earlier round. We also observed a **chimeric** response fusing tokens of two different requests' expected outputs.

**Bisected to a single commit: c7d87229 "ggml-cuda : restore prop.integrated on HIP builds" (#24233).**

| build | result (validated responses, nonce-checked) |
|---|---|
| 505b1ed1 (parent window start) | clean — 0 violations / 168 |
| 5839ba35 (= parent of c7d87229) | clean — 0 / 36 |
| **c7d87229** | **cross-request replays: 3 hard / 36** |
| e8f19cc0 (window end) | cross-request replays: 7 hard + 1 chimera / 96 |

The same harness against **CPU builds** of both window endpoints shows no build-dependent difference (model-compliance noise only) — consistent with the culprit being the HIP integrated-memory path. This presumably explains why it went unnoticed: discrete GPUs are unaffected; it needs an **integrated** AMD GPU (`prop.integrated == 1`), multiple slots and concurrent mixed traffic.

## Environment

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo), gfx1151, 128 GB unified memory, ROCm 7.14, Ubuntu 24.04
- Build: `cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang++` (Release)
- Server: `llama-server -m <model> -ngl 999 -c 65536 -np 4 --kv-unified --jinja --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'`
- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE (Q4-class quant). First hit this in production behind LocalAI (same symptom after its vendored-llama.cpp bump crossed this commit); reproducing on vanilla `llama-server` rules the wrapper out.

## Reproduction

Load pattern per round (~30 s, script below): (B) short "repeat exactly this code: <nonce>" request → (C) large-prompt (~10k tokens) request whose system prompt requires echoing a per-request nonce in the first line → (D) burst of 4 concurrent short nonce requests (2 streamed / 2 plain). Every response is validated to contain its **own** nonce and no nonce of an **earlier** request.

On affected builds the round-N large-prompt request receives a literal foreign nonce as its complete response, typically from a round-(N−1) burst request. Verbatim from run logs at e8f19cc0:

```
R4/C got='pd-20260722-115649-3-d1'      (expected: reply echoing pc-...-4-c + a summary)
R5/C got='pd-20260722-115649-4-d2'
R6/C got='pd-20260722-115649-1-d1'
R7/C got='pd-20260722-115649-6-d1'
R8/C got='pd-20260722-115649-7-d1'
R3/C got='<!-- run:pc-20260722-115649-2-d0 -->'   <-- chimera: pc-...-2 stem fused with a -d0 burst suffix
```

In production we additionally observed: a poisoned slot re-serving its stored answer to unrelated requests **20+ minutes later** (the victim's `usage` then reports the foreign request's token counts), and occasional degeneration into repeated single characters (`/////...`).

<details><summary>repro-crossover.py (needs httpx)</summary>

```python

"""Repro: llama-server cross-request response mix-up under -np 4 --kv-unified.

Each round: (B) short "repeat exactly: <nonce>" request, (C) large-prompt
(~10k tokens) request whose system prompt requires echoing a per-request nonce,
(D) burst of 4 concurrent short nonce requests (2 streamed / 2 plain).
Every response must contain its OWN nonce and no nonce of an EARLIER request.

Usage: python3 repro-crossover.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8080 [--rounds 8]
Requires: pip install httpx
"""

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

This PR adds support for MTP (Multi Token Prediction) heads. I tested this on Qwen3.6 27B and Qwen3.6 35BA3B but in principle it should work for any MTP model. I've posted the detailed results below, but typically I see a steady-state acceptance of around 75% with 3 draft tokens, which is more than >2x speed-up over baseline. The design decisions I took to get to this stage are as follows:

- The MTP model is a separate model which loads from the same GGUF, the idea is that MTP should automatically start and we shouldn't need to distribute the MTP gguf separately but also it has it's own context/kv-cache etc. 
- I saw a problem in #18039 where the hidden features weren't propagated correctly across multiple ubatches, so this PR adds a separate "hook" for the MTP to consume after each `ubatch`
- The MTP speculative class is fairly trivial (although it does depend on #22400, but could work without it)

> [!TIP]
> MTP is compatible with Vision input and Tensor/Pipeline Parallelism

> [!NOTE]
> Prompt processing (PP) speed typically takes a negative hit when MTP is enabled mainly due to Device-To-Host (D2H) embedding transfers. It's something to be optimized in the future.

> [!NOTE]
> Parallel decoding with MTP is supported, but not fully optimized yet.

items.body:
## Overview

[GigaChat-3.5-432B-A28B](https://huggingface.co/ai-sage/GigaChat3.5-432B-A28B-GGUF) is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model with 432B total parameters and 28B active parameters. Built on a DeepSeek-V3-style backbone (MLA attention + DeepSeek MoE), it employs a hybrid attention architecture in which most layers use a Qwen3-Next Gated-Delta-Net (GDN) linear-attention block while a periodic subset retains full MLA attention. The architecture further incorporates gated RMSNorm with a low-rank gating bottleneck arranged as a four-norm sandwich (pre/post attention, pre/post MLP), gated attention applied before the output projection, and learnable MLA query/key scaling factors (alpha_q / alpha_kv). It utilizes 2-layer Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) for accelerated inference via speculative decoding.

items.body: This PR adds a new `--numa mirror` option which mirrors model weights to each Numa node on the system, and uses a thread-local var in the OMP threadpool to select the correct mirror copy local to the thread at runtime, to eliminate cross-socket traffic. Build instructions: ``` apt-get update apt-get install -y libnuma-dev libgomp1 cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-march=native" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-march=native" -DGGML_OPENMP=ON cmake --build build --parallel ``` To test: ```bash # No mirroring: ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ~/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf # Numa mirroring of model weights to every node: ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ~/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --numa mirror ``` Test system is a two-socket Xeon 6238R Cascade Lake, with 768GB of DDR4-2933 (6 channels per socket). Without `--numa mirror`: ``` developer@81ec6c6e6af6:/workspaces/llama-cpp-dbsanfte-dev$ ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ./.devcontainer/Qwen3-32B-Q6_K.gguf | model | size | params | backend | threads | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | pp512 | 20.99 ± 0.01 | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | tg128 | 1.91 ± 0.00 | build: c665d3c9 (6468) ``` With `--numa mirror`: ``` developer@81ec6c6e6af6:/workspaces/llama-cpp-dbsanfte-dev$ ./build/bin/llama-bench -m . /.devcontainer/Qwen3-32B-Q6_K.gguf --numa mirror | model | size | params | backend | threads | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | pp512 | 21.36 ± 0.11 | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | tg128 | 2.70 ± 0.00 | build: c665d3c9 (6468) ``` Intel PCM tool during mirror inference showing both sockets using local mem: There's still a bit of cross-socket traffic (5%) because only model weights are mirrored, not tensors created at inference time. I'll play with that, maybe mirroring those aggressively will help too, or maybe not. Right now anything created at inference time just gets set to live on Node 0.

### Feature Description

Add support for GLM 5.2, which makes use of sparse attention acceleration by skipping top-k index calculation for some layers

### Motivation

GLM 5.2 is currently the top ranked open weights model.

### Possible Implementation

The main change since 5.1 seems to be the sparse sparse attention, specifically the `index_skip_topk_offset: 3` and `index_topk_freq: 4` which signal that the sparse attention is only recalculated every 4 layers after the first 3, while in GLM 5.1 it was calculated every layer. A `indexer_types: [...]` is provided, but seems to just codify the offset+freq.

(I would figure this is being worked on, but I couldn't find any discussion, PR, or issue so I figured I would make one. If no one is actually looking into it, I could give it a shot at some point today.)

### Git commit

b10252 (2026-08-03). **Already fixed at HEAD by 6fed9f6f (#27071)** (global `n_merge <= 0` reject). Filing for the record: the pre-fix behavior is a divide-by-zero reachable from an untrusted mmproj in shipping downstream builds (LM Studio backend 2.28.2 = b10252).

### Operating system

Windows (0xC0000094) and Linux (SIGFPE), x86_64, CPU backend.

### Steps to reproduce the bug

1. Craft a Step3VL mmproj with `clip.vision.projector.scale_factor = 0` (KEY_PROJ_SCALE_FACTOR, optional read defaulting to 4). The global n_merge validation in b10252 (`clip.cpp:1884`) only rejects `< 0 || >= 65536` — **0 passes**. Generator: `python3 gen_mmproj_step3.py s30.gguf 0 256`.
2. Load it (loads and warms up cleanly — warmup_image_size path doesn't divide here), then send any image (128×128 grayscale works).
3. `mtmd_tokenize` → `split_batch_to_chunk` → `clip_n_output_tokens` (b10252 `clip.cpp:3618`):

```cpp
case PROJECTOR_TYPE_STEP3VL:
    int x_patch = img->nx() / (params.patch_size * params.n_merge);  // /0
```

Windows VEH (LM Studio 2.28.2 mtmd.dll): `[VEH] exception 0xC0000094 ... module=mtmd.dll rva=9A22C` during tokenize. Control with scale_factor=4: tokenize + encode all return 0.

Related: same-root-cause unchecked n_merge divisions exist in hunyuanvl (`clip.cpp:3736`, `hunyuanvl.cpp:36`) and minimax_m3, but in b10252 those are intercepted earlier by preprocessor/graph asserts — Step3VL is the only clean path to the native SIGFPE.

### Expected behavior

Reject `n_merge <= 0` at load (as 6fed9f6f does). Downstream builds on pre-6fed9f6f commits crash on a single image message after loading a malicious mmproj.

### Other

Generator `gen_mmproj_step3.py` available on request.

items.body:
## Router per-model config

This PR implements INI-based per-model configuration for llama-server router mode, as discussed in #17850.

### Summary

Advanced users can define custom configurations using an .ini file. Each model can have its own preset with custom parameters while inheriting router defaults for unspecified options.

### Motivation

Multi-model inference servers for small/medium teams need declarative configuration with zero operational friction. Operators should be able to set global defaults via router CLI and override specific parameters per model in a simple text file.

### Key Features

1. INI-based presets - Define model-specific configurations in a simple .ini file
2. Three independent model sources - Cached models (LLAMA_CACHE), local GGUF files (--models-dir), and custom-path models (--models-preset via paths defined in INI file)
3. Flexible argument formats - Accepts long args (ctx-size), short args (c), and env vars (LLAMA_ARG_CTX_SIZE) as INI keys
4. Inheritance system - Preset args are merged with router base args before spawning child processes
5. Custom model paths - Define models with absolute paths directly in presets without filesystem scanning

### Usage

```sh
llama-server --models-preset ./presets.ini
```

The router can combine multiple sources:

```sh
llama-server --models-dir ./local-models --models-preset ./custom-configs.ini -ngl 999 -fa
```

### INI Format

Section names define model identifiers. Keys correspond to CLI arguments without leading dashes.

Supported key formats:
- Long form: n-gpu-layer = 123
- Short form: c = 4096
- Env var: LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_RAM = 0

All three formats are equivalent and can be mixed in the same file.

Example presets.ini:

```ini
version = 1

; Preset for cached HuggingFace model
[ggml-org/gemma-3-27b-it-GGUF:Q6_K]
chat-template = chatml
ngl = 123
jinja = on
ctx-size = 131072

; Custom local model with absolute path
[my-custom-model]
m = /absolute/path/to/model.gguf
mmproj = /absolute/path/to/mmproj.gguf
ctx-size = 65536
temp = 0.7
top-p = 0.8

; MoE model with specific settings
[MoE-Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking]
m = /models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-Q6_K.gguf
n-cpu-moe = 30
temp = 0.6
top-p = 0.95
ctx-size = 32768
```

### How Models Are Loaded

The router discovers models from three sources:

1. Cached models - Scanned from LLAMA_CACHE (typically ~/.cache/llama.cpp)
2. Local directory - Scanned from --models-dir (non-recursive, direct children only)
3. Preset definitions - Custom models defined in --models-preset with explicit paths

Model names from presets can match cached or local models to apply custom configurations, or define entirely new models with custom paths.

### Argument Inheritance

When spawning a child process for a model, arguments are merged in this order:

1. Start with preset args from INI (model-specific settings)
2. Add router base args for any missing keys (global defaults from router CLI)
3. Force control args (port, host, alias - always overridden by router)

Priority order (highest to lowest):
- Control args (port, host, alias, model path) - managed by router, cannot be overridden
- Router base args (inherited from router CLI) - fill in missing preset keys
- Preset args (from INI) - model-specific overrides

Control args automatically managed by router:
- --port, --host, --alias
- --api-key
- --model, --mmproj, --hf-repo
- --models-dir, --models-max, --models-preset

If a preset contains control args, they are removed with a warning.

### Changes

New files:
- common/preset.cpp - INI parser using PEG grammar and preset management
- common/preset.h - Preset structures and API

Modified files:
- common/arg.cpp/h - Added common_params_parse() for map output, is_truthy/is_falsey/is_autoy utilities
- common/common.h - Added models_preset parameter
- common/CMakeLists.txt - Added preset.cpp/h to build
- tools/server/server-models.cpp/h - Integrated preset system with model loading and spawning
- tools/server/README.md - Added preset documentation and examples

### Technical Details

INI parsing:
- Uses existing PEG parser from common/peg-parser.h (grammar by @aldehir)
- Line-oriented parsing handles comments, blank lines, and standard INI sections
- Whitespace and inline comments properly handled

Argument mapping:
- Three key formats (long, short, env) all map to same common_arg via lookup table
- Deduplication handled automatically (short -c and long --ctx-size are the same arg)

Child process spawning:
- Child servers listen on 127.0.0.1 (not inherited hostname) to avoid conflicts when router runs on 0.0.0.0
- Arguments passed as CLI args (not environment variables)
- Router port exported as LLAMA_SERVER_ROUTER_PORT env var for child processes

### Use Case Example

Development team runs inference server with multiple models:

```sh
llama-server --port 8082 -ngl 999 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on --mlock -np 4 -kvu --jinja --models-preset config.ini

# You can combine --models-preset with :
# --models-max N         for router server, maximum number of models to load simultaneously
# --models-dir PATH      directory containing models for the router server (default: disabled)
```

The presets.ini file defines per-model overrides:

```ini
; Minimal setup
[MyModel]
m = /path/to/model.gguf ; or relative path from current working directory

; For this model we want precise sampling parameters and more context
[MoE-Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct]
m = /path/to/unsloth/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Q6_K.gguf
temp = 0.7
top-p = 0.8
top-k = 20
ctx-size = 131072

; Disable flash attention for this model
[Problematic-model]
m = /path/to/problematic-Q8_0.gguf
fa = off

; Large MoE models don't fit in VRAM, so we use n-cpu-moe = 18
[MoE-Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct]
m = /path/to/unsloth/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-GGUF/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf
n-cpu-moe = 18
ctx-size = 32768
```

Global defaults (-ngl 999 -fa -ctk q8_0 etc.) apply to all models, but each preset can override

Hybrid KDA (linear) + MLA (full) attention as in Kimi-Linear-48B, plus five things that architecture does not have:

  2. latent MoE                      (routed experts run at n_expert_latent)

  4. MLA output gate                 (sigmoid gate before o_proj)
  5. full-rank KDA gate              (single ssm_g instead of ssm_g_a/ssm_g_b)

items.body:
## Overview

With CCCL >= 3.2, top-k processes multi-row inputs with one sequential DeviceTopK dispatch per row. This is ok for a few rows and is even optimal for single row or large ncols cases, but for batch workloads it serializes thousands of dispatches per graph. More specifically MiniMax M3's block selection calls top-k with HD * n_tokens rows, causing a massive prompt processing regression (1250 - 77 t/s on 3 * RTX 6000s  https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26297#issuecomment-5146180851 vs https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26297#issuecomment-5146982417. ) for anyone on CUDA toolkit >= 13.2 or with the official release binaries.

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

## Additional information

This PR keeps the per row DeviceTopK path for nrows <= 16, and routes larger row counts to the existing batched argsort + copy path. (behaviour for CCCL < 3.2 is unchanged). Also routes stream capture to the argsort path, which has explicit capture handling, since DeviceTopK's support is not verified. I can drop that if it is known safe.

Long term the proper fix is DeviceSegmentedTopK when CCCL implements it.

items.body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->
Adds support for MiniMax-M3, a 60-layer / 128-expert MoE (3 dense + 57 MoE layers) using MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA): a GQA block-sparse attention where a lightweight per-GQA-group indexer scores the visible causal context, max-pools the scores into 128-token key blocks, and selects the top-16 blocks (the query's local block is always force-included). The main attention then runs only over the selected blocks (16*128 = 2048 KV per query), independent of context length, so decode attention cost stops scaling with context.

Implements the architecture from the MSA paper (arXiv:2606.13392v2) and follows the transformers reference (modular_minimax_m3_vl) for the indexer construction, selection semantics, and RoPE. MTP heads are not present in the released weights. Vision support is a separate PR (#25113).

Note that MSA is not an optional speed optimization, as the model is trained with sparse attention, so block selection is part of the model's semantics. Running dense attention is an out-of-distribution approximation that degrades output quality. The dense path exists only as a fallback for configurations that can't run MSA.

## Additional information

<!-- You can provide more details and link related discussions here. Delete this section if not applicable -->

### Implementation
Batch and decode implement the same block-scoring and selection semantics, block scores bs = maxpool_128(idx_q*idx_k^T + causal mask) plus a host-provided local-force bias (large positive bias on each query's local block), ranked together for top-k. Selection is per GQA group (4 indexer heads, one per group, shared across the group's 16 query heads).

Within each stream, the four GQA groups are mapped onto the FA mask's ne[3] broadcast dimension and executed in one grouped flash-attention call.

- Batch (n_tokens_per_stream > 1, ie. prefill): a small CPU op turns block scores into a block-level 0/-inf mask, then the token-level expansion and combination with the causal mask happens on the GPU, and masked FA runs over the full cache views.

- Decode (1 token per stream): batched top_k on the GPU, index arithmetic expands block ids to flat (token, kv-head) row ids, one ggml_get_rows each gathers the selected K/V/mask, and FA runs over just the 2048 gathered tokens. 

Multi-stream (--parallel N) is supported whenever the KV cache is per-sequence (so kv_unified is false). In that configuration each stream's slots are then position-aligned, which MSA's slot-anchored block selection requires. 

The indexer also needs its own per-layer key cache. It is allocated F32 on the same backend buffer as the main K/V cache. Context-shift is not supported, since shifting would desynchronize the index cache.

### Requirements and fallbacks

- Flash attention required. Both batch and decode call ggml_flash_attn_ext directly and assume the non-transposed V layout that llama.cpp only provides with FA on. FA off uses dense build_attn (no sparsity) with a one-time warning that output quality may be degraded. 

- Unified KV cache with multiple sequences (--kv-unified + -np > 1) would silently break block anchoring so it also falls back to dense with a one-time warning. 

### Limitations

- Block selection is anchored to absolute KV slots. Erasing a prefix or middle of a sequence's history (llama_memory_seq_rm of a partial range) breaks selection silently. Removing whole sequences, trimming the suffix and reusing server slots is fine.
 
- Main KV cache: F16/BF16 are tested. Quantized KV-cache types are not yet validated.

### Quantization

Quants should keep the indexer projections (index_{q,k}_proj) at high precision(F32 ideally) since they drive block selection, so quant error there changes which blocks are read (a discrete retrieval loss), unlike a value projection. The cost is ~1 GB and these are some of the highest-value tensors in the model.

### Conversion

GGUFs must be converted with this branch and must keep the indexer tensors, weights with the indexers stripped will not work. 

### Performance

My tested config is expert-offload  bound.  MSA decode is essentially flat with context (7.7 tok/s at 5k -> 7.67 at 62k), prefill is roughly ~420-480 tok/s at 62k with -b and -ub 2048. Compute buffer at -ub 2048 / 62k ctx is ~4.6 GiB.

### How to test

As mentioned GGUFs converted with this PR are necessary, other's will fail to load. You can either convert one yourself, or you can use [this](https://huggingface.co/Serpen/Minimax-M3-MSA-GGUF/tree/main/Q4_K_M) Q4KM one (graciously provided by @AesSedai). 

CUDA build assumed (`-DGGML_CUDA=ON`), but in theory other backends with flash_attn_ext support for head-dim 128 should work (dense fallback otherwise), ROCm/HIP, Vulkan, Metal untested, reports welcome.

- Feed a ~4k and a ~30k+ prompt and generate. Decode throughput should stay roughly flat with context (fixed 2048-KV budget).

- Multi-stream: llama-server --parallel 2 (or 4) with concurrent requests of different prompt lengths.

### Credits

The initial MiniMax-M3 scaffolding was based on work by @danielhanchen. The sparse-attention indexer, the unified batch/decode MSA graphs, the KV-cache index handling, FA gating, and multi-stream support in this PR are new work.

## Requirements

### Name and Version

version: 716 (10e9780)
built with cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04) 13.3.0 for x86_64-linux-gnu


### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m ./model/with/4096context -c 16384 --rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

The llama-server does not allow using the extended context. Server output announces the context length is capped

> the slot context (%d) exceeds the training context of the model (%d) - capping\n

This is not aware of RoPE settings or other user configurations which would allow for longer context. Disabling this check in llama-server introduced in cd5e3b57 allowed me to use longer context via the RoPE settings.

This "capping" forces the model to load with 4,096 tokens of context and causes my long-context queries to fail.

Please allow us to override this cap. For users who don't know what they are doing, sure, it's probably helpful, but for advanced users there should be a way to disable it.

### First Bad Commit

cd5e3b57

### Relevant log output

```shell
the slot context (%d) exceeds the training context of the model (%d) - capping\n
```

## Overview Based on @pwilkin's ideas in #27493, I finally managed to get coopmat1 int8 to work with good performance on RDNA3 and 4. This new MMQ cm1 shader supports q4_0, q4_1, q5_0, q5_1, q8_0, q3_k, q4_k, q5_k, q6_k, mxfp4, nvfp4 and iq4_nl on RDNA3 and RDNA4. Strix Halo prompt processing performance is significantly improved, RDNA4 is more neutral, but MoE prompt processing is also up significantly. The shader is limited to those two architectures since it hardcodes their specific coopmat access patterns. More architectures can be added if needed. q4_1, q5_1, q4_k, q5_k and nvfp4 on RDNA4 are disabled for MUL_MAT since they run slower than existing fp16 matmul. items.body:
**Summary:** With an external DFlash draft model attached, llama-server produces *different outputs* than the no-drafter baseline at temperature 0 — violating the core speculative-decoding invariant (draft tokens must be verified against the target; greedy outputs must be identical).

**Repro** (AMD Strix Halo / gfx1151, ROCm, Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf + official dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf drafter, GSM8K 5-shot, 60 questions, strict integer grading, identical prompts):

| Config | Accuracy | Battery wall |
|---|---|---|
| no drafter (baseline) | **93.33%** (56/60) | 109 min |
| drafter, -md only | 85.00% (51/60) | ~70 min |
| drafter, -md + -ngld 99 (official recipe flags) | **61.67%** (37/60) | 53 min |
| drafter on a different build lineage (local fork with custom spec patches) | 68.33% (41/60) | 64 min |

Quality degrades monotonically as drafter engagement increases, while speed rises ~2x — the classic signature of verification not being enforced on drafted tokens.

**Control:** the same battery against a target running a *different* spec-dec configuration (MTP + ngram, no external drafter) shows NO degradation (96.67%) — the corruption is specific to the external-dflash-drafter path, not speculative decoding generally.

**Expected:** accuracy at temp 0 must be identical with and without the drafter. Any delta = verification bug.

Environment: b10353+ lineage builds (two independent builds tested); temp 0; 5-shot GSM8K; per-item results and raw server logs available on request.
items.title: spec-dec: external DFlash drafter changes outputs at temperature 0 (verified spec-dec invariant violated) — Muse Glimmer 30B

items.body:
## Environment

- llama.cpp: upstream master as of 2026-08-26 (build **b10643**), self-built Release / CUDA sm_86. The only local patches are unrelated GGML kernel optimizations; `common/chat.cpp` and the server chat pipeline are vanilla.
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M GGUF with embedded official jinja template (+mmproj)
- Server flags: `-c 120000 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 --split-mode layer -ts 1,1,1 --spec-type draft-mtp --tools all` (jinja default on)
- Client: OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, streaming, `tool_choice: auto`, ~33 tools (agentic CLI workload)

## Observed

Episodically (~2×/day under heavy agent use) a slot finishes a long generation normally and then the request dies:

```
I slot print_timing: id 3 | task 0 | eval time = 515042.58 ms / 11708 tokens
I slot print_timing: id 3 | task 0 | draft acceptance = 0.52296 (7151 accepted / 13674 generated)
I slot      release: id 3 | task 0 | stop processing: n_tokens = 37979, truncated = 0
W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: <think>
W srv          stop: cancel task, id_task = 0
```

Note that `common_chat_peg_parse()` logs `effective_input.substr(result.end)` — i.e. **only the unconsumed tail**. In both captured occurrences that tail was literally `<think>\n` (8 bytes).

## Analysis

The model produced a fully valid turn — reasoning + content + one or more well-formed `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` blocks that match the per-request grammar — and then emitted a stray opening `<think>` immediately before stopping. Since the lazy grammar necessarily releases around/between tool calls, a few free tokens can land there; generation then stops (EOS / `n_predict`) leaving an unclosed tag behind.

The strict final parse (non-partial `common_chat_peg_parse()`) fails on that tail and throws:

```
The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format
```

…which makes the server cancel the task, so the client loses the entire already-generated response (~11.7k tokens here) purely because of 8 bytes of trailing garbage.

## Suggested remedies

Any of the following would remove the user-visible failure:

1. Make the autoparser's tool-call root tolerate trailing garbage after the last complete call (e.g. optional untagged `rest()` before end).
2. In `common_chat_peg_parse()` for non-partial input: before failing, retry the parse truncated right after the last complete `</tool_call>`; if it succeeds, return the structured message.
3. At minimum, don't throw on a *final* parse mismatch — degrade to raw-content passthrough instead of canceling the task.

We are running (2)+(3) locally with good results and would be happy to prepare a PR if this direction is acceptable.

## Related

- #27720 — gpt-oss malformed Harmony channel header fails the final PEG parse and errors the turn
- #27279 — peg-native + `response_format.json_schema`: parse throws → 500
- #27025 — same error string, Muse Glimmer tool calls
items.title: [server] final peg-native parse failure on trailing "<think>" tail discards an entire completed generation (Qwen3.8)

### Name and Version

version: b10349 (62bf73d25, includes the #26841 merge)
Built from source (CUDA, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86;120`) in a local Docker image.
Hardware: RTX 3090 + RTX 5060 Ti.

### Operating systems

Linux (Docker container on a Windows host)

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Models

- **Target (FAILS):** [meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF) → `muse-glimmer-30B-kquant-dynamic.gguf`
- **Draft:** same repo → `dflash-kquant.gguf`
- **Target (WORKS):** [unsloth/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF) with the exact same drafter

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Binding the DFlash drafter (`--spec-type draft-dflash`) crashes at load time when the **target** GGUF encodes `muse-glimmer.attention.sliding_window_pattern` as an **array**, which is how the model creator's own official GGUF (`meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF`) encodes it:

```
llama-server -m muse-glimmer-30B-kquant-dynamic.gguf \
    -md dflash-kquant.gguf --spec-type draft-dflash -fa on --jinja
```

crashes with:

```
vector::_M_range_check: __n (which is 1) >= this->size() (which is 1)
```

The exact same drafter file binds and runs fine when the target is the unsloth conversion of the same model, whose `muse-glimmer.attention.sliding_window_pattern` is encoded as a **scalar** (`UINT32 = 4`).

Both target GGUFs load and generate fine **without** the drafter — `src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp` accepts both encodings (scalar period → `set_swa_pattern()`, array → per-layer `is_swa_impl`). The crash only happens on the DFlash bind path, which inherits the target's config and apparently only handles the scalar form. Note the irony: the model creator's official GGUF is the one that cannot bind the official drafter shipped in the same repo, while a third-party conversion can.

**Validated workaround:** copying the target GGUF with gguf-py `copy_with_new_metadata`, rewriting `muse-glimmer.attention.sliding_window_pattern` to scalar `UINT32 = 4`. With that single metadata change the drafter binds and runs (~137 t/s on the RTX 3090).

**Suggested fix:** when the DFlash path inherits the target's config, accept both encodings of `<arch>.attention.sliding_window_pattern`, mirroring what `src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp` already does at target load. Possibly related: the scalar overload `llama_model_loader::get_key_or_arr(enum llm_kv, uint32_t &, bool)` in `src/llama-model-loader.cpp` returns `false` (non-required) or throws when the key is an array, so any call site expecting a scalar silently takes the wrong branch on array-encoded GGUFs.

### First Bad Commit

Not bisected — observed on b10349 (62bf73d25). Possibly present since the DFlash path landed.

### Relevant log output

```
vector::_M_range_check: __n (which is 1) >= this->size() (which is 1)
```
items.title: Eval bug: DFlash drafter fails to bind (vector::_M_range_check) when target GGUF encodes attention.sliding_window_pattern as an array — Muse-Glimmer-30B official GGUF

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> GGUF generated before Aug 27th 2026 must be reconverted, otherwise vision will be broken. See: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27342#issuecomment-5399098880

## Overview

DFlash2 adds two more modules compared to DFlash, grouped dynamic depthwise convolution and candidate selector. 

The formula is for reference. `out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`. `base` is the static kernel, `δ` is the dynamic part predicted from the input.`x` is divided into groups `g(c)` and `δ` is shared across a group. Another one is `edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`. `A`/`B` are the codebooks for the predecessor and the candidate. This position's hidden is projected by `project(h)`to the same rank to multiply `A`. And `unary[c]` is the draft's own score for `c`.  

DFlash2 is enabled when the checkpoint is DFlash2; no need to use extra flag.

We evaled `Qwen3.8-27B` at `Q4_K_M`on Apple M5 Pro 64 GB. And the test data is first 8 problems of GSM8K.
Concurrency is set to 1 and temperature is 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20. We use default `xhigh` reasoning and set
2,048 maximum new tokens.

| Method | Draft quant | Block | Decode TPS | Decode speedup | Acceptance | Normal stops |
|--------|------|--:|------:|------:|-----:|---|
| Autoregressive | — | — | 10.42 | 1.00× | — | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | BF16 | 8 | 19.31 | 1.85× | 4.92 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q8_0 | 8 | 18.43 | 1.77× | 5.08 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q4_K_M | 8 | 18.89 | 1.81× | 5.03 | 8/8 |

## Overview

I found that by tuning `rm_kq_int` and `rm_stdq_int` I'm able to get better performance for batch sizes 5-8 (mostly in that range, some operations get improvements on smaller batch sizes as well) on Strix Halo.

## Additional information

This is my first attempt at this kind of tuning, so it's certainly possible that I've done something wrong. I've tried to be as rigorous as possible in my testing and attach my findings here.

I investigated if `rm_int_n` could be a function of the batch size, but it appears to be a shoulder between n=4 and n=5, at least on this hardware. It seems to me like even more performance could be squeezed out by tuning on a per type basis, but that would require some kind of pattern/infrastructure for that.

I have gated these changes on `device->vendor_id == VK_VENDOR_ID_AMD && device->architecture == AMD_RDNA3` so it should not impact GPUs from other vendors/other generations of AMD GPUs. I only have a Strix Halo machine to test on though, so I can't say if these improvements hold up on other RDNA3 cards. ### Name and Version

version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10438, commit 9d57ce456)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64

Also reproduced on master (b94041a), built for macOS arm64.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell SFF (SM120)
Apple M3 Max

### Models

https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Muse-Glimmer-30B-NVFP4, converted with `convert_hf_to_gguf.py --outtype q8_0`

The converted GGUF: https://huggingface.co/gabrielcosi/Muse-Glimmer-30B-NVFP4-GGUF


### Problem description & steps to reproduce

A compressed-tensors NVFP4 Muse Glimmer checkpoint converts to a GGUF that does not load. Past the load error, the model runs but returns the same token for every prompt.

K-quant conversions of the same model work. Only the NVFP4 path is affected.

Three things go wrong.

**1. The QK-norm tensors are missing.** [`_generate_nvfp4_tensors`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b94041a/conversion/base.py#L800-L802) removes quantized tensors from `model_tensors`, so `modify_tensors` never sees them. Muse Glimmer carries no QK-norm weights of its own, so [`MuseGlimmerModel.modify_tensors`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b94041a/conversion/muse_glimmer.py#L65) synthesizes `attn_q_norm` and `attn_k_norm` there. It keys on `self_attn.q_proj.weight`, which is quantized and already removed. The tensors are never written and the load fails.

**2. Q and K keep the transformers layout.** The same bypass skips [`_unpermute_for_rope`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b94041a/conversion/muse_glimmer.py#L58-L61) on `q_proj` and `k_proj`.

**3. Most NVFP4 scales are ignored.** [`build_lora_mm`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b94041a/src/llama-graph.cpp#L1493) applies the per-tensor scale only when the caller passes it. The muse-glimmer graph passes it for `wo` ([L142](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b94041a/src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp#L142)) and `output` ([L190](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b94041a/src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp#L190)) only. `attn_gate` ([L107](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b94041a/src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp#L107)) and the three FFN projections ([L163-L168](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b94041a/src/models/muse-glimmer.cpp#L163-L168)) pass `NULL`, so those weights run unscaled. The scales are around 4e-5. `qwen3.cpp` passes all three FFN scales.

Steps to reproduce items 1 and 2:

1. Download `RedHatAI/Muse-Glimmer-30B-NVFP4`.
2. Run `python convert_hf_to_gguf.py <dir> --outtype q8_0`. This needs `transformers>=5`, because the model ships `tokenizer_class: TokenizersBackend`.
3. Run `llama-server -m <gguf>`. The load fails with the error below.

To see item 3 on a stock build, download the GGUF linked above. I converted it with items 1 and 2 fixed ([9ec0ea1](https://github.com/gabrielcosi/llama.cpp/commit/9ec0ea187ea86390cf6a480ea6db156894850c18)), so it loads on an unpatched build. Every prompt then returns one repeated token.

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>
<!-- Copy-pasted short logs go into the "console" area here -->

```console
check_tensor_dims: tensor 'blk.0.attn_q_norm.weight' not found
llama_model_load_from_file_impl: failed to load model
common_init_: failed to load model 'muse-nvfp4.gguf'

# Running the linked GGUF, with `--temp 0`:

CUDA:  "The capital of France is" -> "22222222222222222222"
CUDA:  "1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6,"        -> "22222222222222222222"
CPU:   "The capital of France is" -> "33333333333333333333"
CPU:   "1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6,"        -> "33333333333333333333"

```
</details>

## Overview

Issue #27194
- Fuses UNARY(GELU|SIGMOID|SILU|SOFTPLUS)+MUL on Vulkan, matching CUDA's unary_mul
- Review-driven additions:
  - GELU support (gemma4/gemma3n per-layer gating)
  - shape check via standard `ggml_can_repeat`
  - fusion of pairs separated by zero-compute nodes (graph_optimize)
  - OP-on-B support (`ffn_shexp * sigmoid(gate)`, qwen3next/qwen35moe shared-expert gating)

## Additional information

### Design:
- Fusion lives in unary.comp behind UNARY_MUL_FUSION. Specialized pipelines per
  op/dtype, repeat + norepeat variants selected by shape equality. Kernel
  scheduled like mul.comp (256 threads x 2 iterations); writes the MUL dst
  directly, never materializing the unary intermediate.
- Shape gating uses the standard `ggml_can_repeat` broadcast check (admits non-1
  repeat factors, matching ggml and CUDA reference semantics).
- Both operand slots supported:
  - unary as src0: other must repeat against it (`ggml_can_repeat(other, unary)`)
  - unary as src1 (OP-on-B, e.g. qwen shared-expert gating `ffn_shexp * sigmoid(gate)`):
    the unary result must tile into mul->src[0]; a UNARY_MUL_B variant iterates over
    mul's extent and applies the OP to the fastmod-indexed B operand. A backend-local
    pair check (`ggml_can_fuse_subgraph` + Vulkan shape rules) replaces the generic
    same-shape requirement of `ggml_can_fuse` for this pattern. The OP-on-B choice is
    a `op_on_b` specialization constant on the *existing* unary-mul SPIR-V — no
    separate _mul_b shaders — selected via two-entry `{norepeat, op_on_b}` lists,
    mirroring how `norepeat` already works.
- graph_optimize: a consuming MUL may now join its in-set UNARY across a gap of
  unscheduled zero-compute nodes (NONE/VIEW/RESHAPE/TRANSPOSE/PERMUTE). The
  mechanism is a scoped strict-adjacency extension of the existing UNARY->MUL
  blessed pair; in practice GEMMA-3n's per-layer views fall into an earlier
  window's scan range and land ahead of the UNARY, after which strict adjacency
  suffices. Pipelines are stored in a lookup table
  `pipeline_unary_mul[4][2][2][2]` ([op][f16][norepeat][op_on_b]) replacing the
  four nested selection switches.

### Tests:
- Fused ops: 104/104 layouts
  (packed/padded/halves/broadcast/non-1-repeat/view-separated/OP-on-B gate gate
   x gelu/sigmoid/silu/softplus x f32/f16)
- Plain ops: MUL 91/91
- 16957 tests, all backends OK (up from 16935 at the time of the original PR).
- Dispatch-path verified on debug builds (grep `*_mul_f32/_mul_b_f32` descriptor
  requests) and via the sched-driven probe covering adjacent, view-separated,
  reshape-separated, and OP-on-B-broadcast graphs.
- Token-identical vs base build (`4df29be4f`) at temp 0 / seed 42 on Qwen3-8B,
  Gemma-3n-E4B, gemma4-12B, and Muse-Glimmer-30B.
- Hardware: AMD Radeon 8050S Graphics (RADV STRIX_HALO), uma.

```
./build/bin/test-backend-ops -b Vulkan0 -p "layout="      # 104/104 OK (fused unary+mul matrix)
./build/bin/test-backend-ops -b Vulkan0 -o MUL            # 91/91 OK
./build/bin/test-backend-ops                              # 16957/16957 OK
```

### Model results (interleaved same-session A/B vs pre-PR base)

Fusion sites confirmed via dispatch logs:
```
model (fused path)                        correctness   pp2048              tg256
Qwen3-8B (none fire)                     identical     parity              parity
Gemma-3n-E4B (GELU_MUL, 841/pass)         identical     +21.7%              +12.1%
Muse-Glimmer-30B (SIGMOID_MUL, 469/pass)  identical     +16.0%              +1.5%
gemma-4-12B (none fire)                 identical     parity (noisy)     parity (noisy)
```

items.body:
### Summary

`--spec-type draft-dflash` works well at low concurrency, but under concurrent slots the **draft model's predictions get corrupted**, draft acceptance collapses, and throughput goes into reverse (slower than no speculation). We traced this on an AMD gfx1151 APU across two ROCm versions and pinned down that the corruption **scales with the number of concurrently-drafting sequences, not with batch token count, server slot count, or draft length alone**:

| server `-np` | active requests | `--spec-draft-n-max` | noise-block batch | per-slot draft acceptance | aggregate throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 4 | 15 | 64 tok | **0.51 – 0.66** (healthy) | healthy |
| **16** | **4** | 15 | 64 tok | **0.51 – 0.66** (bit-identical to the row above, same seed) | healthy |
| 8 | 8 | 15 | 128 tok | 0.11 – 0.46 (degraded) | degraded |
| 16 | 16 | 7 | 128 tok | 0.22 – 0.74 (bimodal) | bad |
| 16 | 16 | 15 | 256 tok | **0.06 – 0.49** (bimodal; sustained load collapses to **0.0018**) | ~17–21 tok/s vs **37 tok/s** no-spec baseline |
| 16 | 16 | **1** | 32 tok | **0.83 – 0.92** | **~80 tok/s (2.2× the no-spec baseline)** |

Key observations that localize the defect:

1. **Per-slot corruption is established during prefill and persists for the request's lifetime.** 16 *identical* requests (same prompt, seed, temperature) produce an ~8× spread in acceptance across slots, visible from the very first speculative tick. The draft model's top-1 confidence is bimodal per slot: median 0.25 on "broken" slots vs 0.92–0.98 on "healthy" ones.
2. **It is not the server's slot configuration** — a `-np 16` server with only 4 in-flight requests produces bit-identical results to a `-np 4` server.
3. **It is not the drafter's intrinsic quality** — with `--spec-draft-n-max 1` the same 16-way load accepts 83–92 % of drafts and beats the no-spec baseline by 2.2×.
4. **It is not a ROCm-version regression** — identical pathology on ROCm 7.2.1 and 7.14.0 (we cannot test CUDA here; see "ask" at the end).

### Git commit

- Verified at `0b1bad14ff204627636aeb1de22ddcd5acb859d4` (2026-08-11).
- **Still reproduces on current master `0177dcc7300bad8914bb838baabce87899812491` (2026-08-15, freshly built)**: 16 identical concurrent requests → the same bimodal per-slot acceptance (0.05–0.50, broken slots waste 500–977 drafts per 160-token request); the 4-concurrent control on the same server recovers (0.19–0.61). The numbers below are from the pinned build.

Build: `-DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DROCM_PATH=…` (Release, GCC 13.3, `GGML_HIP_GRAPHS=ON` default).

Hardware/runtime: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S iGPU (gfx1151, 96 GB unified), kernel 6.17, ROCm 7.14.0 (side-by-side 7.2.1 with identical results).

Models: Muse-Glimmer-30B target (Q4_K "kquant" GGUF, ~17 GB, all layers on GPU) + the matching DFlash draft GGUF (`general.architecture = dflash`, 5 layers, `block_size=16`, 5 extracted target layers). Any supported dense target + DFlash pair should reproduce the concurrency dependence.

### Command line

```bash
llama-server -m muse-glimmer-30B-kquant-17gb.gguf -ngl 999 \
  -np 16 -c 131072 --jinja \
  -md dflash-kquant.gguf -ngld 99 \
  --spec-type draft-dflash --spec-draft-n-max 15 \
  --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 64 --seed 42 \
  --port 8080 > server.log 2>&1
```

Reproduce (the server log is the instrument — `/metrics` spec counters stay 0 on these builds):

```bash
# 16 identical concurrent streaming requests
seq 16 | xargs -P16 -I{} curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain in detail why the sky is blue."}],
       "max_tokens":160,"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95,"top_k":64,"seed":42}' >/dev/null

grep 'draft acceptance' server.log
```

Controls (each on a fresh server):

- `-P4` instead of `-P16` (same `-np 16` server) → acceptance recovers to ~0.5–0.66.
- `--spec-draft-n-max 1` with `-P16` → acceptance 0.83–0.92, ~2.2× no-spec throughput.
- `-np 4` server, `-P4` → bit-identical to the `-np 16`/`-P4` run (same seed).

### Problem description & logs

Expected: draft acceptance roughly constant w.r.t. concurrency (speculative decoding is lossless; batching drafts from many sequences should not change per-sequence predictions), and DFlash at `-np 16` to at least not be slower than no speculation.

Actual (16 identical concurrent requests, fresh server, `0b1bad1`):

```
slot print_timing: id  1 | draft acceptance = 0.05333 (    4 accepted /    75 generated), mean len =  1.80
slot print_timing: id  7 | draft acceptance = 0.25424 (   45 accepted /   177 generated), mean len =  3.50
slot print_timing: id 10 | draft acceptance = 0.49074 (   53 accepted /   108 generated), mean len =  6.89
slot print_timing: id 12 | draft acceptance = 0.19048 (   44 accepted /   231 generated), mean len =  3.44
slot print_timing: id  0 | draft acceptance = 0.07289 (   32 accepted /   439 generated), mean len =  2.03
...
spec statistics: draft-dflash: #calls(b,g,a) = 16 31 294, #gen tokens = 3758, #acc tokens = 509,
                #mean acc len = 2.73, dur(b,g,a) = 0.020, 4133.404, 0.072 ms
```

Under sustained long-generation load this collapses completely — a 16×512, 5-rep run on ROCm 7.2.1 was aborted after 5 h 16 min with **3,270,000 drafted / 6,060 accepted (0.18 %)**.

Secondary symptoms at `-np 16` (measured on the same runs):

- Prompt processing with DFlash injection runs at ~57 ms/token (~17.5 tok/s) vs ~23 ms/token (~43 tok/s) without DFlash at the same `-np` — the per-sequence sequential `llama_encode` + inject `llama_decode` in `process()` is paid once per sequence per batch.
- Steady-state speculative tick is 1.15–1.5 s; `draft()` alone averages 133 ms per call (256-token noise block); per-token time grows ~3× over a 320-token request (207 → 570 ms/token), i.e. it decays as generations lengthen.
- The HIP backend logs `CUDA graph warmup reset` 1–2× per tick (54–194 per run) as batch composition chang

## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

Enables Muse-Glimmer for OpenVINO backend.

- Added New Op Support: GGML_UNARY_OP_SIGMOID, GGML_OP_ARGMAX
- Decline bf16 `GET_ROWS` on GPU
- Classify sliding-window vs full-attention layers from the per-layer KV cache extent.
- Accuracy improvement: Keep the RoPE angle in f32 under the f16 inference hint.
- Honour `GGML_TENSOR_FLAG_OUTPUT` in `compute_model_outputs()`, which previously used only
  use-count analysis and so dropped tensors that the host reads back.
- Refresh the decoder IO when the cgraph instance changes, and invalidate a cached graph when its
  output set changes.
- Keep the token dimension dynamic for a 2-D activation graph input, plus three dynamic-dim
  propagation gaps (shape-preserving `VIEW`, `CONCAT`, `SSM_CONV`/`GATED_DELTA_NET`).
- Tolerate graph inputs and outputs with no backing storage instead of constructing an `ov::Tensor`
  over a null pointer.
- `GGML_OPENVINO_REDUCE_COMPILE_MEM`: stream requantization in row chunks instead of
  materializing one full F32 array.
- `GGML_OPENVINO_REQUANT_KQUANT`: optionaly choose a 4-bit requant target
  (`q4_sym128`/`q4_asym64`[`_all`]/`native`) instead of inflating Q6_K/Q5_K to Q8_0.
- `GGML_OPENVINO_RELEASE_WEIGHTS` — drop host weight pages after the GPU plugin has its own copy.
  Single model per process; two guards abort loudly rather than read dropped pages.
- `GGML_OPENVINO_SPILL_DIR` — back the repacked weight buffer with an unlinked file so the pages
  are reclaimable.

## Overview

Adds a standard Prometheus histogram metric `llamacpp:request_context_tokens` to the `/metrics` endpoint, recording the distribution of context sizes (in tokens) across completed requests. Closes #27011.

Changes:

- New `--metrics-ctx-buckets B1,B2,...` CLI flag to configure bucket boundaries (default: `1024,4096,8192,16384,32768,65536,131072,262144`; env: `LLAMA_ARG_METRICS_CTX_BUCKETS`)
- Histogram fields and recording logic on `server_metrics` in `server-common.h`
- Prometheus output in `server_task_result_metrics::to_metrics()`, labeled with `model_name` and `model_alias`
- Only emitted when `--metrics` is enabled (existing gate)

Example output:

```

## Overview This PR improves routed MoE prefill performance on RDNA3 by changing how llama.cpp chooses MMQ N-tile sizes. Instead of using the worst case expert width, it estimates the typical routed expert width and uses that when it is smaller than the RDNA3 maximum tile width. The launch grid still uses the original worst case width, so output coverage and correctness are preserved. The change is limited to host side tile selection in `mul_mat_q_case` and does not modify structs, call sites, launch parameters, or device kernels. Benchmarks on a Radeon Pro W7800/gfx1100 with ROCm 7.2.3 show large prefill gains in many routed MoE cases, while decode and non RDNA3 architectures are mostly unchanged. If maintainers or other contributors have access to NVIDIA, CDNA, RDNA2, or RDNA4 hardware, the natural follow up would be to test the same routed width picker under the corresponding MMQ/launch policy and enable it per architecture where it is beneficial. ## Benchmark Summary Hardware/software: - AMD Radeon Pro W7800, gfx1100 / RDNA3 - ROCm 7.2.3 - HIP backend, `-ngl 99` - `GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON` - `-fa 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv f16 -sm none -t 4 --poll 0 -r 5` The improvement depends on the physical ubatch/chunk width that reaches routed MoE MMQ, not total context length: ```text win when: ncols_typical < mmq_x_max crossover_ubatch: 128 * n_experts / n_expert_used ``` So long prompts can still benefit when they are processed in smaller ubatch chunks.

### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description


This is a continuation of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26622. The PR was simple, this might be more complex. 

I would like to propose performance improvements for `--n-cpu-ffn` by automating `--override-tensor` band selection. It is possible to do this by hand, but this makes the process much easier. Currently `--n-cpu-ffn` selects sequentially from layer 0. 

My idea would be to create `--n-cpu-mode` with modes being:
* "largest" - pick layers with the largest FFNs;
* "top" - start from the top layer sequentially going down;
* "bottom" - current default, start from 0 sequentially;
* "smallest" - opposite of largest; 

"largest", "smallest", and "top" should exclude the MTP layer(s) (`nextn_predict_layers`): they return the least performance per byte. Anyone who wants the MTP layer on the CPU too could use mode "bottom" with a large N.

"largest" provides the most performance for me because the cost is per layer, not per byte. I would make it the default (instead of the current "bottom"), because at the same N it offloads more bytes, so existing setups would end up with some free VRAM while speed barely changes, which is harmless. Other options, like "smallest", might be useful for someone else using other quants.

I also tested `--n-cpu-moe` on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: its experts are all the same size, so `largest` does nothing there, but `top` gained ~3% with MTP on (average of prose and code). I don't know why, and the gain is small, so it doesn't matter much.

Most performance improvements happen when using MTP. All MTP runs used `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1`, because with MTP + CPU offload the CUDA graphs get re-captured every step (no measured speedup) and the recapture can OOM at a tight VRAM margin. Output is identical either way.

### Motivation

I created `--n-cpu-ffn` because driving `--override-tensor` needs more technical knowledge, thus it is not as widely used as a simplification like `--n-cpu-moe`. For those seeking the best performance out of their setup a `--n-cpu-mode` would help a lot by simplifying layer counting, which is unique to each quant.

**Here are some benchmarks showing the gains:**

MTP acceptance differs while generating prose and code. For simplicity I merged the two numbers:

```
MTP_tg = (prose_tg + code_tg) / 2
```

The speeds were tested at context prefill of 50k.

MTP costs VRAM, so the `-ot` band size differs when using it to keep a consistent VRAM usage amount. If you don't compensate for MTP's VRAM usage then the results are more exaggerated.

I tried to keep the CPU layer sizes similar between 'modes' and quants (that is why they have similar tg speeds).

Model: Qwen3.8-27B (Unsloth UD3 quants below).

HW: RTX 4070 Ti Super 16 GB; 32 GB DDR5; i5-13600KF;

Version: build 10280 (`0345d3a18`)

(The current `--n-cpu-ffn` implementation equates to using mode "bottom")

#### UD-Q4_K_S

**MTP on**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 25 | 3847 MiB | **21.7** | 877.7 |
| `smallest` | 31 | 3873 MiB | 15.1 | 872.7 |
| `top` | 25 | 3791 MiB | 21.1 | 881.2 |
| `bottom` | 30 | 3796 MiB | 15.5 | 878.6 |

**MTP off**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 17 | 2734 MiB | **15.8** | 999.2 |
| `smallest` | 23 | 2789 MiB | 13.9 | 987.8 |
| `top` | 18 | 2835 MiB | 15.4 | 986.1 |
| `bottom` | 23 | 2813 MiB | 13.7 | 985.0 |

#### UD-Q4_K_M

**MTP on**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 23 | 3840 MiB | **21.7** | 878.4 |
| `smallest` | 29 | 3860 MiB | 18.7 | 876.4 |
| `top` | 24 | 3813 MiB | 21.7 | 877.1 |
| `bottom` | 28 | 3881 MiB | 18.9 | 869.8 |

**MTP off**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn  | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 16 | 2764 MiB | **15.5** | 992.6 |
| `smallest` | 21 | 2755 MiB | 15.1 | 995.8 |
| `top` | 17 | 2825 MiB | 15.2 | 983.4 |
| `bottom` | 21 | 2790 MiB | 14.9 | 986.4 |


#### UD-Q4_K_XL

**MTP on**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 21 | 3806 MiB | **22.3** | 872.4 |
| `smallest` | 28 | 3878 MiB | 19.6 | 864.3 |
| `top` | 22 | 3806 MiB | 21.9 | 869.0 |
| `bottom` | 26 | 3793 MiB | 20.1 | 868.9 |

**MTP off**

| --n-cpu-mode | --n-cpu-ffn | CPU FFN size | tg | pp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `largest` | 15 | 2754 MiB | **15.2** | 983.8 |
| `smallest` | 21 | 2837 MiB | 14.9 | 973.8 |
| `top` | 15 | 2741 MiB | 15.1 | 980.7 |
| `bottom` | 20 | 2786 MiB | 14.9 | 977.4 |

#### Summary (both sides `largest`)

| model | MTP off tg | MTP on tg | MTP gain | `largest` vs current (MTP on) | `largest` vs current (MTP off) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UD-Q4_K_S | 15.8 | 21.7 | +37% | +40% | +15% |
| UD-Q4_K_M | 15.5 | 21.7 | +40% | +15% | +4% |
| UD-Q4_K_XL | 15.2 | 22.3 | +47% | +11% | +2% |

`largest` wins all six tables, while `top` trails it closely. Though this is Unsloth UD3 specific; older UD2 quants had a different size profile.

Smaller bands prefill ~10-12% faster.

### Possible Implementation

* "largest" and "smallest" need per-layer FFN sizes, but the offload args are resolved before the model is loaded. Where should this live?
* Is `--n-cpu-mode` a good name, and are the four modes OK?
* Can "largest" become the default?
* Should this also apply to `--n-cpu-moe`?

## Overview

Fixes #26220 

After the removal of rocWMMA Flash Attention kernel path, the replacement had slower prompt processing at deep context on RDNA 4. The regression was caused by WMMA tensor cores not being used at all for head dim 256.

This PR widens `flash_attn_ext_f16` device guard to unblock MMA at head dim 256. Without it, the tile kernel is used instead which works, but slows down with more context.  The config table also needed a precision fix for DKQ=256. `nbatch_combine` was too small, causing multi-pass FP16 accumulation errors in test-backend-ops.

Additionally, for DKQ>128 on WMMA K/V is loaded directly from VRAM instead of going through LDS. Without it, MMA is actually slower than the tile kernel.

## Additional information

Below are benchmark numbers to confirm no regressions and the speedup. It's worth to mention that, while prompt processing is faster than current master(a7a6d0d2), it's still about 12-20% slower the old rocWMMA kernel depending on context size. There's definitely room for further improvement.

GPU: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, RDNA4), ROCm 7.2.4

### Name and Version

version: 716 (10e9780)
built with cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04) 13.3.0 for x86_64-linux-gnu


### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m ./model/with/4096context -c 16384 --rope-scaling yarn --rope-scale 4
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

The llama-server does not allow using the extended context. Server output announces the context length is capped

> the slot context (%d) exceeds the training context of the model (%d) - capping\n

This is not aware of RoPE settings or other user configurations which would allow for longer context. Disabling this check in llama-server introduced in cd5e3b57 allowed me to use longer context via the RoPE settings.

This "capping" forces the model to load with 4,096 tokens of context and causes my long-context queries to fail.

Please allow us to override this cap. For users who don't know what they are doing, sure, it's probably helpful, but for advanced users there should be a way to disable it.

### First Bad Commit

cd5e3b57

### Relevant log output

```shell
the slot context (%d) exceeds the training context of the model (%d) - capping\n
```

### Summary

`llama-server` crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` in `ggml_backend_cuda_synchronize` (`cudaStreamSynchronize`, `ggml-cuda.cu:2485` on b10107 / `:2499` on b10243) while processing the **second** request of a specific two-request sequence. The crash is **deterministic** (reproduced 5+ times across two builds) and **disappears with `--flash-attn off`**.

### Environment

- Windows 11 Pro, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 12 GB, driver 610.47
- Builds tested: **b10107** and **b10243** (both `win-cuda-13.3-x64` release binaries, cudart DLLs present, GPU active and verified via VRAM usage ~11.5 GiB)
- Model: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf` (unsloth repo, arch `qwen35moe`, MoE A3B)

### Server args (frozen across all probes unless noted)

```
--ctx-size 32768 --parallel 1 --n-gpu-layers 99 --flash-attn on
--cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --no-mmap --jinja
--batch-size 1024 --ubatch-size 512 --no-context-shift
--override-tensor "blk\.(16|17|...|39)\.ffn_.*_exps\.=CPU"
```
(partial MoE expert offload to CPU: model is 22 GB, VRAM is 12 GB)

### Symptom

First request (RAG-style prompt ~900-7000 tokens, JSON-schema constrained output, `enable_thinking=false`) completes normally (~50 tok/s). The second request of the sequence crashes the server immediately after slot selection:

```
slot get_availabl: id 0 | task -1 | selected slot by LCP similarity, sim_best = 0.114 (> 0.100 thold)
slot launch_slot_: id 0 | task 853 | processing task, is_child = 0
E CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
E   current device: 0, in function ggml_backend_cuda_synchronize at D:\a\llama.cpp\llama.cpp\ggml\src\ggml-cuda\ggml-cuda.cu:2485
E   cudaStreamSynchronize(cuda_ctx->stream())
```

### Variable isolation (one change per probe, same request sequence)

| probe | change vs frozen args | result |
|---|---|---|
| control | none (b10107) | **crash** (3/3) |
| A | `--slot-prompt-similarity 0` | crash (slot-reuse hypothesis refuted) |
| B | client sends `cache_prompt: false` | crash |
| C | build **b10243** (same args) | crash (same signature, `:2499`) |
| D | ALL experts to CPU (`blk\..*\.ffn_.*_exps\.=CPU`) | crash |
| E | no `--override-tensor`, `--n-gpu-layers 20` (whole-layer offload) | crash |
| F | `--cache-type-k/v f16` (fa still on) | crash |
| **G** | **`--flash-attn off`** (+ KV f16, required) | **no crash — same 2-request sequence and an 87-request campaign complete cleanly** |

CPU-only inference (no CUDA DLLs) also never crashes.

So: not the build, not prompt-cache/slot reuse, not the MoE offload pattern, not KV quantization — the crash tracks the **CUDA flash-attention path** on this arch/input, across at least b10107→b10243.

Also note: earlier probes with a different input showed the crash is input-dependent (a ~900-token prompt passes, a ~1200-token variant of the same content crashes), which is why we can reproduce it deterministically with our fixed sequence but cannot yet provide a minimal public prompt (the content comes from proprietary documents). Happy to run instrumented builds / additional probes on request, and to share token counts, sampling params, and full server logs.

### Expected behavior

No illegal memory access with `--flash-attn on`; or, if the configuration is unsupported for `qwen35moe` + partial expert offload, a graceful error instead of a crash.
items.title: CUDA illegal memory access in cudaStreamSynchronize (flash-attn path) with Qwen3.6-35B MoE + partial expert offload — deterministic, cross-build (b10107, b10243); disappears with -fa off
