items.title: vulkan: tune mat-vec rows for batched inference on Strix Halo

items.body:
Description

On an AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395, gfx1151 iGPU, 128 GB unified memory) running Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF with a build containing PR #27742, decode throughput collapses as a function of context depth only, not during generation:

  • ~19–21 tok/s for short prompts (< ~512 tokens)
  • drops sharply once total context passes ~1K tokens
  • plateaus at ~5.5–6.1 tok/s from ~2K onward (down to ~4.6 tok/s at 45K) — a ~3.5–4x cliff

Output quality is unaffected (a 45K-token needle-in-haystack test returns the exact hidden value). Prefill is also degraded at depth (pp1 @ d4096 ≈ 9 t/s vs ≈ 20 t/s at d0), but the generation-rate collapse is the main problem.

This looks HIP-path specific: on CUDA devices with the same model/quant the long-context decay is mild (~18.5 → ~15.7 tok/s at 30K depth on DGX Spark / GB10; similar reports on dual-4090 setups at 80–250K context still showing ~21 tok/s decode). Suspect the QSA indexer / ggml_top_k / small per-token gather op chain falling back to an unoptimized or CPU-synced path on HIP once sparse attention kicks in beyond the indexer activation threshold.

Standard llama-bench reproduction (no server needed)

llama-bench supports --n-depth to pad the KV with N previous chat turns, so the decode-rate-vs-depth cliff reproduces with a single command:

Results (mean ± stddev, tg256 @ depth):

context depth | decode t/s -- | -- 0 | 18.33 ± 1.43 256 | 19.56 ± 0.07 512 | 19.57 ± 0.09 1024 | 6.10 ± 0.07 1536 | 6.02 ± 0.07 2048 | 5.93 ± 0.08 3072 | 5.80 ± 0.05 4096 | 5.75 ± 0.06 8192 | 5.49 ± 0.04

(pp1 @ same depths: 19.7 / 19.4 / 20.1 / 13.3 / 7.5 / 5.9 / 10.8 / 9.0 / 6.0 t/s — prefill degrades too.)

The same cliff was independently confirmed through llama-server (-np 1, single client, no concurrency — verified via f_sim_best = 1.000 slot logs and repeat runs): tiny prompt 51 tok → 20.0 tok/s decode; 1402 → 13.2; 2026 → 7.1; 5555 → 5.8; 45634 → 4.6.

Environment

  • Model: unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF UD-IQ4_XS (93.7 GB, 3 shards) — cliff also seen with other quants on this hardware is untested; Q4_K_XL can't fit this machine
  • llama.cpp source: tarball at commit ef687669 (PR #27742 head merged into master 2026-08-27); llama-server --version reports 0.3.0-dev (build 0, commit unknown) because of the tarball build
  • Build flags (HIP): -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGGML_HIP_NO_VMM=ON -DGGML_HIP_MMQ_MFMA=ON -DGGML_HIP_GRAPHS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=OFF (PIC=OFF required: ggml 0.22.0 PIE default conflicts with HIP 32-bit relocations on this toolchain)
  • Backend: ROCm 7.2.4, device detected as AMD Radeon Graphics, gfx1151 (0x1151), VMM: no
  • OS/kernel: Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 7.0.0-30-generic
  • Env: LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE=1 (required — QSA + q8_0 KV asserts at qwen4exp.cpp:544 otherwise), LLAMA_MMAP_RANDOM=1 (makes no difference to the cliff; both values tested)
  • Server flags when reproduced via llama-server: -ngl 99 -c 131072 -np 1 --jinja -fa on --reasoning off --reasoning-budget 0 -t 32 --threads-batch 32 -b 8192 -ub 2048 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --load-mode mmap
  • Memory during the cliff is healthy (used ≈ 73–81 GiB, available ≈ 35–44 GiB, PSI ~0) — not a swap/thrash artifact; this was separately confirmed on a machine where the model fits fully resident

Additional data point

  • -fa off A/B run: the cliff persists almost unchanged (tg256 = 17.13 @ d0 → 6.07 @ d1024 → 5.75 @ d2048 → 5.41 @ d4096). So it is not the HIP flash-attention kernels — it points at the QSA indexer / top-k / gather op chain that activates beyond ~1K context regardless of the attention implementation.

Questions for maintainers

  1. Is the QSA lightning indexer (ggml_top_k and the per-token score/gather op chain) fully implemented in the HIP backend, or does it fall back to CPU at decode time? (Skipping top-k on CUDA reportedly crashes — the HIP equivalent path is what I suspect here.)
  1. GGML_HIP_GRAPHS=OFF is required on gfx1151 in this build configuration — could the loss of graph capture specifically hurt the many-small-kernels QSA decode step?
  1. Any recommended way to profile this on HIP (rocprof with our permissions setup) to narrow down which op blows up at ~1K tokens?

Happy to run additional configurations (other quants, -d sweeps, op-level traces) — this machine is otherwise idle and the model stays loaded.
items.title: qwen4exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next): severe decode slowdown beyond ~1K context on HIP / gfx1151 (Strix Halo)

items.body:
### Name and Version

version 1 (1705d43)
build with Clang 23.0.0 for Windows

### Operating systems

Windows

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

AMD Strix Halo 128GB

### Models

Qwen 3.6 35B MoE Q8

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I was fighting with 30% cpu usage and decreased GPU utilization on AMD Strix halo machine when running Qwen 3.6 35B MoE Q8 generation on ROCm. Vulkan does not have that problem and needs only ~5% cpu to run tg. 
GLM found this issue in src/llama-model.cpp around line 1300:    
```
// there is very little benefit to offloading the input layer, so always keep it on the CPU
pimpl->dev_input = { cpu_dev, &pimpl->cpu_buft_list };
```
This keeps tok_embd on CPU even with -ngl 99, which forces GET_ROWS(tok_embd, inp_tokens) onto the CPU backend at the start of every forward pass. On Stix Halo where CPU and GPU share same DDR5 it hurts a lot.

Possible fix is to mirror the output-layer policy for the input layer when full offload is requested.

Before fix: 
41.33 t/s tg (30% CPU usage)

After full GPU offload: 
47.24 t/s tg (2% CPU usage)

> Repro report for **PR #27742** — the PR discussion is locked (`too heated`), so filing here instead. Everything below is tested against that PR's head (`6c5afc86`) and also the #27774 head (`abdc7a0`).

## Multi-segment prompt regression on Strix Halo (gfx1151) — deterministic repro + a GPU-state gotcha

First of all, thanks for this PR — single-turn usage already works great here (thinking mode included, after the chat-template workaround below).

### Environment

- Strix Halo laptop APU: Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 + Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`), ROCm 7.2, kernel 6.19.8
- Tested both #27774 head (`abdc7a0`) and #27742 head (`6c5afc86`)
- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF` `UD-Q4_K_XL` (111.3 GB)
- `llama-server -ngl auto -c 8192 --parallel 1 --jinja` with `LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE=1` (required, otherwise output is broken as noted earlier in the thread)

### Bug: any prompt with ≥2 message segments degrades to `//////`

Single-segment prompts are **perfect** (long 900-token user turns, thinking mode, cache-hit reruns all fine). Add a second segment and the very first generated token is already `/`, then `/` forever. 100% deterministic, temperature-independent.

Minimal repro via `/completion` (temperature 0):

**CLEAN:**
```
<|im_start|>user
What is the capital of France?<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
```

**DEGEN — multi-turn:**
```
<|im_start|>user
My name is Bob.<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
Noted!<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>user
What is my name?<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
```

**DEGEN — plain text before the first `<|im_start|>` (so even "preamble + one segment" breaks):**
```
Previous conversation: user said hi, assistant replied hello.
<|im_start|>user
What is the capital of France?<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
```

Also degenerate: standalone `system` message + user; `user`+`user`+`user`.

So the boundary is purely **segment count ≥ 2 (or any tokens preceding the first segment)** — content and length are irrelevant. Since the first sampled token is already wrong, this looks like a prefill-path bug for multi-segment inputs (PLE n-gram history / indexer state across segment boundaries?).

On the chat endpoint this means any multi-message conversation degenerates, while single-turn works — which also explains why template variations (system blocks etc.) make it look random. Workaround we use: a custom chat template that folds system text + tools into the first user turn, keeping the prompt single-segment. Thinking mode then works fine for single-turn.

### Gotcha: OOM-killed server leaves the GPU in a bad state

After `llama-server` gets OOM-killed (or `pkill -9`), the GPU enters a state where **every** subsequent run — any binary, any prompt, including previously-clean single-segment repros — outputs only `/`. This silently poisons triage: results look non-deterministic when they aren't. A function-level reset restores it without rebooting:

```
echo 1 | sudo tee /sys/class/drm/card1/device/reset
```

(Context if it matters: this machine already runs `amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0` on the cmdline from an earlier ring-timeout issue.)

### Question

Is multi-segment prefill known / on the roadmap? Happy to test any patch — the repro above is fully deterministic on my end.

items.body:
## Summary

Enables the existing `GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB` code paths on HIP via **hipCUB** (rocPRIM), which provides CUB-compatible APIs (`DeviceRadixSort`, `DeviceSegmentedRadixSort`, `DeviceScan`, `BlockScan/Load/Store`).

This fixes a severe decode cliff and a hard abort on ROCm for `qwen4exp` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next):

- **#27856** — decode collapses 19.6 → ~6 t/s once `n_kv` crosses ~1024 tokens on HIP (Strix Halo)
- **#27865** — over RPC, the worker aborts with `TOP_K failed: invalid configuration argument` once `n_kv` crosses 2048 columns

## Mechanism

Without `GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB`, the HIP backend reports `TOP_K`/`ARGSORT` as unsupported beyond **1024 columns** (`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu`, `supports_op`: `return op->src[0]->ne[0] <= 1024;`), because the no-CUB fallback (`argsort_f32_i32_cuda_bitonic`) exceeds launch limits past that (threads = `ncols_pad/2` > 1024, shared memory `ncols_pad * sizeof(int)` > 64 KiB smpb).

For `qwen4exp`, the QSA lightning indexer runs `ggml_top_k()` over a `[n_kv, n_tps]` tensor (`ne[0] == n_kv`) in **all 12 QSA layers on every decode token**. Past the 1024-column threshold the op moves to CPU — with a device→host copy of the scores, a CPU top-k, a host→device copy of the indices and a sync **per layer per token** → the observed 3–4× decode cliff. Over RPC the crash occurs because `ggml_backend_rpc_device_supports_op()` currently reports unconditional support, so the op is dispatched to a worker whose real backend cannot launch it.

With the CUB paths enabled, `top_k`/`argsort` use `DeviceRadixSort`/`DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` on the GPU for arbitrary column counts, and `supports_op` legitimately reports support.

## Changes

- `argsort.cu`, `top-k.cu`, `mean.cu`, `sum.cu`, `cumsum.cu`: include `<hipcub/hipcub.hpp>` instead of `<cub/cub.cuh>` under `GGML_USE_HIP` (using-declaration or `namespace cub = hipcub;` for the qualified usages in `cumsum.cu`)
- `argsort.cu`: skip the `DeviceSegmentedSort` capture-check on HIP and always use `DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` — rocPRIM has no `DeviceSegmentedSort`, and radix sort works both inside and outside stream capture
- `common.cuh`: alias the stream-capture-status API (`cudaStreamCaptureStatus`, `cudaStreamIsCapturing`, …) — the HIP runtime does not provide these aliases; guarded by `GGML_USE_HIP && GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB`
- `ggml-hip/CMakeLists.txt`: expose `GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB` as a CMake option (previously this define was not reachable from any build system on HIP)

**CUDA builds are unaffected:** every source change is guarded by `GGML_USE_HIP`; `ssm-scan.cu` already excludes itself on HIP and needs no change.

## Validation

2× AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151, ROCm 7.2.1, Thunderbolt RPC cluster), `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` UD-IQ4_XS (93.7 GB, 3 shards), 262144 ctx, `llama-server` + `ggml-rpc-server` (master):

- No TOP_K abort at large `n_kv` (previously a hard worker crash past 2048 columns, #27865)
- Decode: **20.2 t/s** at <1K context, **20.1 t/s** at 18K, 11.7 t/s at 52K — the 1K cliff from #27856 is gone; the remaining degradation is linear (~1 µs per KV token) and comes from the QSA attention being implemented as a mask over the full KV rather than gathering the top-k selection (separate, kernel-level optimization opportunity)
- Prefill: 282 t/s at 18K tokens (`-ub 512`)
- Output quality verified on long generations (800+ tokens, German and English)

Build: `cmake -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DGGML_CUDA_USE_CUB=ON …` with ROCm 7.2.1 (clang from ROCm, `CMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=<rocm>/bin/amdclang++`).

items.body:
## Overview

In ggml_backend_sycl_context::get_scratchpad_mem(), when scratchpad_md.get_size() == 0, a nullptr was passed into dnnl::memory(). This caused oneDNN to throw dnnl_invalid_arguments, producing the "could not create a memory object" crash during ggml_sycl_op_mul_mat evaluation.
Fixed by using scratchpad_size = std::max((size_t)1, scratchpad_md.get_size()) in common.hpp to make sure a valid memory pointer.

The sycl::malloc_device and sycl::free calls in fattn-buffers.cpp are bypassing ggml_sycl_malloc_device. On Intel iGPU, this caused allocations exceeding 4GB to fail and ignored the Level Zero relaxed allocation extension.
Replaced the raw sycl::malloc_device/sycl::free calls in fattn-buffers.cpp with ggml_sycl_malloc_device and ggml_sycl_free_device.

oneDNN rejects VMM pointers (ext_oneapi_virtual_mem) and the environment flags for disabling DNN/VMM was not complete and GGML_SYCL_DISABLE_DNN wasn't actually checked anywhere so using it had no effect. Added try catch around the oneDNN GEMM calls in ggml-sycl.cpp to log a warning and go back to Intel onemkl.

Changes from review

Thanks to @Titaniumtown for the review addressed both comments:

Warning guard in helper.hpp: get_memory_info() is called on every SYCL memory query, so it is very frequent during a normal inference run. Without the warned guard, the ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN warning printed on every single call in stderr. The static bool warned flag makes it print once per process instead.
Style consistency in ggml-sycl.cpp: the GGML_SYCL_DISABLE_DNN / GGML_SYCL_DISABLE_VMM checks were sperated blocks now both are a single boolean expression.

## Additional information

Tested on Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3-8B on an Intel UHD Graphics 770 iGPU (i9-14900K) neither model ran on Intel iGPU previously; both now run correctly, including full offload (-ngl 99).

# [draft-mtp] Draft acceptance collapses to 0.0 under `-np N` with multi-ubatch batches — async `t_h_nextn` device→host copy race

## Summary

Self-speculative decoding (`--spec-type draft-mtp`) silently breaks under parallel slots (`-np 4`): as soon as concurrent requests carry long prompts (decode batches spanning multiple ubatches), draft acceptance drops from a healthy **0.48–0.85** to **exactly 0.00000** on all slots, generation falls back below no-MTP speed, and consumers of the endpoint see empty `message.content` completions (`finish_reason=stop` after a handful of `reasoning_content` tokens).

The trigger is a race between the **async device→host copy of `t_h_nextn`** (the MTP draft's input hidden states) and **any later graph that reuses the `t_h_nextn` extra buffer** — the next ubatch within the same `decode()`, or the next `decode()` call under `-np N` continuous batching. When the copy loses, the MTP draft conditions on NaN `h` rows, its logits go NaN, and every draft is rejected.

Verified at [`f5b9bd39b`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/commit/f5b9bd39b) (build 10176), HIP backend. The same binary is correct at `-np 1` and for single-ubatch batches.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| llama.cpp | [`f5b9bd39b`](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/commit/f5b9bd39b) (b10176), HIP build, `AMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151` |
| ROCm | 7.2.2 (pinned; gfx1151 native) |
| GPU | AMD Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo, gfx1151), 256 GB unified |
| Model | [unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF) `UD-Q4_K_XL` + `mmproj-F16` (`qwen35` hybrid: Gated DeltaNet + Gated Attention, embedded nextn/MTP layer) |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.17 |

Server flags:

```bash
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --mmproj mmproj-F16.gguf --jinja \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9999 -ngl all -fit off -np 4 \
  -c 1048576 -n 131072 -b 1024 -ub 256 -fa on -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 \
  --load-mode dio --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 -rea on \
  --reasoning-format deepseek --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0 --metrics
```

## Reproduction

Self-contained script (stdlib only, no client framework needed) — it fires 4 concurrent chat completions, each with a ~19k-token system prompt, and prints per-request `OK`/`EMPTY` plus finish reasons.

<details>
<summary>repro_mtp_np4.py (click to expand)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduce the draft-mtp acceptance collapse under -np N concurrent load."""
import json, sys, threading, time, urllib.request

URL = "http://127.0.0.1:9999/v1/chat/completions"
N_CONC = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 4
TARGET_TOKENS = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 19000

unit = ("### Skill {i}: skill_{i} handles topic {i}. Steps: analyze, plan, "
        "execute, report. Constraints: verify outputs, cite sources.\n")
SYS = "You are an agent. Available skills:\n" + "".join(
    unit.format(i=i) for i in range(TARGET_TOKENS // 9))

def one(idx, results):
    body = {"model": "local_llm", "max_tokens": 1200, "messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": SYS},
        {"role": "user", "content": f"[{idx}] Say hello and list what you can help with, one line."}]}
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        r = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1200))
        c = r["choices"][0]
        content = (c["message"].get("content") or "").strip()
        results.append((idx, "OK" if content else "EMPTY", c["finish_reason"],
                        r["usage"]["completion_tokens"], time.time() - t0))
    except Exception as e:
        results.append((idx, "ERROR", type(e).__name__, 0, time.time() - t0))

def round_test(round_n):
    results = []
    ts = [threading.Thread(target=one, args=(i, results)) for i in range(N_CONC)]
    for t in ts: t.start()
    for t in ts: t.join()
    empty = sum(1 for r in results if r[1] != "OK")
    for r in results:
        print(f"  round {round_n} req{r[0]}: {r[1]:5s} finish={r[2]:6s} ct={r[3]:5d} {r[4]:7.1f}s")
    print(f"  round {round_n}: empty {empty}/{N_CONC}")
    return empty

if __name__ == "__main__":
    total = sum(round_test(n + 1) for n in range(2))
    print(f"TOTAL empty: {total}/{2 * N_CONC}")
```

</details>

### Expected output on an affected build

Server log (`--metrics`, per slot, at task end):

```
slot print_timing: id 0 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
slot print_timing: id 1 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
slot print_timing: id 2 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
slot print_timing: id 3 | draft acceptance = 0.00000 (    0 accepted /   4786 generated), mean len = 1.00
```

The same server, **sequential** single request on a cold slot:

```
slot print_timing: id 3 | draft acceptance = 0.57865 (  206 accepted /   356 generated), mean len = 3.31
```

Client side, affected requests return `finish_reason=stop` with empty content after a few reasoning tokens, or run away in reasoning until the token cap — both surface as "empty completion" to an agent/chat client.

### What does *not* trigger it

- `-np 4` with short prompts (single-ubatch batches): 0/12 failures over 3 rounds
- Long prompts processed **sequentially** (one slot active): healthy acceptance
- Warm prefix cache (prefill mostly cached): healthy
- `-np 1` with MTP: always healthy

→ the failure requires **concurrent** requests producing decode calls whose batches split across ubatches (long prompts), under multi-slot continuous batching.

## Root-cause analysis

Instrumentation adds two probes (patch inlined at the end of this section):

1. In `llama_context::decode()`'s per-ubatch `t_h_nextn` extraction: after the async copy, `ggml_backend_sched_synchronize()` then compare the **device tensor** contents (via synchronou

## Overview

Make `--fit` work properly on SYCL, so `--fit-target 1` is viable

## Additional information

There are two problems which make --fit not work as well as it should for SYCL devices:

- it doesn't properly account for how much extra VRAM will be needed when the KV cache is fully populated
- it is too pessimistic about how much VRAM is actually required for other reasons.

This means that SYNC users have to spend a long time adjusting `---fit-target` to find a value large enough that it doesn't OOM when all the context is used.

This is a bigger problem for users who can fit all their KV cache onto their GPU, like me with a Arc b70 running unsloth's qwen 3.8. If only 12Gb of VRAM is available, most of the KV cache is in normal RAM anyway, so the under-estimate is less obvious.

With this PR applied, you should be able to run with `--fit-target 1` and not have it OOM. The maximum context size might be a little lower than `--fit` calculated previously, but this time it's calculated correctly and won't crash mid-run.

To properly log memory allocations and deallocations I used a sibling [PR](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27631), but as this is my first contribution I'll keep the other PR in draft until this is merged.

> [!IMPORTANT]
>
> GGUF generated before Aug 27th 2026 must be reconverted, otherwise vision will be broken. See: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27342#issuecomment-5399098880

## Overview

DFlash2 adds two more modules compared to DFlash, grouped dynamic depthwise convolution and candidate selector. 

The formula is for reference. `out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`. `base` is the static kernel, `δ` is the dynamic part predicted from the input.`x` is divided into groups `g(c)` and `δ` is shared across a group. Another one is `edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`. `A`/`B` are the codebooks for the predecessor and the candidate. This position's hidden is projected by `project(h)`to the same rank to multiply `A`. And `unary[c]` is the draft's own score for `c`.  

DFlash2 is enabled when the checkpoint is DFlash2; no need to use extra flag.

We evaled `Qwen3.8-27B` at `Q4_K_M`on Apple M5 Pro 64 GB. And the test data is first 8 problems of GSM8K.
Concurrency is set to 1 and temperature is 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20. We use default `xhigh` reasoning and set
2,048 maximum new tokens.

| Method | Draft quant | Block | Decode TPS | Decode speedup | Acceptance | Normal stops |
|--------|------|--:|------:|------:|-----:|---|
| Autoregressive | — | — | 10.42 | 1.00× | — | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | BF16 | 8 | 19.31 | 1.85× | 4.92 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q8_0 | 8 | 18.43 | 1.77× | 5.08 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q4_K_M | 8 | 18.89 | 1.81× | 5.03 | 8/8 |

When ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft splits allocation on buft max_size, a view-only tail at the end of the context could skip the final alloc_tensor_range. Persistent views (e.g. KV k_stream / v_stream) were then left without ggml_backend_view_init.
Allocate only parent tensors in alloc_tensor_range and initialize all views in a final pass over the context after all splits complete.
## Overview
`ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft` can split a context across multiple buffers when a tensor would exceed the backend buffer-type `max_size` (for example Vulkan's default 1 GiB). If the remaining tail of the context contains only views, the final `alloc_tensor_range` may be skipped, so those views never get `ggml_backend_view_init`.
Persistent KV stream views (`layer.k_stream` / `v_stream`) then keep `tensor->data == NULL` while `view_src` is allocated. Host state save/restore later calls `ggml_backend_tensor_get` / `set` on those views and hits:
`GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated")`
This change:
- allocates only parent tensors inside each split range
- initializes all uninitialized views in one final pass over the context
Also adds `test_view_init_after_max_size_split` in `tests/test-alloc.cpp`
to cover the oversized-parent + view-only-tail case.
## Additional information
Fixes #19839
Fixes #23737
Fixes #21762

Related:
- #21576 (state-IO `!tensor->data` guards; complementary discussion)
I reproduced the assert with Qwen3.6-27B (MTP) when a parent KV tensor exceeded buft `max_size` and the context ended with a view-only tail.
Note on #21576: skipping tensors with `!tensor->data` avoids the assert, but can omit real KV still reachable via `view_src` and misalign the serialized state. This PR fixes the missing view init in the allocator instead.
Prior investigation commit (same patch on older master; kept for reference):
https://github.com/Yoshi4470/llama.cpp/commit/99655d5854e63e736a6a93280e01b7e785a59ba5
## Test plan
- [x] `test-alloc` (includes new `test_view_init_after_max_size_split`)
- [x] Vulkan A/B on the Qwen3.6-27B MTP speculative path (same command, 10 runs each):
  - before (`e3546c794`): 0/10 (assert every time)
  - after (this PR): 10/10 (no assert, completed normally)
- [x] Earlier `amdvlk64.dll` crash after the assert site was resolved by an AMD driver update; treated as separate from this allocator fix
- N/A: equivalent-size CPU repro (not practical on this machine)

### Command used for the A/B runs:
- Vulkan / AMDVLK, Windows, AMD Software 26.6.4
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)
```
llama-cli.exe -np 8 -c 2097152 --no-mmap -m models/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ctkd q4_0 -ctvd q4_0 \
--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 -p "Hello!"
```
## Requirements
- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - Cursor assisted with implementing the finalize-views pass and regression test after I identified the root cause in the alloc split path, and with local verification.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Off-topic comments and AI slop/spam in this thread will be deleted. Keep the discussion focused.

---

Draft. Adds support for `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` (HF `model_type: qwen4_exp`, `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`): converter, text graph, sparse attention, vision, and three quantizer fixes the model needs. Opening as a draft because the weights are not public yet, so the accuracy numbers below cannot be reproduced from outside at the moment.

## Architecture

| subsystem | how it is handled |
|---|---|
| Gated delta net (3 of every 4 layers) | subclasses the existing delta-net base; the only delta from Qwen3.5 is a sigmoid output gate instead of silu |
| MoE, 512 experts, top-10, gated shared expert | `build_moe_ffn`, unchanged |
| Interleaved mrope, partial rotary 64/256 | `ggml_rope_multi` with `LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_IMROPE`, unchanged |
| Hyper-connections (`hc_count = 4`, low rank) | self-contained in `qwen4exp.cpp`; `deepseek4.cpp` is untouched |
| Per-layer embeddings, 97.7 GiB n-gram hash table | host-side row indices in a `set_input`, then `ggml_get_rows` |
| QSA sparse attention (budget 2048, ratio 4) | new graph plus an optional third cache in `llama_memory_hybrid` |
| Vision | stock Qwen3-VL ViT through the existing clip path |

`git diff master --stat -- ggml/` is empty: no new ggml op, and no change to any existing one.

## Correctness, against the reference implementation

| check | result |
|---|---|
| wikitext-2 perplexity, 145 chunks at ctx 2048 | 4.0068 +/- 0.02271 vs 4.0126 for the reference |
| top-1 agreement, 512 tokens of prose | 98.0 percent |
| QSA vs dense below the budget | bit identical on BF16 and F32, max logit delta 0.0 over all 2051 rows |
| QSA vs dense above the budget, 8192 tokens | diverges on 3 percent of positions |
| indexer selection vs the reference | 0.975 mean jaccard against a 0.991 precision floor |
| `test-llama-archs -a qwen4exp` | OK on CPU (0.00e+00), CUDA (8.44e-08) and Meta, roundtrip OK |

Two caveats on that table, since neither is obvious from the numbers. The bit-identical row is measured on BF16 and F32; a quantized model is not bit identical across the boundary, and UD-IQ1_S shows a max logit delta of 2.84e-03. And `test-llama-archs` is a weaker check than it looks for this architecture: its synthesised model carries no PLE tensors, so the PLE `set_input` never runs, and it is insensitive to the GDN fused-QKV segmentation convention (three different segmentations, one correct and two deliberately wrong, all returned 8.44e-08). It is a plumbing and roundtrip check, not a correctness oracle.

The bit-identical result below the budget is the useful one: QSA is dense by construction under `indexer_top_k + compress_ratio - 1` cached tokens, so it is a free oracle on the whole selection and masking path.

## Effect on other architectures

Six shared files contain deletions rather than pure additions:

- `llama-quant.cpp`: three fixes, each byte-exact against the parent commit. `tensor_type_fallback` had no case for 32-block types, so a tensor whose ncols is not divisible by 32 aborted instead of falling back; `--tensor-type` could not name `per_layer_token_embd` because `--token-embedding-type` returned first; and the `work` buffer was sized `nelements * 4` as an upper bound on a value already known exactly, which is 150 GB per process on a model with a 51.2 G element tensor. Six A/B cases, six matching md5s.
- `llama-graph.cpp`: `build_attn_mask_top_k` lifted verbatim out of the DSA `build_attn` overload so both share it. The node construction sequence is identical after splicing the helper back into its call site, and `deepseek32` and `glm-dsa` both pass at 0.00e+00 on CPU.
- `llama-memory-hybrid.cpp`: the new `filter_idx` defaults to `nullptr` and every use is guarded.
- `llama-model-loader.cpp`: adds a `GGUF_TYPE_UINT64` case to a type check that previously threw.
- `llama-hparams.cpp`, `llama-model.cpp`: new fields and new switch cases.

A shared hyper-connection base with `deepseek4` was considered and rejected: the two formulations agree on the residual layout and nothing else (full-rank projection with Sinkhorn normalisation there, low-rank silu gate and a mean collapse here), so factoring it out would touch DSV4's hot path to share about ten lines.

## Note for reviewers

This branch was developed against a snapshot and rebased onto current master. Two rebase conflicts were resolved by hand, both additive: `test-llama-archs.cpp` where master had added a `LLM_ARCH_DEEPSEEK4` condition to a line this port also edits, and `llama-model-saver.cpp` where master reworked the DSV4 key block. Worth a close look, since the local build was against the pre-rebase tree.

## AI Usage
Used Claude and Local Models for testing, iteration and code design - manual verification of model / PR usage

### Git commit

version: 0.3.0-dev (build 10621, commit c1d0e7a00) — tag v0.3.0
OS: Ubuntu, Linux x86_64
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 3090 (24GB), CUDA
Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (deepseek4 arch, 256 experts, UD-Q2_K_XL quant, unsloth)

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When --cpu-moe is passed (which sets model_params::tensor_buft_overrides to keep MoE weights on CPU), the new -fit/--fit memory-fitting logic (moved to common/, now accounting for n_streams — #27496) refuses to run because overrides are already user-set:

common_params_fit_impl: projected to use 24840 MiB of device memory vs. 22341 MiB of free device memory
common_params_fit_impl: cannot meet free memory target of 1024 MiB, need to reduce device memory by 3523 MiB
common_fit_params: failed to fit params to free device memory: model_params::tensor_buft_overrides already set by user, abort

This is logged as a warning (W), not a fatal error, so the server continues loading with the original, unfitted parameters instead of stopping or falling back to a safe configuration. Since the projected footprint (24840 MiB) already exceeds free VRAM (22341 MiB), this reliably ends in an OOM later, at compute-buffer allocation time — the actual failure is much less legible than the root cause:

ggml_backend_cuda_buffer_type_alloc_buffer: allocating 14656.12 MiB on device 0: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
ggml_gallocr_reserve_n_impl: failed to allocate CUDA0 buffer of size 15368060928
graph_reserve: failed to allocate compute buffers
llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: failed to allocate compute pp buffers

This same class of bug was already reported for --fit on + --sleep-idle-seconds (#24684) with the same "tensor_buft_overrides already set by user, abort" message; this report is the --cpu-moe-triggered variant of what looks like the same underlying issue in the fit logic (post-#27496 refactor).

Expected behavior
Either:

-fit should fail loudly (non-zero exit) when it can't fit params to free memory, instead of silently proceeding with an oversized configuration that's guaranteed to OOM later, or
-fit should be able to work around a user-set --cpu-moe/--n-cpu-moe override (e.g. by adjusting context size / batch size instead of tensor placement) rather than aborting entirely.

Actual behavior
Server proceeds past the failed fit and crashes later during compute buffer allocation, with a much less informative error than the original fit failure.

Reproduction

llama-server \
  -m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-Q2_K_XL-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  --cpu-moe \
  -c 524288 \
  -b 8192 -ub 8192 \
  -fa on \
  --port 8000

Workaround
Passing -fit off explicitly avoids the misleading log path (fit was doing nothing useful anyway with --cpu-moe set). Manually reducing -b/-ub (e.g. to 4096) shrinks the compute buffer enough to fit in the remaining VRAM.

cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON
cmake --build build --config Release -j $(nproc)
```

### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 10233 (0ab9d6fed)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Also reproduced on b10217 (`ddd4ec142`) and on current master at the time of writing.

### Operating systems

Linux — Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-28-generic

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (32607 MiB), driver 610.43.02, CUDA UMD 13.3, nvcc 13.3.73, built for `sm_120a`
- AMD Ryzen 7 9700X (8c/16t), 96 GB DDR5

### Models

`unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF` — reproduced on `UD-IQ1_S` (77 GiB), `UD-IQ3_XXS` (98 GiB) and `UD-Q2_K_XL` (91 GiB). arch `deepseek4`.

### Problem description

Whenever a prompt is processed in **more than one forward pass** (i.e. it does not fit
entirely inside a single batch *and* a single micro-batch), DeepSeek-V4 generates **nothing
but repeated `<` characters**. No error, no warning — prefill reports normal throughput and
only the output is garbage.

**The trigger is CUDA flash attention.** Single-variable isolation, identical model, prompt,
`-c 4096` and `-ub 512`:

| config | result | prefill |
|---|---|---|
| `--flash-attn on` | **CORRUPT** | 391.3 t/s |
| `--flash-attn off` | **CLEAN** | 272.8 t/s |
| `--flash-attn off` (repeat) | **CLEAN** | 274.4 t/s |

And a backend A/B at identical settings (`-ub 512`, same quant/prompt):

| backend | result | prefill |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA (layers on GPU) | **CORRUPT** | 439.7 t/s |
| `-ngl 0`, op-offload **on** (1800 MiB VRAM still used) | **CORRUPT** | 117.9 t/s |
| `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" -ngl 0 --no-op-offload` (18 MiB VRAM) | **CLEAN** | 19.2 t/s |

Note the middle row: with zero *layers* offloaded, op-offload still executes on the GPU
(117.9 t/s is not achievable on 8 CPU cores here) and it still corrupts. Only removing CUDA
from the process entirely gives clean output. **`-ngl 0` alone is not a CPU-only test.**

Why `-ub` appeared to matter (it is a symptom, not the cause): the prompt must fit in one
pass. Splitting is what exposes the bug.

| prompt | `-b` | `-ub` | passes | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1811 | 4096 | 4096 | 1 | CLEAN |
| 1811 | 4096 | 512 | 4 | CORRUPT |
| 14379 | 16384 | 16384 | 1 | CLEAN |
| 14379 | 16384 | 4096 | 4 | CORRUPT |
| 30255 | 8192 | 8192 | 4 batches, 1 ubatch each | CORRUPT |

The last row matters: making `-b == -ub` does **not** help, so it is not specific to
micro-batch splits *within* a batch — any additional forward pass triggers it. A very small
`-ub` (1–96) is also clean, and the largest clean `-ub` *shrinks* as the prompt grows
(≤96 at 1.8k tokens, ≤64 at 14.4k), which is consistent with "how much gets split", not with
a fixed threshold.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a deterministic ~1.8k-token prompt (no external files):

```python
lines = [f"Item {i:04d}: alpha bravo charlie delta echo foxtrot golf hotel {i*37%991}."
         for i in range(90)]
open("p.txt","w").write("\n".join(lines))
```

2. Start the server — note **f16 KV** (no `--cache-type-k/v`), so this is not #25382:

```bash
export GGML_CUDA_PDL=0
llama-server -hf unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF:UD-Q2_K_XL \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -c 4096 -np 1 \
  -fa on -fitt 768 -b 4096 -ub 512 -t 8
```

3. Send it to the raw completion endpoint (no chat template involved):

```bash
python3 -c "
import json,urllib.request
p=open('p.txt').read()
b=json.dumps({'prompt':p,'n_predict':40,'temperature':0.0,'cache_prompt':False}).encode()
r=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(
  'http://127.0.0.1:8080/completion',b,{'Content-Type':'application/json'})))
print(repr(r['content']))"
```

**Actual:** `'<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<'`
**Expected:** normal text. Re-run with `-ub 4096` (single pass) or `-fa off` and it is correct.

`-fa off` is not a usable workaround at real context sizes: the non-FA path materialises an
explicit `[n_tokens × n_kv]` score matrix per head (64 heads), so it loads at `-c 131072` and
then OOMs on the first long prompt (I measured a 234712 MiB allocation attempt at `-c 131072`).

### Ruled out

Each tested individually and **verified to have taken effect**; none change the outcome:

- **Quantized KV cache** (#25382 / #26423) — reproduces with **f16** KV, no `--cache-type-k/v`.
- **Chat template** — reproduces on raw `/completion`. (Via `/v1/chat/completions` the `</think>` prefix is emitted correctly *before* the run of `<`.)
- **Prompt caching / context checkpoints** — `-ctxcp 0` still corrupts, and the repro uses `cache_prompt:false`.
- **CUDA graphs** — `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` still corrupts. `LLAMA_GRAPH_REUSE_DISABLE=1` still corrupts.
- **Fusion** — `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1` still corrupts.
- **PDL** — corrupts with `GGML_CUDA_PDL=0` and with PDL enabled.
- **Op offload** — `GGML_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH=999999` still corrupts (prefill drops 439→42 t/s, so it took effect).
- **Matmul backend** — `GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ=1` and `GGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS=1` both still corrupt.
- **Lightning-indexer kernel choice** — patched the dispatch to force the generic vector kernel instead of WMMA (prefill 439→350 t/s, so active): still corrupts.
- **DS4 custom ops** — patched `supports_op` to reject `LIGHTNING_INDEXER` and `DSV4_HC_PRE/POST/COMB`; llama.cpp logs `resolve_fused_ops: ... set to disabled` and runs generic decompositions: still corrupts.
- **`GGML_SCHED_MAX_SPLIT_INPUTS`** 30 → 128 (source edit): no change.
- **Host buffers** — `--no-host` still corrupts (prefill 645→38 t/s).
- **`--swa-full`**, **`-nkvo`**, **`-kvu`**, **`LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE=1`**: all still corrupt.
- **Threads** `-t 8`/`-t 12`, with and without `-tb`; **sampling** `temperature` 0.0 and 1.0.
- **Toolkit/driver** are current and self-consistent; build targets the correct arch.

### Op-level tests do not catch it

- `test-backend-ops test -b CUDA0 -o DSV4_HC_PRE,DSV4_HC_POST,DSV4_HC_COMB,LIGHTNING_INDEXER,SET_ROWS` → **267/267 pass**.
- Exported the **real** graph ops from a corrupting run (`test-export-graph-ops`) and replaye

items.body:
Summary

When llama-server --embeddings runs a pooled embedding model on the Metal backend, the graph still contains MUL_MAT result_output (the LM head). Its output is never read — result_embd_pooled is a GET_ROWS from result_norm — but it is fully materialized on every request.

For Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (vocab 151669) at 7343 tokens that discarded tensor is f32 [151669, 7343] = 4,454,821,868 bytes (4.15 GiB), and it grows linearly with input length. Past some input size the Metal backend then produces out-of-bounds behavior and the server returns all-NaN vectors. Gating the LM head behind an embeddings + pooling check eliminates the failure and drops the MTL0 compute buffer by roughly 10×.

Symptom

Embeddings come back as all-NaN. nlohmann/json serializes NaN as null, so a client sees a vector of null rather than an error.

  • /health continues returning 200
  • no Metal error is logged
  • no recovery short of restarting the process
  • -ngl 0 (CPU) is completely clean

The onset depends on how far past the threshold the input is:

  • Near the threshold (~7343 tokens at vocab 151669): the triggering request itself returns a valid vector, and every request after it — including a 4-token input — returns all-NaN for the lifetime of the process. This is consistent with the overrun landing in a mapped neighbor allocation rather than in the triggering request's own output.
  • Well past it (28,001 tokens): the triggering request is already all-NaN itself.

Worth stating explicitly because the near-threshold case is the dangerous one — the request that breaks the server looks successful, so a pipeline that validates only the newest response never sees a failure.

Environment

Reproduced on unmodified upstream master:

  • build 1 (192067b), AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101, Darwin arm64, shallow clone of ggml-org/llama.cpp, -DGGML_METAL=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
  • Apple M5 Max, 128 GB unified memory (110100 MiB visible to Metal), macOS
  • llama-server --embeddings, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B f16, -c 32768 -np 1 -b 8192 -ub 8192 -ngl 99

Originally found on two independent forks; the pristine build above was made specifically to rule out fork-local Metal changes, and reproduces identically.

Reproduction

bash
llama-server -m Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B-f16.gguf --embeddings \
  -ngl 99 -c 32768 -b 8192 -ub 8192 -np 1 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8084

python3 -c "print('가나다라마바사한글테스트문장입니다'*2000, end='')" > /tmp/long.txt

curl -s localhost:8084/v1/embeddings -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "$(python3 -c "import json;print(json.dumps({'input':open('/tmp/long.txt').read(),'model':'emb'}))")" \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);v=d['data'][0]['embedding'];print('prompt_tokens',d['usage']['prompt_tokens'],'nan',sum(1 for x in v if x is None or x!=x),'/',len(v))"

curl -s localhost:8084/v1/embeddings -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello","model":"emb"}'

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Loading large models with the ROCm backend hangs on my device. It loads in to memory (I can see memory usage grow) but it slows down as more memory is allocated and eventually just hangs. Or maybe slows down to a point where progress is so glacial I cannot observe it in a reasonable time. This bug only seems to affect larger models.

#### The following models exhibit this behaviour:

- MiniMax M2.1 (mradermacher/MiniMax-M2.1-i1-GGUF:IQ3_XXS, ~82GB in weights)
- Step 3.5 flash (bartowski/stepfun-ai_Step-3.5-Flash-GGUF:Q3_K_S, ~80GB)

- GLM-4.6V (unsloth/GLM-4.6V-GGUF:Q4_K_XL, ~61GB)

Loading does not finish and it seems to be using between 1.7-2.0 CPU cores once stuck.

#### The following models load and run correctly on ROCm:

- gpt-oss-120b (mradermacher/gpt-oss-120b-Derestricted-i1-GGUF, ~60GB - slows down a lot near the end)
- GLM 4.7 Flash (unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-GGUF:Q8_K_XL, ~33GB - loads quickly)

items.body:
## Overview

<!-- Describe what this PR does and why. Be concise but complete -->

This PR adds support for MTP (Multi Token Prediction) heads. I tested this on Qwen3.6 27B and Qwen3.6 35BA3B but in principle it should work for any MTP model. I've posted the detailed results below, but typically I see a steady-state acceptance of around 75% with 3 draft tokens, which is more than >2x speed-up over baseline. The design decisions I took to get to this stage are as follows:

- The MTP model is a separate model which loads from the same GGUF, the idea is that MTP should automatically start and we shouldn't need to distribute the MTP gguf separately but also it has it's own context/kv-cache etc. 
- I saw a problem in #18039 where the hidden features weren't propagated correctly across multiple ubatches, so this PR adds a separate "hook" for the MTP to consume after each `ubatch`
- The MTP speculative class is fairly trivial (although it does depend on #22400, but could work without it)

> [!TIP]
> MTP is compatible with Vision input and Tensor/Pipeline Parallelism

> [!NOTE]
> Prompt processing (PP) speed typically takes a negative hit when MTP is enabled mainly due to Device-To-Host (D2H) embedding transfers. It's something to be optimized in the future.

> [!NOTE]
> Parallel decoding with MTP is supported, but not fully optimized yet.

items.body:
## Overview

Fixes a regression after #24233, which restored HIP integrated GPU detection. On my AMD APU, this also made the ROCm host-buffer path available for HIP integrated GPUs. With that path enabled, prompt input appears corrupted: chat templates and system prompts can be ignored, and generated output becomes garbage.

This change keeps integrated GPU detection/reporting intact, but disables direct ROCm_Host compute on HIP integrated GPUs. The fix does not disable host-buffer exposure entirely, pinned buffers remain available to preserve functionality, while only the problematic direct compute path is blocked.

## Additional information

Tested locally on gfx1151 / RDNA3.5 APU with ROCm 7.14. The corrupted input/output issue is fixed with this patch.
The issue appeared in external harnesses like Pi and OpenCode. It can also be reproduced in the built-in web UI with a sufficiently large combined first input. For example, gemma-4-26B-A4B with 4676 tokens of context or more outputs `<unused49>` indefinitely. Other models can be way more resilient and their output starts by saying 'Based on the text provided, which appears to be a corrupted or "hallucinated" version of a Wikipedia article'.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - I used AI assistance to review and patch the relevant code. I tested and reviewed the final change myself.

### Command line

```shell
llama-server -m Ornith-1.0-35B-UD-Q3_K_M.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 262144 -np 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa auto --port 8080
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When a Metal allocation fails during init, the server logs the failure, logs that the
backend is unrecoverable, and then finishes starting up anyway. It prints `model loaded`,
binds the port, and answers `/health` with `{"status":"ok"}`. Every completion request
after that returns HTTP 500.

The per-request errors are reported correctly, so this isn't silent corruption. The
problem is that startup completes and `/health` reports ready for a process that can
never serve a request. Anything using `/health` as a readiness probe treats it as up.

I should say up front that `-ngl 99` disabled the auto-fit that would otherwise have
prevented this:

```
W common_fit_params: failed to fit params to free device memory: n_gpu_layers already set by user to 99, abort
```

So the OOM itself is arguably my own fault. The part I think is still a bug is what
happens afterwards — the backend reports itself unrecoverable and the server starts
anyway.

Steps:

1. Pick a context size where the allocation cannot fit. On a 24 GB M5 the Metal device
   reports 18186 MiB, and this model at `-c 262144` needs 19005 MiB. llama.cpp's own
   memory breakdown says so directly:
   ```
   cmn  common_param:   - MTL0    : Apple M5 (18186 MiB, 18185 MiB free)
   load_tensors:  MTL0_Mapped model buffer size = 15897.19 MiB
   llama_kv_cache:       MTL0 KV buffer size =  2720.00 MiB
   common_memory_breakdown_print: |   - MTL0 (Apple M5)    | 18186 = ... + (19005 = 15897 +    2782 +     325) +         398 |
   ```
   At `-c 65536` the KV cache drops to ~680 MiB and it fits.
2. Start the server with the command line above.
3. 15 `Insufficient Memory` errors during init, then the backend declares itself
   unrecoverable and the decode fails.
4. Server prints `model loaded` and `listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080`.
5. `/health` → 200 `{"status":"ok"}`.
6. Any completion request → 500, and the OOM count roughly doubles.
7. Re-run at `-c 65536` and the same model starts and serves normally.

### What I'd expect

Exit non-zero at startup, the way other unrecoverable init failures already do — a
quantized V cache without flash attention returns `nullptr` and the server refuses to
start (b9960 `src/llama-context.cpp:3518`; on master the same check is at `:3602`,
reworded to `quantized V cache requires flash_attn to be enabled`).

Failing that, `/health` should reflect it. It currently returns `{"status":"ok"}`
unconditionally once the model is marked loaded (b9960
`tools/server/server-context.cpp:4322`, master `:4448`); the only gate is the
server-state middleware, which fires solely on `!is_ready`.

### Relevant log output

Init (timestamps and log-level prefixes trimmed):

```
ggml_metal_synchronize: error: command buffer 0 failed with status 5
error: Insufficient Memory (00000008:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory)
   ... 15 occurrences ...
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
graph_compute: ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async failed with error -1
process_ubatch: failed to compute graph, compute status: -1
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
cmn  common_conte: llama_decode() failed: -3
srv  llama_server: model loaded
srv  llama_server: listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080
```

One completion request afterwards:

```
ggml_metal_graph_compute: backend is in error state from a previous command buffer failure - recreate the backend to recover
llama_decode: failed to decode, ret = -3
srv        decode: Compute error. off = 0, n_batch = 2048, ret = -3
srv    send_error: task id = 0, error: Compute error.
srv  update_slots: decode() failed: Compute error.
```

Observed from the client:

```
$ curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' localhost:8080/health
{"status":"ok"}
200

$ curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' localhost:8080/completion \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"prompt":"int add(int a,int b){","n_predict":20,"temperature":0}'
{"error":{"code":500,"message":"Compute error.","type":"server_error"}}
500
```

`Insufficient Memory` count: 15 after init, 28 after one request, 29 including shutdown.

### Notes

Reproduced on b9960 (`a935fbffe`). I haven't run master, but both relevant paths look
unchanged there: the init probe still treats a failed `llama_decode` as non-fatal and
continues (master `common/common.cpp:1576`, b9960 `:1497`), and `/health` is still
unconditional. Worth confirming against master before acting on it.

One model, one machine, Metal only. Speculative decoding was not involved
(`speculative decoding not supported by this context` appears in the log).

items.body:
## Bug Description

GLM-5.2 crashes deterministically when attempting distributed inference across multiple DGX Spark nodes via ggml-rpc. The crash occurs during graph computation with `invalid data ptr` on the worker side and `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` abort on the orchestrator side. This appears analogous to #26424 (DeepSeek V4, Metal) but affects CUDA (sm_121).

## Environment

- **Hardware:** 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, Grace Blackwell, 128GB unified memory each)
- **OS:** DGX OS (Ubuntu-based, aarch64)
- **CUDA:** sm_121 native build
- **llama.cpp:** master `5788b510a` (ggml 0.18.1), built with `-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_RPC=ON`
- **Network:** 1Gbit Ethernet between nodes
- **Model:** GLM-5.2 UD-IQ4_NL (also reproduced with UD-Q4_K_M), unsloth GGUF split files

## Setup

**Workers (3 nodes):**

```
./build/bin/ggml-rpc-server -c --host 192.168.1.XXX --port 50052
```

**Orchestrator (1 node):**

```
./build/bin/llama-server \
  -m ~/models/gguf/glm-5.2/UD-IQ4_NL/GLM-5.2-UD-IQ4_NL-00001-of-00009.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  -ngl 999 -c 4096 \
  --tensor-split 1,1,1,1 \
  --rpc 192.168.1.121:50052,192.168.1.111:50052,192.168.1.128:50052
```

## Expected Behavior

Model loads across 4 nodes and serves inference (works with Gemma-4-26B, Qwen3.6-35B, Mistral-Small-3.2 on identical setup).

## Actual Behavior

Weights distribute successfully (~113GB cache per worker), but crashes during graph_compute:

**Worker output:**

[create_node] invalid data ptr[graph_compute] failed to create graph node 30 (id=197768091778640)
Client connection closed

**Orchestrator output:**

ggml-rpc.cpp:519: Remote RPC server crashed or returned malformed response
recv failed (bytes_recv=0, size_to_recv=8)

Stack trace: `ggml_backend_rpc_buffer_get_tensor` → `ggml_backend_tensor_copy` → `ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async` → `llama_context::graph_compute` → `llama_context::decode` (during `common_init_from_params`).

## Reproducibility

- 100% deterministic — same worker, same graph node (30)
- Reproduced with UD-IQ4_NL (~348GB) and UD-Q4_K_M (~434GB)
- Reproduced with `-c 4096` and `-c 131072`
- Reproduced with and without `--no-warmup`
- All 4 nodes on identical commit (`5788b510a`, fresh pull)

## What Works

- Single-node llama.cpp on same hardware (Gemma, Qwen, Mistral)
- 2-node llama.cpp RPC with smaller models (Gemma-4-26B, ~51.8 tok/s)
- GLM-5.2 on single-node (4×RTX 6000, Ollama, Note: Different machine! But same model GLM 5.2 UD-IQ4_NL)

## Related

- #26424 — DeepSeek V4 Flash RPC crash (Metal, similar MoE/MLA architecture)
- GLM-5.2 uses IndexShare and MTP/NextN layers — likely unsupported ops in RPC graph distribution

## Logs

Full orchestrator and worker terminal output, dmesg are attached.

[glm-rpc-orch.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708516/glm-rpc-orch.log)

[glm-rpc-worker3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708521/glm-rpc-worker3.log)

[glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30708525/glm-rpc-dmesg-g3.log)

items.body: This PR adds a new `--numa mirror` option which mirrors model weights to each Numa node on the system, and uses a thread-local var in the OMP threadpool to select the correct mirror copy local to the thread at runtime, to eliminate cross-socket traffic. Build instructions: ``` apt-get update apt-get install -y libnuma-dev libgomp1 cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-march=native" -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-march=native" -DGGML_OPENMP=ON cmake --build build --parallel ``` To test: ```bash # No mirroring: ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ~/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf # Numa mirroring of model weights to every node: ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ~/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --numa mirror ``` Test system is a two-socket Xeon 6238R Cascade Lake, with 768GB of DDR4-2933 (6 channels per socket). Without `--numa mirror`: ``` developer@81ec6c6e6af6:/workspaces/llama-cpp-dbsanfte-dev$ ./build/bin/llama-bench -m ./.devcontainer/Qwen3-32B-Q6_K.gguf | model | size | params | backend | threads | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | pp512 | 20.99 ± 0.01 | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | tg128 | 1.91 ± 0.00 | build: c665d3c9 (6468) ``` With `--numa mirror`: ``` developer@81ec6c6e6af6:/workspaces/llama-cpp-dbsanfte-dev$ ./build/bin/llama-bench -m . /.devcontainer/Qwen3-32B-Q6_K.gguf --numa mirror | model | size | params | backend | threads | test | t/s | | ------------------------------ | ---------: | ---------: | ---------- | ------: | --------------: | -------------------: | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | pp512 | 21.36 ± 0.11 | | qwen3 32B Q6_K | 25.03 GiB | 32.76 B | CPU | 56 | tg128 | 2.70 ± 0.00 | build: c665d3c9 (6468) ``` Intel PCM tool during mirror inference showing both sockets using local mem: There's still a bit of cross-socket traffic (5%) because only model weights are mirrored, not tensors created at inference time. I'll play with that, maybe mirroring those aggressively will help too, or maybe not. Right now anything created at inference time just gets set to live on Node 0.

### GGML backends

2x Bosgame M5 Ryzen AI Max+ 395

VMM: no

  ROCm0: Radeon 8060S Graphics (120000 MiB, ...)

### Models

https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
GGUF quantization: UD-IQ3_XXS
4 shards
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00004.gguf

speculative draft model used: dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf

any quantization. Just depends, whether rpc is used

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### Summary

A ROCm RPC worker on AMD gfx1151 aborts in `GGML_OP_TOP_K` while processing a sufficiently long DeepSeek V4 Flash prompt.

Short requests work correctly.

A long request consistently reaches exactly 4096 processed prompt tokens and then causes the remote ROCm RPC worker to abort with:

```text
ggml_cuda_compute_forward: TOP_K failed
ROCm error: invalid configuration argument
```

The client then reports:

```text
Remote RPC server crashed or returned malformed response
recv failed (bytes_recv=0, size_to_recv=8)
```

This is reproducible on both:

```text
TheRock / ROCm 7.13.0
TheRock / ROCm 7.14.0
```

using the same llama.cpp commit:

```text
3653e6d6d
```

Replacing only the remote ROCm RPC worker with a Vulkan/RADV RPC worker on the exact same Radeon 8060S / gfx1151 hardware makes the same setup stable.

Vulkan is significantly slower, but it does not crash.

### Difference from #24177

This appears related to #24177 because both failures involve the AMD `TOP_K` path and an RPC worker abort.

However, this case is different:

- `--no-spec-draft-backend-sampling` is already enabled.
- The failure occurs during prompt prefill, not draft-token backend sampling.
- Short prompts work.
- Long prompts reproducibly fail after 4096 processed prompt tokens.
- Reducing `--ubatch-size` from 256 to 128 does not change the failure point.
- Switching only the RPC worker backend from ROCm to Vulkan avoids the crash.

Therefore, the `--no-spec-draft-backend-sampling` workaround from #24177 does not avoid this failure.

### Server command

```bash
/usr/local/bin/llama-server \
  --model /opt/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/UD-IQ3_XXS/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-UD-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00004.gguf \
  --alias deepseek-v4-flash-q3-xxs \
  --gpu-layers all \
  --fit off \
  --load-mode none \
  --ctx-size 1048576 \
  --parallel 4 \
  --jinja \
  --rpc 10.44.0.2:50053 \
  --split-mode layer \
  --tensor-split 1,1 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 \
  --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --no-spec-draft-backend-sampling \
  --spec-draft-type-v q8_0 \
  --temp 1.0 \
  --top-p 0.95 \
  --min-p 0.0 \
  --top-k 0 \
  --spec-type draft-dspark \
  --model-draft /opt/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/UD-IQ3_XXS/dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf \
  --spec-draft-n-max 2 \
  --batch-size 1024 \
  --ubatch-size 128 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --port 5800
```

Remote worker:

```bash
ggml-rpc-server \
  --host 10.44.0.2 \
  --port 50053 \
  --device ROCm0
```

### Reproduction

1. Start a ROCm `ggml-rpc-server` on the gfx1151 remote system.
2. Start `llama-server` with the command above.
3. Send a short chat request.
4. The short request completes normally.
5. Send a long chat request containing approximately 18k prompt tokens.
6. Prompt processing proceeds normally:

```text
prompt processing, n_tokens = 1024, progress = 0.06
prompt processing, n_tokens = 2048, progress = 0.11
prompt processing, n_tokens = 3072, progress = 0.17
prompt processing, n_tokens = 4096, progress = 0.22
```

7. Immediately after the 4096-token point, the remote ROCm RPC worker aborts.

Changing:

```text
--ubatch-size 256
```

to:

```text
--ubatch-size 128
```

does not change the behavior.

Both fail after 4096 processed prompt tokens.

## Control tests

### Short prompt, ROCm RPC

Works correctly.

Example successful request:

```text
prompt eval time = 1086.65 ms / 33 tokens
eval time = 23099.77 ms / 388 tokens
total time = 24186.42 ms / 421 tokens
draft acceptance = 0.64118
```

### Long prompt, ROCm RPC

Crashes consistently after:

```text
n_tokens = 4096
```

### Long prompt, Vulkan RPC on the same remote gfx1151 GPU

Does not crash.

Only the remote worker backend was changed:

```text
ROCm/HIP -> crash
Vulkan/RADV -> stable
```

This suggests the problem is specific to the ROCm implementation or dispatch of `GGML_OP_TOP_K` on gfx1151 rather than RPC itself.

## First Bad Commit

Unknown.

Reproduced with:

```text
llama.cpp 10311
commit 217df17ac
```

on both ROCm/TheRock 7.13.0 and 7.14.0.

I have not bisected older llama.cpp revisions.

```

on both ROCm/TheRock 7.13.0 and 7.14.0.

### Relevant log output

### Client

```text

slot print_timing: id 1 | task 176 | prompt processing, n_tokens = 2048, progress = 0.11
slot print_timing: id 1 | task 176 | prompt processing, n_tokens = 3072, progress = 0.17
slot print_timing: id 1 | task 176 | prompt processing, n_tokens = 4096, progress = 0.22

/opt/src/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-rpc/ggml-rpc.cpp:519:

recv failed (bytes_recv=0, size_to_recv=8)

libggml-base.so.0(ggml_backend_tensor_copy+0x156)
libggml-base.so.0(ggml_backend_sched_graph_compute_async+0x1f0)
libllama.so.0(llama_context::graph_compute...)
libllama.so.0(llama_context::process_ubatch...)

items.body:
## Overview

**cuda: fuse MoE weighted expert reduction**

Fuses the MoE expert-combine tail on the CUDA backend into one reduction kernel, removing the intermediate tensor traffic between its stages.

After `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID`, the combine is a per-expert scale/weight multiply plus an ordered left-to-right `VIEW`+`ADD` chain that sums the `k = n_expert_used` experts. Those are logical nodes: the backend already fuses consecutive MULs/ADDs, so for the common top-k = 8 case it runs as **two physical `k_bin_bcast` kernels** (fused two-MUL + fused seven-ADD) with the full weighted-expert tensor `[n_embd, k, n_tokens]` written out and read back between them. This PR replaces that with **one kernel** that reads each expert row once and writes the `[n_embd, n_tokens]` result once:

```
dst[t,c] = sum_e ((experts[t,e,c] * expert_scale[t,e]) * weight[t,e])
```

The sum keeps the original left-to-right order. **The primary benefit is reduced global-memory traffic** (the eliminated intermediate tensor)

**Matching** is purely structural (op / shape / stride / view offset / add-chain / closure / aliasing) — never the quant or model. Two shapes: short (`experts * router_weight`) and long (`(experts * expert_scale) * router_weight`). The long form appears whenever a per-expert broadcast scale is applied before the router weight (e.g. the NVFP4 `scale_2` output scale, but the same graph slot can carry other scales); the matcher keys only on that second MUL's presence.

**Kernels:** unrolled templates for `k = 2..8`, one runtime-`k` kernel for `k = 9..15`, a `float4` path when `n_embd % 4 == 0` and aligned (scalar fallback), and an optional per-expert scale via a template flag. The `k <= 15` cap is `ggml_can_fuse_subgraph`'s 31-node limit on the long form (`2*k + 1 <= 31`); larger `n_expert_used` falls back.

**Correctness:** full-model WikiText-2 perplexity is unchanged (**5.8857 ± 0.03661**, on vs off) and `test-backend-ops` passes; the reduction keeps the original left-to-right order. Guards: `weights`/`expert_scale` are copied to scratch when they overlap `dst` (read while writing `dst`); fusion is skipped when `experts` overlaps `dst`; view offsets/strides and the add-chain are validated before fusing.

**Fallback / kill switch:** any unsupported top-k or failed structural/layout/closure/alias check leaves the graph unchanged and runs the per-op path. Enabled by default; `GGML_CUDA_MOE_WEIGHTED_REDUCTION=0` forces the reference path.

## Additional information


**Performance** — prefill `t/s`, default-ON vs `=0`, same binary, mean-vs-mean:

| Hardware | Model | Quant | pp2048 | pp8192 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| RTX 5090 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | NVFP4 | +3.6% | +3.6% |
| RTX 5090 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | Q4_K_M | +4.1% | +3.9% |
| RTX 5090 | Gemma-4-26B-A4B | NVFP4 | +4.3% | +4.3% |
| DGX Spark (GB10) | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | NVFP4 | +5.4% | +5.4% |
| DGX Spark (GB10) | Gemma-4-26B-A4B | Q4_K_M | +7.1% | +6.2% |

**Testing** (both modes, same binary): `test-backend-ops` **13,178/13,178** pass; CTest **42/42** pass; CPU-vs-CUDA compared; WikiText-2 PPL identical **5.8857 ± 0.03661**; `llama-cli` output unchanged. CUDA backend only; no changes to weights or numerics.

### Name and Version

### Description

I'm observing a reproducible VRAM memory leak when running DeepSeek V4 Flash GGUF with DSpark speculative decoding enabled. After each PP+TG (prefill + generate) cycle, VRAM usage increases by approximately **10 MB**, and this accumulation continues until the process eventually runs out of memory (OOM).

This issue does **not** occur with:
- Step 3.7 + DSpark
- Qwen3.8-27B + DSpark

Both of the above maintain stable VRAM usage across multiple cycles.

### Environment
- Model: DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731 version) GGUF + DSpark
- Framework: llama.cpp
- Issue: VRAM leak, ~10 MB per PP+TG cycle

### Suspected Root Cause

I suspect this is a **Draft KV Cache leak** specific to the DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 model when used with DSpark. Specifically:

1. **KV cache positions** are written during every draft step but are **never compacted or properly reclaimed**, leading to continuous VRAM growth[reference:0]. A similar issue has been reported in related forks where "positions are written every tree step but never compacted," causing OOM under sustained traffic[reference:1].

2. **DSpark draft KV-cache group poisoning**: The DSpark draft model's KV cache is flagged as an "eagle group" (same as EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP/DFlash)[reference:2]. The multi-group cache-hit lookup requires **every** KV-cache group to report a nonzero hit for cache reuse to succeed — any single group reporting zero short-circuits the entire request's lookup[reference:3].

3. **Sparse and discontinuous draft KV**: DSpark's draft-layer KV is recomputed from the target model's real hidden state every decode step, meaning it has **no cross-request reuse value**[reference:4]. Its stored blocks are sparse and discontinuous (e.g., `[MISS, MISS, HIT, MISS, MISS]`)[reference:5], never satisfying the consecutive-hit window required for cache lookup[reference:6].

4. **"One-vote veto" effect**: This permanently poisons the AND-combination lookup for the entire request[reference:7], even though the model's real KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) independently have a working hit rate around 89%[reference:8]. As a result, the prefix caching mechanism is effectively disabled — every new request cannot reuse historical caches and must recompute and write new KV cache entries, causing VRAM to grow until exhaustion.

A similar fix has been proposed in vLLM where DSpark draft KV-cache groups are excluded from the cache-hit lookup poisoning mechanism[reference:9]. The same root cause likely applies to llama.cpp.

### Why Step 3.7 and Qwen3.8-27B Are Not Affected

These models likely have different DSpark implementations or KV cache structures that do **not** trigger this cache lookup conflict, allowing normal cache reuse and stable VRAM usage.

### Suggested Fix Direction

- Exclude DSpark draft KV-cache groups from the prefix caching lookup's "all-groups-must-hit" requirement, similar to the approach taken in vLLM PR #47891[reference:10].
- Alternatively, ensure DSpark draft KV cache positions are properly compacted or reclaimed after each generation cycle, as addressed in PR #23461 for draft/MTP resources.

### Additional Context

There have been related reports of DeepSeek V4 KV cache not being reclaimed on slot release, and DSpark-specific KV cache issues with offloading connectors[reference:13]. This may share a root cause with the hybrid-attention KV handling.

Please let me know if additional logs or reproduction steps would be helpful.

Thanks!

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Running llama-server (with `-sm tensor -fa 1 --tensor-read-lazy --load-mode mmap --override-tensor per_layer_token_embd.weight=CPU -ub 512 -b 8192 -ts 4,4,4,3,3`) with unified KV cache works great until there's a second request while the first one is running. As soon as the second request starts processing the first request's decode gets confused and starts recalling incorrectly from previous context.

Claude had this to say when asked why it was breaking:

Mechanism

set_input_qsa (src/llama-memory-hybrid-idx.cpp:383-417) is written per stream, but n_stream = unified ? 1 : n_seq_max (src/llama-kv-cache.cpp:85). Under unified KV it makes one pass over the single cell array holding every conversation's cells, and keys the block map by position:

const llama_pos p = cells.pos_get(j);
blk_of[j] = p/r;
cur_blk_cells[b*r + (p%r)] = j;   // every conversation has a token at position p → collision, last writer wins
filled[b]++;                      // counts foreign cells too

Both conversations occupy positions 0..N, so they collide in every block slot. Each block's pooled indexer key ends up built from whichever conversation wrote last, so conversation A's top-2048 block selection is scored against B's content — A can no longer find its own context. filled[b] inflation also makes incomplete blocks look poolable. The attention mask still hides foreign cells, so there's no leakage of B's text into A — it presents as amnesia and hallucination about A's own history, which is why it reads like a quantization/quality problem.

Nothing forces non-unified for indexer models: cparams.kv_unified is taken straight from params (src/llama-context.cpp:273).

Code was added recently in #27742 so presumably that.

## Overview

This PR implements Speculative Prefill, based on the ICML 2025 paper: *"Speculative Prefill: Turbocharging TTFT with Lightweight and Training-Free Token Importance Estimation"* by Jingyu Liu, Beidi Chen, Ce Zhang ([arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.02789), [GitHub](https://github.com/Jingyu6/speculative_prefill))

> [!NOTE]
> In contrast to speculative decoding, this is not lossless and can cause model performance degradation.

### Approach
In long-context inference, prefill TTFT scales quadratically with prompt length. Speculative prefill reduces this compute by using a smaller draft model to estimate which context tokens are most relevant to the query before evaluating the main target model:

1. **Draft lookahead**: The draft model prefills the prompt and generates $K$ lookahead tokens (default: 8).
2. **Attention extraction**: Softmax attention matrices (`kq_soft_max`) are captured during draft generation via an evaluation callback.
3. **Importance pooling & chunking**: Attention scores are smoothed with a 1D average-pooling filter ($W = 13$), max-reduced across heads/layers, and aggregated into contiguous chunks ($C = 32$).
4. **Sparse target prefill**: Only the top-$p$ fraction of chunks (plus BOS and prompt boundary tokens) are fed into the target model's KV cache.
5. **Generation**: The target model generates tokens autoregressively as normal.

### Benchmarks & Performance Evaluation

All benchmarks were run natively on Vulkan (`AMD Radeon 8060S`, RADV STRIX_HALO, 128 GiB unified LPDDR5X) using **Qwen3.8-27B (Q6_K_XL)** as target and **Qwen3.5-2B (Q4_K_XL)** as the primary draft model (unless noted otherwise).

| **50%** | 1,795.3 ms (1.61x) | 3,273.8 ms (1.63x) | 6,174.8 ms (1.75x) |

#### 2. Synthetic Retrieval & QA Benchmarks

* **Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIAH)**: 100.0% retrieval accuracy across depths (20%, 50%, 80%) down to $p = 0.15$ (298 / 2,058 tokens kept, 1,798.0 ms vs 6,863.2 ms baseline, **3.82x speedup**).

The results below were measured on the development branch, which shares the performance-relevant mirror implementation with this PR.

## What is this?

* Fully replicates large CPU weights on every NUMA node; CPU GEMM paths read from the node-local copy.
* Targets dual-socket systems with large memory pools, especially systems with multiple GPUs split across NUMA nodes.
* Implements `GGML_NUMA_STRATEGY_MIRROR` - enum value 4, already reserved in `ggml/include/ggml-cpu.h` but previously unwired.

## Key points

* `tensor->data` is never modified. The primary copy remains on node 0; KV cache, activations, and all other backends are unaffected.
* Adds one extra weight copy per additional NUMA node. On a dual-socket system, NPS2/NPS4 therefore require 3x/7x additional copies; NPS1 is recommended.
* GPU expert-weight uploads (op offload) read from the replica local to the destination GPU's PCIe NUMA affinity. The NUMA node is obtained from sysfs using `cudaDeviceGetPCIBusId`, resolved through `get_proc_address`, and cached per backend. The bytes are identical; only transfer locality changes. GPUs on the home node retain the existing behavior.

  On the development branch, forcing the wrong source node reduced op-offload prefill throughput by ~48% (`1375.7 -> 711.0 pp`), while remaining bit-exact (`160/160`). Test hook: `GGML_NUMA_MIRROR_SRC_NODE=<n>`.
* Remapping occurs only at CPU GEMM read sites (`mul_mat`, `mul_mat_id`, llamafile SGEMM x2, repack x2) through `ggml_numa_mirror_remap()`.
* Each thread selects its replica using `getcpu()` at entry. This remains correct even if a thread migrates, so explicit CPU pinning is not required for correctness.
* Replica discovery is lazy at `graph_compute`; no allocator hooks are required. Allocation uses anonymous `mmap` plus raw `mbind`, with no `libnuma` dependency.
* Primary placement self-heals using `move_pages()` sampling followed by a 1 GiB probe before full migration. If pinned pages prevent migration, a warning recommends `numactl --membind=0`.
* Repack/AMX extra buffer types are mirrored as well.
* Emits a one-shot coverage report and warns when coverage is below 50%.
* Disabled mode, non-Linux platforms, and single-node systems are no-ops. The hot remap path adds one atomic load per call.

## Limitations

Currently Linux-only, with a maximum of 16 mirrored buffers. A pinned primary allocation may require the `numactl --membind=0` hint.

## Related work

This PR builds on the long-running NUMA work discussed in #1437.

The `--numa mirror` flag name and the mirror concept come from #16000 by @dbsanfte.

The implementation here uses a different mechanism. #16000 turns every tensor->data access into an accessor across 123 files (+4692 lines). This PR leaves tensor->data untouched and confines remapping to the CPU GEMM read sites plus the scheduler's expert-upload source pointer (+516/-10 across 11 files). The sole backend-side addition is a small CUDA helper in ggml-cuda.cu that resolves a GPU's PCIe NUMA node through sysfs; no backend compute or copy path is otherwise modified.

It is also complementary to the sharded-prefetch experiments discussed in #16000. Sharding keeps memory usage at 1x and primarily targets GPU-offload prefill. Mirroring instead targets CPU decode reads: a shard cannot simultaneously provide node-local access to cores on both sockets, whereas a replica can.

## Results

Test system: 2x AMD EPYC 7532 (Zen 2, 32 cores/socket), NPS1, 16x64 GB DDR4-2666 (1 DIMM per channel across all 16 channels), 1 TB total RAM, and 5x RTX 3090.

Measured memory read bandwidth:

* Socket-local: 137 GB/s
* Cross-socket (xGMI): 47.7 GB/s
* Remote access penalty: ~2.1x

### Attribution - GLM-5.2 UD-Q3_K_XL

~302 GB weights, MoE, experts on CPU via `-ot exps=CPU`, attention/shared layers on GPU, `llama-server`, full model.

| config                         |             decode t/s | prefill t/s |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------: | ----------: |
| interleave=all (baseline)      |                   7.20 |        85.4 |
| membind=0, no mirror           |                   6.12 |        95.5 |
| membind=0 + mirror             |               **9.06** |       108.4 |
| pinned + interleave, no mirror |                   7.44 |       148.3 |
| pinned + membind=0 + mirror    | **9.02** (median 9.35) |       146.8 |

* Attribution control: at identical placement (`membind=0`), mirror alone improves decode from `6.12 -> 9.06`, or **+48%**.
* Compared with the best non-mirror configuration in each placement regime, decode improves by **+21-26%**.
* `membind=0` alone costs 15% decode performance (`6.12` vs `7.20`). The gain comes from the replicas, not from binding.
* "Pinned" rows use pinned host buffers for GPU op offload.

### Cross-model - DeepSeek-V4-Flash UD-Q8_K_XL

170 GB, MXFP4 experts, not repack-eligible; exercises the plain host-buffer path. One probe, `n=5`.

| threads     | placement                 | mirror  | decode t/s | resident RAM |
| ----------- | ------------------------- | ------- | ---------: | -----------: |
| 32 (node 0) | cpunodebind=0 + membind=0 | no      |      18.88 |      87.9 GB |
| 64          | membind=0                 | no      |      14.80 |      87.9 GB |
| 64          | interleave=all            | no      |      16.80 |      87.9 GB |
| 64          | membind=0                 | **yes** |  **20.81** |     178.3 GB |

* At identical placement and thread count, mirror improves decode by **+40.6%** (`14.80 -> 20.81`).
* Without replicas, 32 node-local cores outperform 64 cores (`18.88` vs `14.80/16.80`). The second socket's cores cannot compensate for remote weight access; mirroring is what makes them useful.
* The additional ~86 GB of replicated weights buys the +40% decode improvement.

### GLM-5.3-Flash 321B UD-Q4_K_XL

186 GB.

Using the same binary with only `--numa mirror` toggled and position-matched prompts, decode improved by **+46% to +76%**, depending on context depth.
