## Summary

On AMD gfx1151 / Vulkan / RADV, `llama-server` with `--spec-type draft-mtp` dies mid-**prompt** (`decode() failed: vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost`) at tens of thousands of tokens. The same argv with MTP off survives past 125k. A one-site diagnostic that **keeps MTP flags on** but skips `common_speculative_process` while no slot is `SLOT_STATE_GENERATING` also survives past 125k on both 1-seat and 4-seat topologies; generate still drafts.

This is not a checkpoint / `get_tensor` death (`--ctx-checkpoints 0`, this-boot `create_checkpoint=0` `get_tensor=0` `update_tgt=0`). It is not “Vulkan FA at 114k without MTP” on one seat (MTP-off 1×262144 finished 125948). It is the extra draft-context decode that `impl_draft_mtp::process` runs after every target ubatch on `!is_mem_shared` Qwen3.8.

`GGML_VK_MAX_NODES_PER_SUBMIT=1` is already set (the UMA submit-frequency workaround from #24872 / the turboquant fork). It is not enough.

## Name and Version

```
b10352-4dee52f82
Vulkan backend, llama-server
```

`/props` `build_info` = `b10352-4dee52f82`.

## Operating systems

Linux (AMD Strix Halo box).

## GGML backends

Vulkan (RADV).

## Hardware

- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`), 128 GB unified LPDDR5X
- GTT pool 124 GiB (UMA frame buffer ~2 GiB)
- RADV / Mesa **last recorded 2026-08-16: Mesa 25.2.8** (not re-probed on the day of this write-up)
- Env on every arm: `GGML_VK_MAX_NODES_PER_SUBMIT=1`, `queue_preemption_timeout_ms=60000`

## Models

- `Qwen3.8-27B` UD-Q8_K_XL + `mmproj-F16` (Unsloth)
- Hybrid (`qwen35`-family): most layers recurrent, a minority full-attention. Qwen3.8 MTP is `!is_mem_shared`, so the draft context is a **separate** `llama_decode(ctx_dft, same n_tokens)` after the target ubatch.

## Problem description

With `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2`, long unique-prefix prefill dies in `vk::Queue::submit` during prompt processing:

```
radv/amdgpu: The CS has been cancelled because the context is lost. This context is innocent.
ggml_vulkan: device lost on Vulkan0
srv  update_slots: decode() failed: vk::Queue::submit: ErrorDeviceLost
```

dmesg is a compute-ring timeout then reset (`ring comp_1.2.0` / `comp_1.0.1`), process **survives** as a zombie (`/v1/models` 200, later `/completion` 500).

Call site (b10352 `server-context.cpp` `decode()`, then `common/speculative.cpp` `impl_draft_mtp::process`): after every successful target `llama_decode(ctx_tgt, ubatch)`, `common_speculative_process` runs. On this model that is a second same-width draft decode. `--ubatch-size 1024` ⇒ a 1024-wide draft graph after every 1024-wide target graph, at rising `pos`. The outer `decode()` catch does **not** say which of the two `llama_decode`s threw; the A/B below isolates the extra one.

There is an in-tree TODO immediately above the call:

```
// TODO: avoid restoring the draft context and re-evaluating the drafted tokens when not needed [TAG_SPEC_AVOID_DRAFT_REEVAL]
//       for now, always re-evaluate for simplicity
```

## A/B (same box, same GGUF, same day)

Shared flags on every arm unless noted:

```
-ngl 999 --flash-attn on --ubatch-size 1024 --batch-size 2048
--cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0
--cache-prompt --cache-reuse 256 --cache-ram 0 --ctx-checkpoints 0
--image-min-tokens 1024 --threads 16 --jinja
GGML_VK_MAX_NODES_PER_SUBMIT=1
```

Hop = `/completion` unique prefix, tokenized **~125948**, `n_predict=1`.

| Arm | MTP | seats (`-c` / `-np` / slot) | process() during prompt | last healthy n | result |
|--|--|--|--|--:|--|
| A | **off** (no `--spec-type`) | 1 × 262144 | n/a | **125948** | HTTP **200**, 992.6 s, 126.90 t/s, DeviceLost=0, `get_tensor=0` |
| B | **on** `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2` | 1 × 262144 | stock (every ubatch) | **55296** / 0.44 | HTTP **500** at t=6:16.751, `decode() / vk::Queue::submit`, this-boot `create_check=0` `get_tensor=0` `update_tgt=0` |
| C | **on** n-max 2 | 1 × 262144 | **skipped** unless a slot is `SLOT_STATE_GENERATING` | **125948** | HTTP **200**, 993.2 s, 126.81 t/s, DeviceLost=0. Skip log counts 1/16/32/48. Hop 2: `draft_n=6` accepted **2** |
| D | **on** n-max 2 | **4 × 262144** (`-c 1048576 -np 4`) | **skipped** as C | **125949** | HTTP **200**, 994.6 s, 126.64 t/s, DeviceLost=0. Same skip counts. Hop 2: `draft_n=6` accepted **2** |

Production 4-seat MTP-on **stock** process-every-ubatch (same argv as D, unpatched binary) died three times in the **114–117k** band (`n_tokens=114025`, `114688`, `116736`), same raise, same zero copy counters. Do not collapse the 1-seat 55k death into those 4-seat 114k deaths — same class, different CONFIG. Arm D is the 4-seat isolation: skip the extra decode and the 114–117k band is crossed.

After C/D hop 1, `begin()` warned `ctx_dft pos_max=-1` (the skip did what it said). Hop 2 was a short unique prompt, `n_predict=32`: generate still ran draft-mtp (`draft_n=6`, accepted 2). Accept is degraded vs a filled draft KV — expected with an empty `ctx_dft`, not a reason to drop `--spec-type draft-mtp`.

## Minimal diagnostic patch (not proposed as the final ship)

In `tools/server/server-context.cpp`, around the existing `common_speculative_process(spec.get(), batch_view)` after the target ubatch:

```cpp
const bool any_generating = std::any_of(slots.begin(), slots.end(), [](const server_slot & s) {
    return s.state == SLOT_STATE_GENERATING;
});
if (any_generating) {
    if (!common_speculative_process(spec.get(), batch_view)) {
        throw std::runtime_error("failed to process speculative batch");
    }
}
// else: skip draft-context fill during prompt. MTP flags stay on.
```

That is what arms C and D ran. A production-shaped fix is probably **tail-only / last-ubatch** process during prompt (so `pending_h` / draft KV is warm for generate) rather than skip-all. Windowed / smaller draft ubatch is another lever. `--spec-type none` is a diagnostic, not a fix.

## What this is not

- **Not** `--ctx-checkpoints` / `create_checkpoint` / `vk_buffer_get_tensor

## Overview

This PR adds support to `llama-quantize` to quantize models using an imatrix file which does not have importance data for all blocks.

This is currently mainly MTP-enabled GGUFs while using an imatrix file, where MTP layers are not evaluated during imatrix generation, but could also affect future architectures or features.

It is an alternative to https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/23258 and takes a much more minimalist approach, suggested by @bartowski1182:

- imatrix generation is not modified and does not use MTP layers
- Missing layers are instead quantized using a simple, fast quantization method:
    - Q4_0 for Q6_* and below presets
    - MXFP4 for MXFP4
    - Q8_0 for Q8_0

Since MTP benefits far more from speed, even at the cost of some accuracy, this might be preferable to the earlier PR.

I am yet to run comparative benchmarks between the two.

N/A

On Windows with the Vulkan backend, `llama-server` loads the model normally but terminates immediately with an Access Violation (`0xC0000005` / exit code `-1073741819`) upon receiving the first `/v1/chat/completions` request under default context checkpoint settings. ## Overview

DFlash2 adds two more modules compared to DFlash, grouped dynamic depthwise convolution and candidate selector. 

The formula is for reference. `out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`. `base` is the static kernel, `δ` is the dynamic part predicted from the input.`x` is divided into groups `g(c)` and `δ` is shared across a group. Another one is `edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`. `A`/`B` are the codebooks for the predecessor and the candidate. This position's hidden is projected by `project(h)`to the same rank to multiply `A`. And `unary[c]` is the draft's own score for `c`.  

DFlash2 is enabled when the checkpoint is DFlash2; no need to use extra flag.

We evaled `Qwen3.8-27B` at `Q4_K_M`on Apple M5 Pro 64 GB. And the test data is first 8 problems of GSM8K.
Concurrency is set to 1 and temperature is 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20. We use default `xhigh` reasoning and set
2,048 maximum new tokens.

| Method | Draft quant | Block | Decode TPS | Decode speedup | Acceptance | Normal stops |
|--------|------|--:|------:|------:|-----:|---|
| Autoregressive | — | — | 10.42 | 1.00× | — | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | BF16 | 8 | 19.31 | 1.85× | 4.92 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q8_0 | 8 | 18.43 | 1.77× | 5.08 | 8/8 |
| DFlash2 | Q4_K_M | 8 | 18.89 | 1.81× | 5.03 | 8/8 |

## Overview

string_to_spv_func hardcodes `target-env=vulkan1.2` for every shader but those with `_cm2` in the name. A large portion of shaders don't have `_cm2` (`mul_mm`, `mul_mat_vec`, `flash_attn`, `conv`, `argsort`, `cumsum`, etc) but declare `local_size_*_id` that lowers to SPIR-V's `LocalSizeId` execution mode which is invalid under vulkan1.2 environment ruleset without `maintenance4`. Ubuntu 24.04 bundled glslc doesn't enforce the Vulkan-env rule, so it "magically" worked; a current glslc refuses to compile the shaders and Vulkan backend fails to build.

fix: after local #include, detect which shaders actually declare `local_size_*_id` and only bump them to `--target-env=vulkan1.3` leaving everything else vulkan1.2. Chose this over the current existing precedent of disabling `-O` for `shader-compiler-bug` shaders (see #16860 workaround) because that would not optimize the hottest kernels (`mul_mat_vec`, `mul_mm`, `flash_attn`) we want on this hardware.

verification: test-backend-ops 17251/17251 pass on Vulkan0 (full suite). No known duplicate PR/issue found (searched LocalSizeId, maintenance4, target-env=vulkan1.2 / vulkan1.3).

items.body:
## Summary

Batched decoding of a many-expert MoE model (Qwen3-Coder-Next 30B-A3B, 512 experts, top-10,
Q4_K_XL) on an AMD Strix Halo iGPU (gfx1151, RADV, Vulkan backend) shows a large throughput
cliff at exactly **9 concurrent sequences**: aggregate TG drops from 122.5 t/s (B=8) to
82.9 t/s (B=9) and only recovers above B≥24. I traced it to two fixed batch-size thresholds
in the Vulkan backend that switch from the mul_mat_vec kernels to the tiled matmul kernels
above 8 tokens. Raising them removes the cliff on this hardware/model: +56% at B=9, +34% at
B=16, +20% at B=32, with monotonic scaling through B=32 and no regression at B≤8.

## Environment

- HW: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (Strix Halo), Radeon 8060S iGPU (gfx1151), 128 GB unified LPDDR5X
- Driver: RADV (Mesa), Vulkan backend, coopmat enabled
- llama.cpp: reproduced on b9293 and on current master (20a04b2)
- Model: Qwen3-Coder-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL (30B-A3B MoE, 512 experts, top-10)

## Reproduction

```
llama-batched-bench -m Qwen3-Coder-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -c 32768 -ngl 999 -fa 1 \
  -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 --no-mmap -npp 512 -ntg 128 -npl 1,2,4,8,9,12,16,24,32
```

Aggregate TG t/s, master (20a04b2), stock:

| B | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 9 | 12 | 16 | 24 | 32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stock | 45.4 | 69.0 | 96.2 | 122.5 | **82.9** | 93.1 | 103.8 | 118.9 | 130.9 |

The cliff is at the B=8→9 boundary and recovers slowly — a dispatch-boundary signature, not
bandwidth saturation. `GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT=1` makes B=16 *worse* (86.4), so it is not a
coopmat tile issue: any mul_mm path at small n loses to the MMV path on this bandwidth-bound
device.

## Root cause

Two fixed thresholds switch away from the mul_mat_vec kernels above 8 tokens:

1. `mul_mat_vec_max_cols = 8` (ggml-vulkan.cpp) — dense projections;
2. `ggml_vk_use_mul_mat_vec_id(): src2->ne[1] <= 8` — the MUL_MAT_ID expert path, which
   dominates. `GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER=1` shows the expert matmuls growing super-linearly across
   the boundary (per-call, decode phase):

   - `MUL_MAT_ID q4_K m=512 n=10 k=2048 n_expert=512`: 166 µs at batch=8 → 440 µs at batch=12 (2.65×)
   - `MUL_MAT_ID q5_K m=2048 n=10 k=512 n_expert=512`: 213 µs → 488 µs (2.29×)

   Dense MUL_MAT_VEC entries scale sub-linearly per token across the same boundary (healthy).

The `<= 8` heuristic makes sense for few-expert MoEs (8-expert Mixtral-style), where tokens
share experts and the gather-based mm-id amortizes weight reads. For a 512-expert/top-10
model, token–expert overlap at these batch sizes is near zero (B=12 → 120 draws over 512
experts), so switching to mm-id amortizes nothing and pays the tile-inefficiency cost.
vec-id dispatches per token (descriptor sets = nei1) and has no structural limit.

## Experiment: raising the thresholds

Local change: `mul_mat_vec_max_cols` 8→16, and the vec-id gate `ne[1] <= 8` → `<= 32`.

| B | 8 | 9 | 12 | 16 | 24 | 32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stock | 122.5 | 82.9 | 93.1 | 103.8 | 118.9 | 130.9 |
| patched | 126.5 | **129.4** | **135.7** | **139.0** | **150.9** | **157.2** |

- Monotonic through B=32; B=1–4 unchanged (49.1/71.5/99.5 vs 45.4/69.0/96.2).
- `test-backend-ops test -o MUL_MAT` and `-o MUL_MAT_ID` pass vs CPU.
- temp=0 output is byte-identical to stock (same model/prompt).
- End-to-end (llama-server, real prompts, ~1600-tok streams): +41% aggregate at 16 concurrent
  slots, J/token floor drops 0.61 → 0.506 on this device.

## Suggested direction

A flat constant is probably wrong in both directions — for few-expert MoEs the mm-id switch
is right where it is; for many-expert MoEs vec-id keeps winning far beyond 8. A density-based
gate for MUL_MAT_ID would capture both regimes, e.g. stay on vec-id while expected rows per
activated expert is low:

```
use_vec_id = n_tokens * n_experts_used <= C * n_expert   // C ≈ 1–2, to be tuned
```

(Qwen 512/top-10 → vec-id up to ~50–100 tokens; Mixtral 8/top-2 → switches at ~8, like today.)
For the dense `mul_mat_vec_max_cols`, per-arch tuning similar to what PR #20905 did for the
CUDA backend may apply; on gfx1151/RADV, 16 cols showed no downside in my runs.

I'm happy to run benchmarks/validation on this hardware (Strix Halo / gfx1151 / RADV) if
useful — full benchmark logs and the perf-logger dumps are available.

items.body:
When ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft splits allocation on buft max_size, a view-only tail at the end of the context could skip the final alloc_tensor_range. Persistent views (e.g. KV k_stream / v_stream) were then left without ggml_backend_view_init.
Allocate only parent tensors in alloc_tensor_range and initialize all views in a final pass over the context after all splits complete.
## Overview
`ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors_from_buft` can split a context across multiple buffers when a tensor would exceed the backend buffer-type `max_size` (for example Vulkan's default 1 GiB). If the remaining tail of the context contains only views, the final `alloc_tensor_range` may be skipped, so those views never get `ggml_backend_view_init`.
Persistent KV stream views (`layer.k_stream` / `v_stream`) then keep `tensor->data == NULL` while `view_src` is allocated. Host state save/restore later calls `ggml_backend_tensor_get` / `set` on those views and hits:
`GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL && "tensor not allocated")`
This change:
- allocates only parent tensors inside each split range
- initializes all uninitialized views in one final pass over the context
Also adds `test_view_init_after_max_size_split` in `tests/test-alloc.cpp`
to cover the oversized-parent + view-only-tail case.
## Additional information
Fixes #19839
Fixes #23737
Fixes #21762

Related:
- #21576 (state-IO `!tensor->data` guards; complementary discussion)
I reproduced the assert with Qwen3.6-27B (MTP) when a parent KV tensor exceeded buft `max_size` and the context ended with a view-only tail.
Note on #21576: skipping tensors with `!tensor->data` avoids the assert, but can omit real KV still reachable via `view_src` and misalign the serialized state. This PR fixes the missing view init in the allocator instead.
Prior investigation commit (same patch on older master; kept for reference):
https://github.com/Yoshi4470/llama.cpp/commit/99655d5854e63e736a6a93280e01b7e785a59ba5
## Test plan
- [x] `test-alloc` (includes new `test_view_init_after_max_size_split`)
- [x] Vulkan A/B on the Qwen3.6-27B MTP speculative path (same command, 10 runs each):
  - before (`e3546c794`): 0/10 (assert every time)
  - after (this PR): 10/10 (no assert, completed normally)
- [x] Earlier `amdvlk64.dll` crash after the assert site was resolved by an AMD driver update; treated as separate from this allocator fix
- N/A: equivalent-size CPU repro (not practical on this machine)

### Command used for the A/B runs:
- Vulkan / AMDVLK, Windows, AMD Software 26.6.4
- AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with Radeon 8060S (gfx1151)
```
llama-cli.exe -np 8 -c 2097152 --no-mmap -m models/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
-ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 -ctkd q4_0 -ctvd q4_0 \
--spec-type ngram-mod,draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 6 --spec-draft-p-min 0.75 -p "Hello!"
```
## Requirements
- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - Cursor assisted with implementing the finalize-views pass and regression test after I identified the root cause in the alloc split path, and with local verification.

items.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Off-topic comments and AI slop/spam in this thread will be deleted. Keep the discussion focused.

---

Draft. Adds support for `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` (HF `model_type: qwen4_exp`, `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration`): converter, text graph, sparse attention, vision, and three quantizer fixes the model needs. Opening as a draft because the weights are not public yet, so the accuracy numbers below cannot be reproduced from outside at the moment.

## Architecture

| subsystem | how it is handled |
|---|---|
| Gated delta net (3 of every 4 layers) | subclasses the existing delta-net base; the only delta from Qwen3.5 is a sigmoid output gate instead of silu |
| MoE, 512 experts, top-10, gated shared expert | `build_moe_ffn`, unchanged |
| Interleaved mrope, partial rotary 64/256 | `ggml_rope_multi` with `LLAMA_ROPE_TYPE_IMROPE`, unchanged |
| Hyper-connections (`hc_count = 4`, low rank) | self-contained in `qwen4exp.cpp`; `deepseek4.cpp` is untouched |
| Per-layer embeddings, 97.7 GiB n-gram hash table | host-side row indices in a `set_input`, then `ggml_get_rows` |
| QSA sparse attention (budget 2048, ratio 4) | new graph plus an optional third cache in `llama_memory_hybrid` |
| Vision | stock Qwen3-VL ViT through the existing clip path |

`git diff master --stat -- ggml/` is empty: no new ggml op, and no change to any existing one.

## Correctness, against the reference implementation

| check | result |
|---|---|
| wikitext-2 perplexity, 145 chunks at ctx 2048 | 4.0068 +/- 0.02271 vs 4.0126 for the reference |
| top-1 agreement, 512 tokens of prose | 98.0 percent |
| QSA vs dense below the budget | bit identical on BF16 and F32, max logit delta 0.0 over all 2051 rows |
| QSA vs dense above the budget, 8192 tokens | diverges on 3 percent of positions |
| indexer selection vs the reference | 0.975 mean jaccard against a 0.991 precision floor |
| `test-llama-archs -a qwen4exp` | OK on CPU (0.00e+00), CUDA (8.44e-08) and Meta, roundtrip OK |

Two caveats on that table, since neither is obvious from the numbers. The bit-identical row is measured on BF16 and F32; a quantized model is not bit identical across the boundary, and UD-IQ1_S shows a max logit delta of 2.84e-03. And `test-llama-archs` is a weaker check than it looks for this architecture: its synthesised model carries no PLE tensors, so the PLE `set_input` never runs, and it is insensitive to the GDN fused-QKV segmentation convention (three different segmentations, one correct and two deliberately wrong, all returned 8.44e-08). It is a plumbing and roundtrip check, not a correctness oracle.

The bit-identical result below the budget is the useful one: QSA is dense by construction under `indexer_top_k + compress_ratio - 1` cached tokens, so it is a free oracle on the whole selection and masking path.

## Effect on other architectures

Six shared files contain deletions rather than pure additions:

- `llama-quant.cpp`: three fixes, each byte-exact against the parent commit. `tensor_type_fallback` had no case for 32-block types, so a tensor whose ncols is not divisible by 32 aborted instead of falling back; `--tensor-type` could not name `per_layer_token_embd` because `--token-embedding-type` returned first; and the `work` buffer was sized `nelements * 4` as an upper bound on a value already known exactly, which is 150 GB per process on a model with a 51.2 G element tensor. Six A/B cases, six matching md5s.
- `llama-graph.cpp`: `build_attn_mask_top_k` lifted verbatim out of the DSA `build_attn` overload so both share it. The node construction sequence is identical after splicing the helper back into its call site, and `deepseek32` and `glm-dsa` both pass at 0.00e+00 on CPU.
- `llama-memory-hybrid.cpp`: the new `filter_idx` defaults to `nullptr` and every use is guarded.
- `llama-model-loader.cpp`: adds a `GGUF_TYPE_UINT64` case to a type check that previously threw.
- `llama-hparams.cpp`, `llama-model.cpp`: new fields and new switch cases.

A shared hyper-connection base with `deepseek4` was considered and rejected: the two formulations agree on the residual layout and nothing else (full-rank projection with Sinkhorn normalisation there, low-rank silu gate and a mean collapse here), so factoring it out would touch DSV4's hot path to share about ten lines.

## Note for reviewers

This branch was developed against a snapshot and rebased onto current master. Two rebase conflicts were resolved by hand, both additive: `test-llama-archs.cpp` where master had added a `LLM_ARCH_DEEPSEEK4` condition to a line this port also edits, and `llama-model-saver.cpp` where master reworked the DSV4 key block. Worth a close look, since the local build was against the pre-rebase tree.

## AI Usage
Used Claude and Local Models for testing, iteration and code design - manual verification of model / PR usage

  Identical behaviour on both — ~950 builds apart, so not a recent regression.
  

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

   AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (Navi 31, gfx1100), 24 GB VRAM
  ROCm 7.2.0, amdgpu driver 6.16.13
  Ubuntu, kernel 6.14.0-27-generic
  


### Models

- **Ornith 1.5 35B-A3B — I-Compact**
  `Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-APEX-MTP-I-Compact.gguf`
  [Hugging Face – Ornith 1.5 35B-A3B GGUF](https://huggingface.co/AtomicChat/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-GGUF)

- **Ornith 1.0 35B — I-Compact**
  [Hugging Face – Ornith 1.0 35B GGUF](https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.0-35B-GGUF)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Summary 
On hybrid SSM/attention MoE models (general.architecture=qwen35moe, carrying ssm.* keys and
full_attention_interval), llama-server grows RSS by a fixed ~126 MiB on every request and never
releases it. Growth is perfectly linear and does not decelerate — 40 consecutive requests took RSS from 1340
MiB to 6379 MiB at exactly +126 MiB each. 
The allocation is anonymous (RssAnon grows; RssFile stays flat at 110 MiB) and is reclaimed only by
restarting the process. 
A non-SSM model on the identical build, GPU and driver does not leak at all (gpt-oss-20b mxfp4: +0 MiB
request over 12 requests), which is what points at the hybrid/recurrent path rather than at the server or the
backend generally. 
Environmentllama.cpp b9722 (159d093a4) and b10673 (f5e85d43a) — identical behaviourBackend ROCm/HIP, -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1100GPU AMD RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, 24 GB)OS Ubuntu, kernel 6.14.0-27-genericCompiler GNU 13.3.0 
Reproduction 
llama-server -m Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-APEX-MTP-I-Compact.gguf \
-ngl 99 --n-cpu-moe 0 --ctx-size 147456 \
--cache-type-k q4_0 --cache-type-v q4_0 \
--parallel 1 --jinja --flash-attn on --no-mmap \
--batch-size 4096 --ubatch-size 256 --port 8099

Then repeat any trivial completion and sample VmRSS from /proc/<pid>/status after each: 
curl -s -X POST localhost:8099/v1/chat/completions \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"one obscure fact, briefly."}],"max_tokens":40}'

Observed (b10673, 40 requests): 
startreq 12req 24req 36req 40
RSS=1340RSS=2851RSS=4363RSS=5875RSS=6379MiB
MiBMiBMiBMiBdelta=+126
delta=+126
delta=+126
delta=+126
What it is NOT — controlled matrix 
Every row is the same measurement protocol; only the named variable changed.variable value A value B leakllama.cpp build b9722 b10673 (~950 newer) 126.3 / 125.9MTP spec-decode on off 126.5 / 126.3context size 147456 32768 126.3 / 126.3context size 163840 (Ornith 1.0) — 126vision / mmproj on off 126.3 / 126.9max_tokens 220 / 90 40 126.5 / 126.3 / 126KV cache type q4_0 f16 126.3 / 127flash attention on off 126.3 / 127model file Ornith 1.5 Ornith 1.0 (different file) 126 / 126architecture qwen35moe (SSM) gpt-oss-20b (no SSM) 126 / 0 
So it is independent of build, MTP, context length, vision, generated tokens, KV quantization and flash attention
— and it tracks the architecture. 
Why we suspect the recurrent/SSM state path 
The leak is a fixed size per request, unaffected by context length or tokens generated. That matches an
allocation sized by the SSM state dimensions rather than by sequence length. The affected GGUFs carry: 
qwen35moe, ssm.conv_kernel, ssm.group_count,
ssm.inner_size, ssm.state_size, ssm.time_step_rank,
full_attention_interval

Both affected models are hybrid (3 of every 4 layers linear/SSM). The unaffected control model has no ssm.*
keys. 
Our reading is that per-sequence recurrent state is allocated per request and not freed on sequence teardown,
but we have not instrumented the allocator — that part is inference from the measurements above, not
established. 
Impact 
On a 32 GB host this exhausts RAM in roughly 120 requests. In our case that interacted with an amdgpu
VRAM→GTT eviction of the model (~16.6 GB) which then could not fit in host RAM, taking the machine down.
We now mitigate by restarting the lane on an RSS threshold, but the allocation itself looks like a genuine bug

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

<summary>Logs</summary>
<!-- Copy-pasted short logs go into the "console" area here -->

size 256 \ –port 8099 –host 127.0.0.1

pid=$(ss -lptn ‘sport = :8099’ | grep -oE ‘pid=[0-9]+’ | head -1 | cut -d= -f2) for i in $(seq 1 40); do curl -s -o /dev
null -X POST localhost:8099/v1/chat/completions \ -H ‘Content-Type: application/json’ \ -d ‘{“messages”

VmRSS=%d MiB\n”, i, $2/1024}’ /proc/$pid/status done

## Overview

This is an attempt to reduce the amount of matrix multiplication shaders we need by using a spec constant for the type of the A input, similar to how it works for KV cache types in Flash Attention. Additionally, it replaces the current static s, m and l shapes with a map and allows improved tuning through more shapes and a custom selection function, which should help with work like #24407.

It's still draft because currently it regresses Nvidia, because for dynamic type selection all quants with shared memory requirements must also be available. I thought it would eliminate those that are not used, this works on AMD, but not on Nvidia. @jeffbolznv Do you know why? There are other ways to resolve this, hopefully I'll find something that works.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES, AI was used to draft the code, I reviewed, tested and corrected it afterwards.

### Name and Version

llama-b10639-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64
build: 5e6a37cb1 (10639)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64


### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server.exe -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0

or

llama-bench.exe -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Summary

On the ROCm backend, using any q5_0 KV cache type (either K or V) causes the compute graph to fragment from 2 splits into 34 splits. This pushes ~550-580 MiB of compute to the CPU host buffer and causes a ~68% regression in prompt processing throughput.

The issue is **specific to the ROCm backend**. The same build on Vulkan handles q5_0 KV cache correctly (2 splits, no regression). A fork of llama.cpp (build 11429) also handles it correctly on ROCm.

## Environment

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), 24 GB VRAM
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 7900X
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_XL (16.34 GiB, 27.32 B params)
- Flash attention: enabled (`-fa 1`)

## Benchmark results

| KV Cache | graph splits | GPU compute buf | CPU compute buf | pp512 | tg128 |
|----------|:-----------:|:--------------:|:--------------:|:-----:|:-----:|
| q8_0 / q8_0 (ROCm) | 2 | 786.53 MiB | 161.53 MiB | 957.11 t/s | 37.53 t/s |
| q8_0 / q5_0 (ROCm) | **34** | **122.28 MiB** | **551.28 MiB** | **300.10 t/s** | **27.96 t/s** |
| q5_0 / q5_0 (ROCm) | **34** | **122.28 MiB** | **580.53 MiB** | **302.49 t/s** | **28.39 t/s** |
| q8_0 / q8_0 (Vulkan, same build) | 2 | 270.53 MiB | 158.53 MiB | 771.39 t/s | 37.17 t/s |
| q8_0 / q5_0 (Vulkan, same build) | **2** | **295.03 MiB** | **183.03 MiB** | **762.60 t/s** | **37.01 t/s** |

The trigger is q5_0 in the KV cache. It does not matter whether it's used for K, V, or both. The broken GPU compute buffer size is identical (122.28 MiB) in both q8_0/q5_0 and q5_0/q5_0 cases, confirming it's the same code path.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build llama.cpp with ROCm support (or use a prebuilt ROCm binary)
2. Run `llama-bench -m <model.gguf> -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` (or `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0`)
3. Observe ~68% pp512 regression vs. q8_0/q8_0
4. Compare with the same build on Vulkan — no regression

## Expected behavior

q5_0 KV cache should perform similarly to q8_0 KV cache (within a small margin) when using flash attention, as it does on Vulkan and on the beellama fork (build 11429).

## Key log evidence

The main model's `sched_reserve` output:

**Working (q8_0/q8_0, ROCm):**

sched_reserve: ROCm0 compute buffer size = 786.53 MiB
sched_reserve: ROCm_Host compute buffer size = 161.53 MiB
sched_reserve: graph nodes = 4135
sched_reserve: graph splits = 2

**Broken (q5_0/q5_0, ROCm):**

sched_reserve: ROCm0 compute buffer size = 122.28 MiB
sched_reserve: ROCm_Host compute buffer size = 580.53 MiB
sched_reserve: graph nodes = 4135
sched_reserve: graph splits = 34

**Working (q8_0/q5_0, Vulkan, same build 10639):**

sched_reserve: Vulkan1 compute buffer size = 295.03 MiB
sched_reserve: Vulkan_Host compute buffer size = 183.03 MiB
sched_reserve: graph nodes = 4135
sched_reserve: graph splits = 2


The 4135-node graph is the main model forward pass. The 34 splits mean 32 extra GPU↔CPU synchronization points per step.


### First Bad Commit

Not yet identified. The issue is present in build 10639.

items.body:
## Summary

On a gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU, RDNA3.5) system with ROCm 7.2.4, the **HIP/ROCm** backend
produces corrupted output where the **Vulkan** backend, running the **same weights, the same
build, and byte-identical flags on the same machine**, is correct on every attempt.

Measured on three architectures. Two fail on HIP, with **different severity**; one is
unaffected:

| model | `general.architecture` | topology | Vulkan | HIP/ROCm |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct `Q4_K_M` | `llama` | dense | **16/16** @30,516 · 6/6 @1,616 | **0/16** @30,516 · **0/6 @1,616** |
| Qwen3.8-27B `UD-Q8_K_XL` | `qwen35` | dense | **16/16** @29,355 | **0/16** @29,355 · 6/6 @1,349 |
| Ling-3.0-flash `IQ4_XS` | `bailingmoe3` | 512-expert MoE | **16/16** @29,275 | **16/16** @29,275 |

(`@N` = prompt tokens. Each cell is 8 requests run twice; the repeat is deliberate, because a
single 8/8 is not enough to call a backend clean.)

Backend and binary path were read from `/proc/<pid>/exe` on **every** run, not inferred from
the launcher — an earlier "Vulkan" result in this investigation turned out to be the HIP server
still answering after a boot script silently failed.

### Two severities, deliberately not merged

- **`llama` is broken outright on HIP** — at *every* depth tested, including a 1,616-token
  prompt. Output is degenerate word salad:
  `'for 4\n<|contextual background\nline keep track\nTheater in line while mind the material and context in'`
  The same model, flags and template on Vulkan is 6/6 shallow and 16/16 at 30,516 tokens, so
  this is not a configuration error.
- **`qwen35` is correct at shallow depth and fails past roughly 29k tokens** when the request
  also carries a moderately large tool array. Output stays fluent and well-formed; the model
  confidently mis-states **its own tool list**. With an array of `read_file`, `tool_00` …
  `tool_15`:

  > I don't have a `read_file` tool available in my current toolset. The tools I have access to
  > are `tool_01` through `tool_15`, which are placeholder utilities that accept a single string
  > argument. None of them are file-reading tools.

  It has read the placeholders' *descriptions* correctly while losing the entries at the **head**
  of the array. Other samples invented tool names absent from the request entirely, or ran to
  the token limit emitting `finish_reason: "length"` with empty content and no tool call.

Whether these are one defect with severity varying by model, or two, is **not established here**.

### Hypothesis, on a single data point — please treat as a lead, not a finding

The two failing models are **dense**; the one that passes is a **512-expert MoE**. Dense and
MoE matmuls take different paths (`mul_mat` vs `mul_mat_id`), which may be where to look. This
rests on **one** MoE observation and no second MoE was tested. It is offered as a starting
point, not a claim.

## Still present on current master

Reproduced on stock upstream **`b21e4de74567f5eef213765c9476a843c2e43f0d`** — `master`
re-fetched immediately before building — from a clean detached worktree with no local patches,
built for gfx1151 with ROCm 7.2.4.

The same result holds on **`3a653fea932e`** (12 days earlier). **The two SHAs agreeing is
expected rather than corroborating:** there are 7 commits between them and **none touch
`ggml/src/ggml-cuda` or `ggml/src/ggml-hip`**, so it simply means nothing has been attempted on
this code path in that window. It should not be read as an independent second confirmation.

### It is not `e79e4bf66` — please do not close this as a duplicate of that commit

`e79e4bf66` ("ggml-hip : remove -funsafe-math-optimizations", #26696) is **present in every
tested tree and does not fix this.** It is the obvious suspect and it matched on every checkable
detail:

- its message describes `-fassociative-math` reassociating FP reductions and *"can flip greedy
  argmax on **RDNA3.5** (e.g. **MTP speculative decode** diverging from the non-speculative
  baseline)"*;
- the hardware here is gfx1151, which **is** RDNA3.5;
- one of the failing workloads runs `--spec-type draft-mtp`;
- an older tree used here still carries the flag at `ggml/src/ggml-hip/CMakeLists.txt:130`,
  while every tree tested above does not.

With that flag already removed, the defect reproduces at 0/16. This is either a second,
independent problem or the same one with another cause.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Build | stock `b21e4de74567f`; also reproduced on `3a653fea932e` |
| GPU | gfx1151 (Strix Halo APU), 128 GB unified memory |
| ROCm | 7.2.4 (hipcc 7.2.53211-97f5574fe2, AMD clang 22.0.0git roc-7.2.4) |
| OS | Linux |
| Build flags | `-DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1151 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_HIP_COMPILER=<rocm>/lib/llvm/bin/clang++ -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=ON` |

## Server flags — identical on both backends, only the binary differs

```
-ngl 999 --flash-attn on
--ctx-size 65536 --ubatch-size 1024 --batch-size 2048
--parallel 1 --threads 16
--cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16
--cache-prompt --cache-reuse 256 --cache-ram 0
--ctx-checkpoints 32 --checkpoint-min-step 8192
--temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0.0
--jinja        # each model uses its own embedded chat template
```

Verified byte-identical with `diff` between the two launcher files; the only differences are a
comment header, the slot-save path, and the binary path.

## Causes eliminated, each by changing ONE variable

Listed so nobody spends replies asking. Every row was measured; all remained failing:

| varied | result |
|---|---|

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

# ROCm/HIP Backend: Native gfx1031 (RX 6700 XT) Support + Flash-Attention Assert Fix

## TL;DR

On RDNA2 (gfx1031 / RX 6700 XT), the ROCm/HIP backend currently requires **two workarounds** to become usable for long-context inference: a runtime GFX-version override (masquerading as gfx1030) and a manual source patch that silences a flash-attention assert of unknown correctness impact. Once running, ROCm delivers a **~85% prefill speedup** over Vulkan at 8K context, translating to a **~23% net wall-clock win** over a full prefill+decode cycle — despite a 15–18% decode-speed deficit. This makes ROCm the clearly superior backend for this hardware *if* the build/runtime friction is resolved. This report asks for two specific fixes; a separate, still-in-progress investigation into a decode-time sampler gap (`TOP_K` unsupported on ROCm in `llama-server`) will be filed independently once sufficient data is collected.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT (gfx1031, RDNA2, Navi22) |
| CPU | Intel Core i5-11400F |
| RAM | 16GB DDR4 @ 3200 MT/s (XMP) |
| OS | Ubuntu 26.04 LTS |
| llama.cpp commit | `0a50d9909` (build 10108) |
| ROCm version | 7.1.52801-9999 |
| Compiler | clang / hipcc (`CMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang`, `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=hipcc`) |

GPU tuned via LACT (Performance level: Manual, Power Profile: Compute, power limit 182/223W, core voltage offset -90mV, VRAM 1900MHz) — same tuning applied for both backends under test, no backend-specific tuning.

## Why this matters (benchmark data)

Model: `gemma-4-12b-it-IQ4_NL.gguf` (6.24 GiB, 11.91B params). Test: `llama-bench --n-prompt 8192 --n-gen 512 --batch-size 1024 --ubatch-size 1024 --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --n-gpu-layers 99 --flash-attn on`. 3 runs per backend, both with flash-attention enabled and identical batch/cache settings — the only variable changed is the backend.

| Backend | pp8192 (t/s) | tg512 (t/s) |
|---|---|---|
| ROCm (avg of 3) | 653.9 | 34.60 |
| Vulkan (avg of 3) | 354.4 | 40.92 |
| **Δ** | **+84.5%** | **-15.4%** |

Converting to wall-clock for a full 8192-prefill + 512-generate cycle:

| Backend | Prefill time | Decode time | **Total** |
|---|---|---|---|
| ROCm | 12.5s | 14.8s | **27.3s** |
| Vulkan | 23.1s | 12.5s | **35.6s** |

**ROCm wins net wall-clock by ~23%**, despite losing on raw decode throughput, because prefill dominates the cycle at this context depth. The crossover point (below which Vulkan is net-faster) is roughly ~1,760 prompt tokens — meaning ROCm is the better backend for effectively all long-context workloads on this hardware, once it can be built and run without manual intervention.

*(Decode-side deficit is currently under separate investigation — a `TOP_K` sampler op is reported unsupported on the ROCm device in `llama-server`, but this has not yet been confirmed as the cause of the `llama-bench` decode gap, since `llama-bench` explicitly excludes sampling time from its measurements. That will be reported separately once isolated.)*

## Issue 1 — gfx1031 has no working native target; requires runtime override

**Attempted:** building with `-DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1031 -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1031` directly.
**Result:** fails to run correctly on this hardware without the runtime workaround below — confirmed, not assumed.

**Current workaround:**
```bash
cmake -S ~/Projects/llama2 -B ~/Projects/llama2/build-rocm \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=hipcc \
  -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1030 -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx1030
cmake --build ~/Projects/llama2/build-rocm -j"$(nproc)"

# at runtime, gfx1031 must masquerade as gfx1030:
HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=10.3.0 ./build-rocm/bin/llama-bench ...
```

**Ask:** native `gfx1031` target support that runs correctly without `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION`, so RX 6600/6700-series (Navi22) users don't need to build for a neighboring architecture and override the GFX version at runtime.

## Issue 2 — Flash-attention assert crash on this backend/target combo

**Location:** `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-common.cuh` — `GGML_ASSERT(max_blocks_per_sm > 0);`

**Current workaround (patches source, correctness impact unknown):**
```bash
sed -i 's/GGML_ASSERT(max_blocks_per_sm > 0);/if (max_blocks_per_sm <= 0) { max_blocks_per_sm = 1; }/g' \
  ~/Projects/llama2/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn-common.cuh
```

**Why this can't just stay disabled:** turning flash-attention off is not a viable fallback for this use case —

items.body:
qwen4exp landed in #27742 without MTP: `supports_mtp_export = False`, `no_mtp = True`,
no `graph_mtp`. The official `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` checkpoint ships **31 `mtp.*`
tensors** that the converter drops, so the model's own draft head is unavailable and
`ngram-mod` is the only speculation option.

This wires the head up end to end — conversion, tensor loading, the MTP graph, the MTP
context's memory — and fixes one recurrent-rollback gap that speculation on this
architecture depends on.

`graph_mtp` is **derived from @JJJYmmm's #27739** (closed in favour of #27742). Not a
straight copy: that branch used `hparams.hc_count`, `model.hc_mix_*` and
`build_hc_pre`/`build_hc_post` where the merged branch has `hparams.dsv4_hc_mult`,
`model.hc_head_*` and `build_hc_mix`/`build_hc_combine`. The structure and the reasoning
are theirs.

## Usage

```
python convert_hf_to_gguf.py --mtp --outtype q8_0 --outfile out/ Qwen3.8-Flash-Next/
llama-server -m Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-<quant>.gguf \
             -md mtp-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Q8_0.gguf -ngld 99 \
             --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max <N>
```

`--mtp` emits a standalone draft file, so it pairs with an existing main GGUF and does
not require requantising the model.

## The recurrent-rollback fix (please review this part closely)

Registering the arch in `llm_arch_supports_rs_rollback()` is necessary but **not
sufficient**, and enabling it alone silently corrupts state — acceptance collapses from
~72% to ~5% and generations truncate.

`llm_build_delta_net_base::build_conv_state` has a `[TAG_RECURRENT_ROLLBACK_SPLITS]`
branch that materialises all `n_rs_seq + 1` conv-state snapshots into the rotating
bands. qwen4exp does not use it: it has its own `build_conv_state_at`, shared by the
delta-net conv **and** the PLE conv row, which only ever wrote slot 0
(`kv_head * row_size`). With `n_rs_seq > 0` the reads gather via
`s_copy() = idx*mem_size + src0` from bands nothing had written.

So this PR writes every rollback slot in `build_conv_state_at`, mirroring the base
implementation. The SSM state needed no change — qwen4exp inherits
`build_recurrent_attn`, which already handles rollback.

Without it, `common_context_can_seq_rm()` reports `..._TYPE_FULL`, and every speculative
rejection full-clears the sequence, restores a 112 MiB checkpoint and replays forward.
That is correct but pathological: it intermittently wedged a request for 300 s at
~0.2 t/s after a prompt switch, ~300 graph computes per emitted token.

## Design notes

**The head seeds from the wide hyper-connection residual, not the final hidden state.**
qwen4exp has no `model.norm` — the final HC mixer *is* the output norm. `n_embd_out()` is
`n_embd * hc_count` (10240, not 2560), so `t_h_nextn` is the flattened HC streams as the
last trunk block leaves them, before the head mixer. The trunk therefore also stops
cropping `inp_out_ids` at the last layer when a draft context wants those rows, following
the existing `cparams.embeddings_nextn` pattern from `mimo2`.

**`fc_embedding` and `fc_hidden` are joined at conversion time.** The reference sums two
projections where the shared nextn tensor map expects one `eh_proj`;
`A*e + B*h == [A|B] * concat(e, h)`, so concatenating along the input axis is exact.

**The draft block runs attention dense.** `build_layer_attn` is called with a null hybrid
context, selecting the existing dense path (its "no cache or no ratio means dense" branch
just needed a null guard). A QSA indexer would need its own cache for one block. The
`indexer.*` weights are present but unused (~2 MB) — happy to `TENSOR_SKIP` them.

The MTP context reuses the existing `mtp_on_hybrid_qwen` path: a plain KV cache filtered
to the nextn layer.

## Results

Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (Strix Halo, Vulkan/RADV), UD-IQ4_XS target + Q8_0 draft, `-np 1`,
greedy, 200 tokens, median of 3.

Decode t/s (draft acceptance), median of 3 runs per prompt:

| `--spec-draft-n-max` | code | prose | list | median | vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| off (no speculation) | 25.3 | 25.3 | 25.2 | 25.2 | 1.00x |
| **3** | 41.1 (71.8%) | **38.7** (65.2%) | 48.7 (91.8%) | 41.1 | **1.63x** |
| 5 | **41.5** (64.4%) | 32.5 (45.7%) | **51.9** (87.4%) | 41.5 | 1.64x |
| 8 | 17.8 (48.3%) | 13.2 (32.5%) | 24.9 (73.3%) | 17.8 | 0.71x |

`n-max 3` and `5` have the same median, but 3 has the better worst case (1.53x on prose
vs 1.28x) while 5 is better on code and list. **3 is the suggested default.**

`n-max 8` falls below baseline: acceptance drops *and* `n_rs_seq` grows with `n-max`, so
the rollback-slot writes in `build_conv_state_at` cost `n_rs_seq + 1` copies per ubatch.
That cost is inherent to the existing `[TAG_RECURRENT_ROLLBACK_SPLITS]` design, not new
here, but it bounds how far `n-max` is worth pushing on this architecture.

Within-config spread was under +/-0.5 t/s and acceptance was identical across repeats.

## Notes / limitations

- The draft file is ~4.1 GB: block 48 is a full block including all 512 experts.
- `n_rs_seq` tracks `--spec-draft-n-max`, so the RS buffer grows with it
  (450 MiB at n-max 3 vs ~112 MiB with rollback disabled).
- `no_mtp` now defaults to `False`, so a normal conversion also includes the MTP block in
  the main file. It loads `TENSOR_SKIP` unless a draft is requested — file size only,
  matching the other nextn archs.
- Single MTP block only (`GGML_ASSERT(n_layer_nextn == 1)`); the checkpoint has one.
- Tested on Vulkan only.

## Overview

**Co-authors:** @jxia4intel, @sliu39

**PR 2/3** of the Intel Xe optimization series — see https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24408 (mega PR, draft) for the full feature set.

**Target platforms:** Xe-LPG Plus, Xe2, Xe3

This PR adds Intel Xe-specific flash attention optimization kernels for both ARLH iGPU (Xe1, UMA, coopmat1) and Xe2/Xe3. Dependency: builds on top of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24404 (Xe-LPG Plus coopmat1 enable). Independent of https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24407 (GEMM+CW).

### Flash Attention (Intel Xe)

- New Vulkan shaders: single-phase prefill (`flash_attn_hdim64/96/128`) and two-phase split prefill/decode variants
- Pipelines keyed by `(head_dim, gqa_ratio)` for runtime dispatch across various GQA ratios without combinatorial pipeline proliferation
- Supports non-power-of-two GQA ratios via subgroup splitting (`qk_groups`)
- Intel Xe1 (integrated GPU, UMA, cooperative matrix) and Xe2 paths with separate warptile tuning
- Two-phase decode splits softmax reduction across subgroups; shared QK state copy (`fa_copy_qstate`) between prefill phases

items.title: vulkan: add Intel Xe flash attention optimization kernels (2/3, Xe-LPG Plus/Xe2/Xe3)

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
$ llama-server --version
version: 10233 (0ab9d6fed)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```
Also reproduced on b10217 (`ddd4ec142`) and on current master at the time of writing.

### Operating systems

Linux — Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-28-generic

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (32607 MiB), driver 610.43.02, CUDA UMD 13.3, nvcc 13.3.73, built for `sm_120a`
- AMD Ryzen 7 9700X (8c/16t), 96 GB DDR5

### Models

`unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF` — reproduced on `UD-IQ1_S` (77 GiB), `UD-IQ3_XXS` (98 GiB) and `UD-Q2_K_XL` (91 GiB). arch `deepseek4`.

### Problem description

Whenever a prompt is processed in **more than one forward pass** (i.e. it does not fit
entirely inside a single batch *and* a single micro-batch), DeepSeek-V4 generates **nothing
but repeated `<` characters**. No error, no warning — prefill reports normal throughput and
only the output is garbage.

**The trigger is CUDA flash attention.** Single-variable isolation, identical model, prompt,
`-c 4096` and `-ub 512`:

| config | result | prefill |
|---|---|---|
| `--flash-attn on` | **CORRUPT** | 391.3 t/s |
| `--flash-attn off` | **CLEAN** | 272.8 t/s |
| `--flash-attn off` (repeat) | **CLEAN** | 274.4 t/s |

And a backend A/B at identical settings (`-ub 512`, same quant/prompt):

| backend | result | prefill |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA (layers on GPU) | **CORRUPT** | 439.7 t/s |
| `-ngl 0`, op-offload **on** (1800 MiB VRAM still used) | **CORRUPT** | 117.9 t/s |
| `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" -ngl 0 --no-op-offload` (18 MiB VRAM) | **CLEAN** | 19.2 t/s |

Note the middle row: with zero *layers* offloaded, op-offload still executes on the GPU
(117.9 t/s is not achievable on 8 CPU cores here) and it still corrupts. Only removing CUDA
from the process entirely gives clean output. **`-ngl 0` alone is not a CPU-only test.**

Why `-ub` appeared to matter (it is a symptom, not the cause): the prompt must fit in one
pass. Splitting is what exposes the bug.

| prompt | `-b` | `-ub` | passes | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1811 | 4096 | 4096 | 1 | CLEAN |
| 1811 | 4096 | 512 | 4 | CORRUPT |
| 14379 | 16384 | 16384 | 1 | CLEAN |
| 14379 | 16384 | 4096 | 4 | CORRUPT |
| 30255 | 8192 | 8192 | 4 batches, 1 ubatch each | CORRUPT |

The last row matters: making `-b == -ub` does **not** help, so it is not specific to
micro-batch splits *within* a batch — any additional forward pass triggers it. A very small
`-ub` (1–96) is also clean, and the largest clean `-ub` *shrinks* as the prompt grows
(≤96 at 1.8k tokens, ≤64 at 14.4k), which is consistent with "how much gets split", not with
a fixed threshold.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a deterministic ~1.8k-token prompt (no external files):

```python
lines = [f"Item {i:04d}: alpha bravo charlie delta echo foxtrot golf hotel {i*37%991}."
         for i in range(90)]
open("p.txt","w").write("\n".join(lines))
```

2. Start the server — note **f16 KV** (no `--cache-type-k/v`), so this is not #25382:

```bash
export GGML_CUDA_PDL=0
llama-server -hf unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF:UD-Q2_K_XL \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -c 4096 -np 1 \
  -fa on -fitt 768 -b 4096 -ub 512 -t 8
```

3. Send it to the raw completion endpoint (no chat template involved):

```bash
python3 -c "
import json,urllib.request
p=open('p.txt').read()
b=json.dumps({'prompt':p,'n_predict':40,'temperature':0.0,'cache_prompt':False}).encode()
r=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(
  'http://127.0.0.1:8080/completion',b,{'Content-Type':'application/json'})))
print(repr(r['content']))"
```

**Actual:** `'<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<'`
**Expected:** normal text. Re-run with `-ub 4096` (single pass) or `-fa off` and it is correct.

`-fa off` is not a usable workaround at real context sizes: the non-FA path materialises an
explicit `[n_tokens × n_kv]` score matrix per head (64 heads), so it loads at `-c 131072` and
then OOMs on the first long prompt (I measured a 234712 MiB allocation attempt at `-c 131072`).

### Ruled out

Each tested individually and **verified to have taken effect**; none change the outcome:

- **Quantized KV cache** (#25382 / #26423) — reproduces with **f16** KV, no `--cache-type-k/v`.
- **Chat template** — reproduces on raw `/completion`. (Via `/v1/chat/completions` the `</think>` prefix is emitted correctly *before* the run of `<`.)
- **Prompt caching / context checkpoints** — `-ctxcp 0` still corrupts, and the repro uses `cache_prompt:false`.
- **CUDA graphs** — `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` still corrupts. `LLAMA_GRAPH_REUSE_DISABLE=1` still corrupts.
- **Fusion** — `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1` still corrupts.
- **PDL** — corrupts with `GGML_CUDA_PDL=0` and with PDL enabled.
- **Op offload** — `GGML_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH=999999` still corrupts (prefill drops 439→42 t/s, so it took effect).
- **Matmul backend** — `GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ=1` and `GGML_CUDA_FORCE_CUBLAS=1` both still corrupt.
- **Lightning-indexer kernel choice** — patched the dispatch to force the generic vector kernel instead of WMMA (prefill 439→350 t/s, so active): still corrupts.
- **DS4 custom ops** — patched `supports_op` to reject `LIGHTNING_INDEXER` and `DSV4_HC_PRE/POST/COMB`; llama.cpp logs `resolve_fused_ops: ... set to disabled` and runs generic decompositions: still corrupts.
- **`GGML_SCHED_MAX_SPLIT_INPUTS`** 30 → 128 (source edit): no change.
- **Host buffers** — `--no-host` still corrupts (prefill 645→38 t/s).
- **`--swa-full`**, **`-nkvo`**, **`-kvu`**, **`LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE=1`**: all still corrupt.
- **Threads** `-t 8`/`-t 12`, with and without `-tb`; **sampling** `temperature` 0.0 and 1.0.
- **Toolkit/driver** are current and self-consistent; build targets the correct arch.

- `test-backend-ops test -b CUDA0 -o DSV4_HC_PRE,DSV4_HC_POST,DSV4_HC_COMB,LIGHTNING_INDEXER,SET_ROWS` → **267/267 pass**.

items.title: Eval bug: DeepSeek-V4 emits only repeated `<` whenever a prompt spans more than one forward pass — CUDA flash attention (clean on CPU, clean with -fa off)

items.body:
### What happens

With `--slot-save-path`, `POST /slots/{id}?action=save` and `?action=restore` both report
success on a hybrid/recurrent model, but the restored sequence gives **no prefix reuse** —
the next request re-prefills every token. The server even logs a perfect prefix match
immediately before recomputing everything:

```
slot get_availabl: id 0 | task -1 | selected slot by LCP similarity, f_sim_best = 1.000 (> 0.100 thold), f_keep = 0.999
slot print_timing: id 0 | task 15 | prompt eval time = 18801.28 ms / 5892 tokens
```

Measured on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (hybrid attention + SSM), 5,892-token prompt:

| | prompt eval | wall |
|---|---|---|
| cold | 5,892 tok | 19,057 ms |
| after `action=restore` | 5,892 tok | 19,238 ms |
| in-memory warm slot (no restore) | 4 tok | 496 ms |

So restore costs the full recompute while the in-memory path reuses fine. It is silent —
save/restore return normal success JSON and nothing is logged at default verbosity.

### Why

`llama_state_seq_save_file` serialises the sequence's KV/recurrent state, and that part
works — the file round-trips and `n_restored` matches. But for hybrid/recurrent memory the
server cannot truncate KV, so reusing a prefix requires a **context checkpoint** from
`slot.prompt.checkpoints`. That path is in `server-context.cpp`:

```
// forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data
// (likely due to SWA or hybrid/recurrent memory, see #13194)
```

`slot.prompt.checkpoints` is in-RAM only and is not part of the state file. Worse, the
restore handler calls `slot->prompt.clear()`, which empties the list. So after any restore
there are no checkpoints, `do_reset` fires, and everything is recomputed. The message is
`SLT_TRC`, so it does not appear at ordinary log levels — which is why this fails quietly.

This affects every hybrid/recurrent architecture, not one model.

### Fix that worked

Persisting the checkpoints alongside the state file and reloading them on restore:

```
cold                     5,892 tok   19,057 ms
after restore (patched)      4 tok      508 ms      (restore itself: 153 ms)
```

I did this as a `<filepath>.ckpt` sidecar written/read by the SLOT_SAVE / SLOT_RESTORE
handlers, so llama.cpp's own state format is untouched, and a missing or corrupt sidecar
degrades to exactly the current behaviour. Patch attached in a comment below.

I'm not attached to the sidecar approach — embedding the checkpoints in the state file with
a version bump may well be preferable. Happy to rework it if you'd rather have that; mainly
I wanted the failure mode documented, since it currently looks like success.

### Caveats on my patch

- Tested on one model and one configuration (`-np 1`, `-c 131072`, `-ctxcp 8 -cms 2048`).
- No regression test against a non-hybrid model. It should be inert there (an empty
  checkpoint list writes only a 12-byte header) but I have not verified that.
- Ad-hoc binary format, no unit tests.
- Requires `-ctxcp` to be set, or there are no checkpoints to save in the first place.

### Environment

- Vulkan backend, RADV, Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151), Fedora 44
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS, via the branch in #27742
- `llama-server -c 131072 -np 1 -cram 0 -ctxcp 8 -cms 2048 --slot-save-path ...`
items.title: server: slot restore gives no prefix reuse on hybrid/recurrent models (context checkpoints are not persisted)

items.body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 10068 (571d0d540)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64
```

Verified still present on `master` (`178a6c44`): `tools/server/server-context.cpp`
has no commits between `571d0d540` and `178a6c44`.

### Operating systems

Mac (macOS 26.3, Apple M5 Pro, Metal)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```sh
llama-server -m Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4_MOE.gguf \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 -c 0 -ngl 99 --jinja \
  --slot-save-path ./kv
```

### Problem description

`POST /slots/{id}?action=restore` reports complete success — `n_restored` equals
the full token count and the slot subsequently reports those tokens in
`/slots` — but the restored state is **never reused**. The next request with an
identical prefix reprocesses every token: `cache_n = 0`.

The endpoint therefore appears to work while delivering none of its benefit, and
says nothing about it at default verbosity.

On a hybrid/recurrent model this is not a partial regression, it is total: the
restore is worth exactly zero. Measured here on a 14,906-token prefix — restore
completes in 0.12s versus 75.9s to recompute, and then all 14,914 tokens are
recomputed anyway.

This is a **different bug** from the known in-memory checkpoint issues; see
"Relationship to existing issues" below. In-memory reuse on this setup is
healthy (97.9% hit rate) — only the on-disk path is broken.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Requires: a hybrid/recurrent model (e.g. Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6, DeltaNet, Mamba)
# and llama-server started with --slot-save-path
H='Content-Type: application/json'
U=http://127.0.0.1:8080

# a prompt long enough to be worth caching
P=$(python3 -c "print('### POLICY\n' + '\n'.join(f'Rule {i}: verify precondition {(i*7)%89} then record outcome {(i*13)%83}.' for i in range(300)))")

req() { jq -n --arg p "$1" '{prompt:$p, n_predict:1, cache_prompt:true}'; }

# 1. cold — populates a slot
curl -s $U/completion -H "$H" -d "$(req "$P

Q: a?
A:")" | jq -c '.timings | {cache_n, prompt_n}'
#    → {"cache_n":0,"prompt_n":5529}

# 2. find the slot that actually holds it, and save
ID=$(curl -s $U/slots | jq -r 'map(select(.n_prompt_tokens > 0))[0].id')
curl -s -X POST "$U/slots/$ID?action=save" -H "$H" -d '{"filename":"t.bin"}' | jq -c '{n_saved}'
#    → {"n_saved":5529}

# 3. wipe every slot
for i in $(curl -s $U/slots | jq -r '.[].id'); do curl -s -X POST "$U/slots/$i?action=erase" >/dev/null; done

# 4. restore — reports full success
curl -s -X POST "$U/slots/$ID?action=restore" -H "$H" -d '{"filename":"t.bin"}' | jq -c '{n_restored}'
#    → {"n_restored":5529}

# 5. same prefix again, pinned to that slot
curl -s $U/completion -H "$H" -d "$(req "$P

Q: b?
A:" | jq --argjson s "$ID" '. + {id_slot:$s}')" | jq -c '.timings | {cache_n, prompt_n}'
#    → {"cache_n":0,"prompt_n":5529}   ← BUG: expected a large cache_n
```

Step 5 should reuse the prefix. It reprocesses all of it.

### What is actually happening

The prefix match itself is **correct**. `server-context.cpp:3149`

```cpp
n_past = slot.prompt.tokens.get_common_prefix(input_tokens);
```

returns the full 5,529 — restore does repopulate `slot.prompt.tokens`. The
result is then discarded a few lines later, at `server-context.cpp:3284-3318`:

```cpp
if (pos_min >= pos_min_thold) {
    const auto it = std::find_if(
        slot.prompt.checkpoints.rbegin(),
        slot.prompt.checkpoints.rend(), ...);

    bool do_reset = it == slot.prompt.checkpoints.rend();     // :3300
    ...
    if (do_reset) {
        SLT_TRC(slot, "forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data ...");
        pos_next = 0;
        n_past   = 0;                                          // :3317
    }
}
```

A hybrid/recurrent model cannot partially rewind its recurrent state, so a
context checkpoint is the only way to roll back to a prefix — a requirement
extended from SWA-only to hybrid/recurrent in #16382. After a restore,
`slot.prompt.checkpoints` is **empty**, so `do_reset` is always true.

It is empty for two compounding reasons:

1. **The save file never contained checkpoints.** `server-context.cpp:2529-2531`
   serializes only the token list and the sequence's KV cells:
   ```cpp
   const llama_tokens tokens = slot->prompt.tokens.get_text_tokens();
   const size_t nwrite = llama_state_seq_save_file(ctx_tgt, filepath.c_str(),
                                                   slot->id, tokens.data(), token_count);
   ```
2. **Restore then clears whatever was there.** `server-context.cpp:2576-2577`
   ```cpp
   slot->prompt.clear();              // clears tokens AND checkpoints
   slot->prompt.tokens.insert(tokens);
   ```

So the on-disk path can never satisfy the checkpoint requirement introduced by
#16382. `git log` shows the save/restore payload has not been touched
substantively since `1d36b3670` (2025-05-02); #16382 landed 2025-10-03.

Notably the **in-memory** prompt cache added in #16391 got this right — it
stores a whole `server_prompt`, checkpoints included
(`server-task.cpp`: `prompt = std::move(it_best->prompt);`), and even accounts
for checkpoint bytes in `server_prompt_cache_state::size()`. That is precisely
why RAM reuse works while disk reuse does not.

### Why this is invisible

The reset is logged with `SLT_TRC` → `LOG_TRC` → `LOG_LEVEL_TRACE` (= 4).
At default verbosity, and even at `-lv 3`, nothing is printed. Users see a
successful restore, a correct `n_restored`, correct `/slots` output, and silent
full reprocessing. `-lv 4` is required:

```
slot   operator(): id  3 | task 10 | forcing full prompt re-processing due to
lack of cache data (likely due to SWA or hybrid/recurrent memory, see
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/13194#issuecomment-2868343055)
```

### Control experiment

To confirm checkpoints are the load-bearing mechanism rather than something
specific to restore — with **no save/restore involved at all**, only
`--ctx-checkpoints 0`:

```

items.body:
## Overview

Updated PR from the previous closed [one](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27008).

LIGHTNING_INDEXER: Added support for F32, F16, BF16, and several quantized formats.

The Lightning Indexer has only been implemented in the CPU backend, CUDA backend but not in the Vulkan backend. This is an implementation of the Indexer for DeepSeek V4 on the Vulkan backend.

Assisted-by: OpenCode

Currently the Hyper-connection Operations for the Vulkan backend are being implemented by @kh0pper. The one missing operation in the PR was the lightning indexer.

#https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26585 — "vulkan: tiled transpose for 0<->2 permuted CONT"

The original PR which was closed:
#https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26548 — "vulkan: add DeepSeek-V4 hyper-connection fused ops (DSV4_HC_COMB/PRE/POST)".


## Additional information

- Implements GGML_OP_LIGHTNING_INDEXER for Vulkan. Previously CPU, CUDA, SYCL, Metal only.
- K types: f32, f16, bf16, q8_0, q5_1, q5_0, q4_1, q4_0, iq4_nl.
- Extracts the FA_TYPE_* values and helpers from flash_attn_base.glsl into a new shared fa_types.glsl, so the indexer reuses FA's dequant path rather than redeclaring it.
- Two SPIR-V variants selected on subgroup_arithmetic && subgroup_require_full_support, same pattern as ssm_scan.

Numbers (RTX 3090, test-backend-ops perf, K=f16)

| Shape         | µs     | GFLOPS |
|---------------|-------:|-------:|
| nh=32 kv=256  | 10.81  | 195.6  |
| nh=64 kv=256  | 19.50  | 216.8  |
| nh=32 kv=4096 | 81.55  | 414.7  |
| nh=64 kv=4096 | 159.16 | 425.0  |


Correctness evidence

- test-backend-ops: 180/180 LIGHTNING_INDEXER cases, 16931/16931 full Vulkan suite.
- GGML_VULKAN_CHECK_RESULTS against CPU on live DeepSeek-V4-Flash shapes: avg_err 3.42e-10.
